entries.english:
1347. The affix वुञ् comes in the remaining senses after a Vṛiddha word denoting a locality of the East-folk, the word having a penultimate r or ending in ī.
This debars छ ॥ Thus पाटलिपुत्रकः ॥ So also with words ending in ई ॥ As, काकन्दी - काकन्दकः, (VI. 4. 148).
Note:— Why do we say प्राचाम् 'of the East-folk'? Observe दातामित्रीयः formed by छ ॥ The त् in ईत् in the sûtra is for the sake of distinctness.
entries.note: Heading number corrected from 1847 to 1347; missing and damaged characters restored.

entries.english:
1348. The affix वुञ् comes in the remaining senses, after a Vṛiddha word denoting an inhabited kingdom, or a limit of such kingdom.
The phrases वृद्धात् and देशे are understood here, being qualified by जनपद and तदवधि ॥ This debars the affix छ ॥ Thus भादर्शकः is an example of जनपद ॥
Note:— And ‹?› and श्यामयानकः from ‹?› and श्यामायन two uninhabited countries, are illustrations of जनपदावधि ॥
The अवधि or limit of an inhabited country or जनपद must be a country and not a village. This is so, in order to prevent, by anticipation, the application of छ by IV. 2. 137 (§ 1361) to words like निगर्त which is an arid desert: as गर्त्तकः ॥ The word तदवधि means either "the boundary of that (जनपद)" or "that which itself is a boundary".
entries.note: Embedded damaged Devanagari represented by placeholder; OCR typos corrected.

entries.english:
1349. The affix वुञ् comes in the remaining senses, even after a word which is not a Vṛiddha, and which is always plural, when it denotes an inhabited country or a limit of such country, as well as after such Vṛiddha words.
The words जनपद and तदवधि are to be read into the aphorism. This debars छ and अण् ॥ Thus from अङ्ग, वङ्गाः and कलिङ्गाः which are non-Vṛiddha kingdom denoting words, always having a plural form, we have ‹?›. Similarly ‹?› and ‹?› are always non-Vṛiddha plural words, denoting boundary of kingdoms; we have from them ‹?›. The affix will apply, of course to Vṛiddha word by the last sûtra, though these be always plural in form. Thus ‹?› from ‹?› and ‹?›. So also to Vṛiddha words denoting limit of Kingdom: कालंजराः - कालंजरकः, वैकुलिकाः - वैकुलिकः ॥
Why have we used the word विषय in the sûtra? The word विषय is used in the sûtra to indicate that the word should be plural in essence, having no corresponding singular form. Therefore the rule will not apply to वर्तन्यः plural of वर्तनी ॥ The derivative from it will be वार्तनः ॥ For वर्तन्यः is an ekaśesha plural of वर्त्तनी + वर्तनी + वर्त्तनी ॥

entries.english:
1350. The affix वुञ् comes in the remaining senses after a word, whether Vṛiddha or not, denoting a locality and having as its second term the words 'kachchha', 'agni', 'vaktra' and 'garta'.
This debars छ and अण् ॥ As वारुकच्छकः, काण्डदग्धकः, सिन्धुवक्त्रकः, and बहुगर्तकः ॥ Kâśikâ reads the sûtra as गर्त &c.
The word उत्तरपद in the sûtra should be read with every one of the words कच्छ &c.

entries.english:
1351. The affix वुञ् comes, in the remaining senses, after the words dhûma &c., denoting country.
This debars छ &c. धौमकः, तैर्थकः &c.
Note:— The word ‹?› occurs in the list. It would have taken ‹?› by IV. 2. 121 as it has ‹?› as penultimate. Its mention here shows that it need not denote a locality for the application of this affix. Similarly the words विदेह and ‹?› being names of ‹?› would have taken वुञ् by IV. 2. 124, here in this list, therefore, they do not denote country. Thus वैदेहानां क्षत्रियाणां स्वम् = वैदेहकम् "the property of Videha Kshatriyas". So also ‹?›. The word ‹?› occurs in the list. It takes the affix when the derivative word means a 'ship' or a 'sailor'. Thus ‹?› and ‹?›. Otherwise not; as ‹?› "Oceanic water".
1 धूम, 2 खडण्ड (खण्डिक and खराण्ड), 3 शशादन, 4 अर्जुनाव (प्रार्जुनाव), 5 माहकस्थली, 6 थानकम्पली, 7 माहिषस्थली, 8 मानस्थली (माषस्थली), 9 भट्टस्थली, 10 मकस्थली, 11 समुद्रस्थली, 12 दाण्डायनस्थली, 13 राजस्थली, 14 विदेह, 15 राजगृह, 16 सानासाह, 17 शिष्य (शिष्य), 18 मित्रवर्ध (मित्रवर्धः मित्र, वर्ध), 19 मद्याली, 20 मद्रकुल, 21 आजीकूल (आजीकूल), 22 वाहाथ, 23 नयाहाथ, 24 सरफाय (सह्राय), 25 वर्च, 26 वर्ज्य, 27 गर्त (बर्चगर्त), 28 आनर्त, 29 माकर, 30 पाथेय, 31 घोष, 32 पल्ली (वली), 33 आराजी, 34 धातूंगजी, 35 श्रावय, 36 तीर्थ (वयाततीर्थ), 37 कुलात् सौवीरेषु, 38 समुद्रान्नावे मनुष्ये च, 39 कुत्ति, 40 अन्तरीय (अन्तरीप), 41 दीप, 42 अरुण, 43 उज्जयनी (उज्जयिनी), 44 पट्टार, 45 दक्षिणापथ, 46 साकेत, 47 घोषस्थली, 48 भक्षास्थली, 49 गर्तकूल, 50 मनवली, 51 सुरक्षी ॥

entries.english:
1352. The affix वुञ् comes after the word 'nagara' in the remaining senses, when censure or praise is implied.
The word कुत्सनं which is equivalent to निन्दनं or 'blame or censure', and प्रावीण्यं which means नैपुण्यं "dexterity" qualify the sense of the affix. Thus नागरकः 'a thief or a skilful person'. The word literally means 'a town-born, or town-bred', but by the usage of language, it always denotes a person having the vices or virtues of a town, such as a thief or an artist.
Why do we say "when censure or dexterity is implied"? Observe नागरा ब्राह्मणाः 'the Nagara Brahmanas'.

1353. The affix वुञ् comes, in the remaining senses, after the word अरण्य, in the sense of a man.
This debars the affix अण् of 1325 Vartika. Thus आरण्यकः मनुष्यः 'a forester'.
Vart:— It should be stated rather that the affix वुञ् is added to अरण्य in the sense of 'a way', 'a lesson, or doctrine (Upanishad)', 'a maxim', 'a play or game', 'a man' and 'an elephant'. Thus आरण्यकः पन्थाः, अध्यायः, न्यायः, विहारः, मनुष्यः or हस्ती ॥
entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page 756; vārtika continues on page 757.

entries.english:
Vart:— Optionally when the sense is that of cow-dung, as आरण्याः or आरण्यका गोमयाः ॥
Note:— Why do we say when having these senses? Otherwise the affix will be अण् as आरण्याः पशवः 'wild beasts'.

1354. The affix वुञ् comes optionally in the remaining senses, after the words 'Kuru', and 'Yugandhara'.
Thus कौरवकः or कौरवः, यौगन्धरकः or यौगन्धराः ॥

1355. The affix कन् comes in the remaining senses, after the words 'madra' and 'vṛji'.
This debars वुञ्, though the words denote inhabited countries. Thus मद्रकः 'born in Madra', वृजिकः ॥

1356. The affix अण् comes in the remaining senses, after a word denoting a place, and having the letter क as its penultimate.
This debars वुञ् in the case of words which denote जनपद or inhabited countries; of course the words which do not denote जनपद will have taken अण् even without this rule. Thus आर्पिकः 'born in ऋषिका'. So also माहिषिकः ॥
Note:— The affix अण् will apply even when the word ends in an i which would have otherwise taken ठञ् by IV. 2. 116 (S. 1340). Thus ऐक्ष्वाकः 'born in इक्ष्वाकु'.
The word देशे is understood in this sūtra.

1357. The affix अण् comes, in the remaining senses, after the words kachchha &c. denoting places.
The word देशे is understood here. This debars वुञ् &c. Thus काच्छः, सैन्धवः, वार्णवः &c.
Note:— The words कच्छ &c. are not invariable plural words, because by the next sūtra, it is shown that these words may signify man and then habits &c. The word विज्ञापक occurs in this list. It would have taken अण् by the last sūtra also, because it has क as its penultimate. Its mention in the list is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra by which it takes वुञ् also under certain conditions.
1 कच्छ, 2 सिन्धु, 3 वर्णु, 4 गन्धार, 5 मधुमत्, 6 कम्बोज, 7 कश्मीर, 8 साल्व, 9 कुरु, 10 षण्ड (अण्ड, षण्ड, खण्ड), 11 शीर्ष, 12 अनूप, 13 अजवाह, 14 विज्ञापक, 15 कुलूत (कूतून), 16 रङ्क ॥

1358. The affix वुञ् comes after the words kachchha &c. in the senses of 'born &c.' when the meaning is 'a man' or 'what exists in man'.
This debars अण् ॥ Thus काच्छकः 'a man born in Kutch', काच्छकमस्य हसितं जल्पितम् ॥ 'His joke or talk is of Kutch or a Kutch laughter'.
Why do we say 'when meaning a man or what exists in man?' Observe काच्छी गौः 'The cow of Kutch'.

1359. The affix वुञ् comes after the word साल्व in the senses of being born &c. when denoting a man or what exists in man, provided that it does not mean a foot-soldier.
The word साल्व which occurs in the कच्छादि class, would have taken वुञ् by the last sūtra, when the sense was that of a man or some human attribute. The present sūtra makes a restriction. Thus साल्वको मनुष्यः, साल्वकमस्य हसितं जल्पितम् ॥
Why do we say 'when not meaning a foot-soldier'? Observe साल्वः पदातिर्व्रजति 'the Sālva foot-soldier goes'.
entries.note: Heading misprinted/misread as 1369 in OCR; corrected to 1359.

entries.english:
1360. The affix वुञ् comes in the remaining senses of being born &c., after the word साल्व, when the word signifies 'a cow' or 'a barley gruel'.
This debars अण् of IV. 2. 133 (S. 1357). Thus साल्वको गौः 'the cows born in Sālva', साल्विका यवागूः 'the barley gruel of Sālva'. In other cases we have साल्वम् ॥

1361. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses after a Nominal-stem denoting a place and having the word गर्त as its second term.
This debars अण् ॥ The word देशे is to be read into the sūtra. This rule being a subsequent one debars the affixes क and कण् of sūtra IV. 2. 117 (S. 1341). Thus वृकगर्तीयम् 'born in the wolf's hole.' The word उत्तरपद is used in the sūtra, so as to prevent the application of the rule to a word which ends in गर्त but is preceded by the affix बहु, as बहुगर्तम् ॥ Here बहु is an affix (V. 3. 68, S. 2023) and not a pada.

1362. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses after the words gahā &c.
This debars अण् &c. Thus गहीयम् 'belonging to a cave', अन्तस्थीयम् &c.
Vārtika:— The words मुखतस् and पार्श्वतस् get the affix तस्, but before the affix छ the स् of तस् is elided. Thus मुखतीयम् and पार्श्वतीयम् ॥ This Vārtika also indicates that the elision of टि of the Indeclinable as ordained by the Vārtika under S. 1324 is a rule of limited scope.
Vārt:— The augment कुक् is added to जन and पर before the affix छ. As जनकीयम्, परकीयम् ॥
Vārt:— The same augment is added to the word देव also as, देवकीयम् ॥
Vārt:— The same augment is added to the word स्व as स्वकीयम् ॥
Vārt:— The affix छण् comes after the words वेणु &c. No list of such words is given. It is an आकृतिगण ॥ Thus वैणुकीयम्, वैत्रकीयम्, औत्तरपत्रकीयम्, मांस्यकीयम्, माध्यमकीयम् ॥
Note:— In the list of गहादि occurs the following 'मध्यमध्यमं चाण् चरणे'. It means 'The word मध्य becomes changed into मध्यम when the affix छ is to be added. Thus मध्यमीयाः ॥ But when the sense is that of a Veda-school or Charaṇa, the affix अण् is added instead of छ as माध्यमाः ॥ The word मध्यम here
entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page 759.

entries.english:
has the restricted sense of the middle of the earth, and not any middle generally. Thus मध्यमीया means पृथिवीमध्ये भवा ॥ So also when the affix is applied in the sense of वरण, it has the sense of निवास of sûtra IV. 2. 69 S. 1269 and not all the other senses. Thus त्रयः प्राच्याः त्रय औदीच्याः त्रयो मध्यमाः "three Charanas dwell in the East, three in the West, and three in the Middle".

1 गह, 2 अन्तस्थ, 3 समः, 4 विषम, 5 मध्य (मध्यस्य वा वरणे), 6 उत्तम, 7 ‹?›, 8 चङ्ग, 9 मगध, 10 पूर्वपक्ष, 11 अपरपक्ष, 12 अधमशाख, 13 उत्तमशाख, 14 एकशाख, 15 समानशाख, 16 समानग्राम, 17 एकग्राम, 18 एकवृक्ष, 19 एकपलाश, 20 हृदयम्, 21 ईषत् (ईषा), 22 अपरस्पन्दन (अवस्यन्दी and अवस्कन्द), 23 कामप्रस्थ, 24 खाडायन (शाण्डिकायनि, खाण्डायने and खाण्डायनी), 25 कापरण (कपिश and कामवरण), 26 नारायण, 27 सौमित्रिक, 28 शैशिर, 29 आहुत, 30 वैवशर्मि (देवशर्मन्), 31 श्रौति, 32 हंसि, 33 भामित्रि, 34 व्याड, 35 वीज (वैपजि), 36 औध्यधि, 37 आनृशंशि, 38 शांति, 39 आमिशर्मि (अमिशर्मन्), 40 मौजि, 41 वादक (आराट?), 42 वाल्मीकि, 43 सेमवृद्धि (सेमवृध्दिन्), 44 आध्यक्ष्णि, 45 भैयाहणारी, 46 ऐक, 47 बिन्दवि, 48 हन्तास, 49 इस, 50 तस्य, 51 उत्तर, 52 अनन्तर (अन्तर), 53 मुखपार्श्वतसोर्लोपः (also मुखीय and पार्श्वतीय), 54 जनपरयोः कुक् च (also जनकीय and परकीय), 55 देवस्य च, 56 शुकासिभ्यश्छः, 57 आसुरि, 58 शौधि, 59 पार्शक. It is an आकृतिगण ॥

entries.english:
1363. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses, after the words beginning with कट denoting the places of the East-folk.

The word देशे is understood here also. The word प्राक् of the sûtra qualifies देशे. This debars अञ् ॥ Thus कटनगरीयम्, कटघोषीयम्, कटपल्लवीयम् ॥

1364. The letter क is the substitute of the final of the word राजन्, when छ is added.

This sûtra only teaches the substitution of क; for राजन् would have taken छ by IV. 2. 114 S. 1337. Thus राजकीयम् ॥ The word वृद्ध does not govern this sûtra, not being appropriate.

1365. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses, after a Vriddha word denoting a place and ending with अक or इक, or having ख as its penultimate.

The word देशे must be read into the sûtra. This debars the अञ् of IV. 2. 132 S. 1356 as well as the affixes ordained by IV. 2. 117 and 123 S. 1341 and 1347.

Thus अक। — ब्राह्मणकीयम् ॥ — "One born in Brahmanaka a country where the Brahmana caste live by the profession of arms". इक। — सांकलिकीयम् ॥

Note:—The words सौसुक &c. are also governed by this rule though they end in क ॥ Thus सौसुकीयम्, मौसुकीयम्, ऐन्द्रकीयम् ॥

1366. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses after the Vriddha words, having the words kanthā, palada, nagara, grāma and hrada, as last terms.

This debars the other affixes such as अञ् and वुञ् of IV. 2. 117 S. 1341. Thus दाक्षिकन्धीयम्, दाक्षिपलदीयम्, दाक्षिनगरीयम्, दाक्षिग्रामीयम्, दाक्षिह्रदीयम् ॥

1367. The affix छ comes after the word पर्वत in the remaining senses.

This debars अण् ॥ Thus पर्वतीयो राजा "the hill-king", पर्वतीयः पुरुषः "the hill-man".

1368. The affix छ optionally comes in the remaining senses after the word पर्वत when it does not denote a man.

Thus पर्वतीयानि or पार्वतानि फलानि "hill fruits".

Why do we say अमनुष्ये "not human"? Observe पर्वतीयो मनुष्यः where there is no option allowed.

1369. The affix छ comes in the remaining senses after कृकण and पर्ण when denoting the country of Bhāradvāja.

The word देशे is understood here also. The word भारद्वाज does not here mean Gotra, but country. Thus कृकणीयम् and पर्णीयम् ॥

Why do we say "denoting country of Bharadvajas?" Observe कार्कणम्, पार्णम् &c.

1370. The affix खञ् also comes optionally in the remaining senses, after the words 'yushmad' and 'asmad'.

The regulating power of the word वृद्ध ceases. The word च indicates that the affix may be छ as well. The word "optionally" shows that the general affix अण् may also be employed. Thus there are three affixes, खञ्, छ and अण्; and hence there being no equal enumeration, the rule of mutual correspondence (I. 3. 10) does not apply.

The words युष्मद् and अस्मद् are Vriddha, as they belong to Tyadādi class (I. 1. 74 S. 1336), and would have taken छ by IV. 2. 114 S. 1337; the present sûtra enjoins three affixes for each. Thus युष्मद् + अण् = यौष्माक + अ = यौष्माकः (IV. 3. 2 S. 1371). युष्मद् + छ = युष्मद् + ईय = युष्मदीयः (VII. 1. 2). युष्मद् + खञ् = युष्माक + ईन = यौष्माकीनः (IV. 3. 2 S. 1371, VII. 1. 2, and VIII. 4. 2 S. 475 and 197). So also आस्माकः, अस्मदीयः, and आस्माकीनः ॥

1371. When this affix खञ् is added and when अण् is added, then युष्माक and अस्माक are the substitutes of युष्मद् and अस्मद् ॥

Note 1:—The pronoun तस्मिन् refers to the visible affix खञ् and not to the understood affix छ which was drawn into the last sûtra by the word च ॥

Why does the rule of mutual correspondence (I. 3. 10 S. 128) not apply here, there being two affixes, two words, and two substitutes? This, however, is not done, because the sûtra can be divided into two separate aphorisms: as (1) तस्मिन् खञि युष्मदस्मदोर्युष्माकास्माकौ भवतः (2) ततोऽणि च ॥ i.e. (1) when खञ् is added, युष्माक and अस्माक are the substitutes of युष्मद् and अस्मद् respectively. (2). So also when अण् follows.

As for illustrations, see the preceding sûtra, e.g. यौष्माकीनः, आस्माकीनः with खञ्, and यौष्माकः and आस्माकः with अण् ॥

Note:—This substitution does not take place when छ is added, as युष्मदीयः and अस्मदीयः ॥

1372. In expressing one individual, तवक and ममक are the substitutes of 'yushmad' and 'asmad' respectively, when खञ् and अण् follow.

As तावकीनः 'belonging to thee', तावकः; मामकीनः 'belonging to me' and मामकः । But when the affix is छ, the form will be त्वदीय and मदीय by the following rule.

Note:—The word एकवचने should not be construed as meaning the affix of the singular number, as the affix ङस् ॥ Because the affix of the singular is always elided (लुक्) after these words, and by rule I. 1. 63, S. 263 there will not be the application of this rule. This difficulty is, however, got over by explaining the word एकवचने as equal to एकार्थे ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari and corrected OCR misreadings.

entries.english:
1373. त्व is substituted for युष्म् and म for अस्म्, when they signify a single individual, even when an affix follows, or a word is in composition.

As त्वदीयः, मदीयः, with the affix छ (IV. 2. 114, S. 1337, I. 1. 74, S. 1336).

Similarly when a second member of the compound follows. As तव पुत्रः = त्वत्पुत्रः, मत्पुत्रः ॥ त्वद्भार्याऽस्य त्वद्भार्यः ॥

Note:—When more than one individual is signified, the substitution does not take place, as युष्मदीयं (= युष्माकमिदम्), अस्मदीयम्, युष्मत्पुत्रः (= युष्माकं पुत्रः), अस्मत्पुत्रः ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1374. The affix यत् comes after the word अर्द्ध in the remaining senses.

This debars अण् ॥ Thus अर्द्ध्यम् 'belonging to half'.
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1375. The affix यत् comes, in the remaining senses, after the word 'ardha', when preceded by 'para', 'avara', 'adhama', and 'uttama'.

Thus परार्ध्यम्, अवरार्ध्यम्, अधमार्ध्यम्, उत्तमार्ध्यम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1376. And the affix ञ् also (as well as यत्) comes in the remaining senses, after the word 'ardha', when the prior term denotes a direction.

By च, the affix यत् is also used. This debars अण् ॥ Thus पौर्वार्धम् or पौर्वार्धिकम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari and repaired broken lines.

entries.english:
1377. The affixes अञ् and ठञ् come in the remaining senses after the word 'ardha', preceded by a word denoting direction, when a particular portion of a village or an inhabited country is meant.

The phrase दिक्पूर्वपदात् is to be read into the sûtra. This debars यत् ॥ Thus इमे खल्वस्माकं ग्रामस्य जनपदस्य वा पौर्वार्धाः or पौर्वार्धिकाः "Those verily belong to the eastern half of our village or country". The word पौर्वार्धा = ग्रामस्य पूर्वस्मिन्नर्द्धे भवाः and is a Taddhitârtha compound.

Though the anuvritti of ठञ् was current in this Sûtra from the preceding, yet it is repeated here for the sake of precision; for had the sûtra been ग्रामजनपदेकदेशादञ्, then the च would have drawn in not only the affix ठञ् but the affix यत् which is not desired.
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1378. After the word मध्य there is the affix म in the remaining senses.

This debars अण् ॥ As मध्यमः "middlemost".

1379. The affix अण् comes in the remaining senses after the word 'madhya', the meaning being 'fit' or 'proper'.

The word सांप्रतिक means equity, propriety, right, fit. As नातिदीर्घं नातिह्रस्वं मध्यं काष्ठम् "the proper piece of wood—neither too long nor too short". मध्यो वैयाकरणः "the fit Grammarian, neither too refined nor too dull."
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1380. The affix यञ् comes, in the remaining senses, after the word द्वीप, which is near the sea.

Note:—The word द्वीप occurs in the list of Kachchhâdi (IV. 2. 133, S. 1357), and would have taken अण्; and by sûtra IV. 2. 134, S. 1358, it would have taken वुञ् also. The present sûtra debars both those affixes, when the word द्वीप means अनुसमुद्रम् or 'near the sea'.

Thus द्वैप्यम् or द्वैप्या, 'living on or relating to an island'. As यं द्विपाद्भवन्तोऽनुचरन्ति चक्रम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1381. The affix ठञ् comes in the remaining senses after the words denoting time.

This debars अण् ॥ The affix छ which comes after Vriddha words is prohibited by this sûtra. Thus मासिकम् 'monthly', सांवत्सरिकम् 'annual', सायंप्रातिकः "morning and evening", पौनःपुनिकः 'again and again'.

How do you explain the forms शार्बर and आश्विन in the following lines of Kâlidâsa and Bhâravi: शार्बरस्य तमसो निषिद्धये (Kâlidâsa) and आश्विनमशेषविषयम् (Bhâravi)? Or the forms समानकालीनम् and प्राक्कालीनम्? These forms are ungrammatical according to the best authorities.

Note:—The words which denote time even indirectly, also take this affix. As कादम्बपुष्पिकः पेलवः कालः ॥

The word काल governs all the subsequent sûtras up to IV. 3. 25, S. 1393 (तत्र जातः) ।
entries.note: Corrected SK serial number in heading and reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1382. The affix ठञ् comes in the remaining senses after the word शरद्, when expressing श्राद्ध ।

This debars अण् (IV. 3. 16, S. 1387). The word श्राद्धे means the 'funeral oblation', and not श्रद्धावान् पुरुषः a faithful or believing person.

Thus शारदिकं श्राद्धम् 'the autumnal Śrâddha'. When not meaning 'Śrâddha', it will be शारदम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari.

entries.english:
1383. The affix ठञ् comes optionally in the remaining senses after the word शरद् when expressing illness or heat.

Thus शारदिकः or शारदो रोगः 'the autumnal disease', शारदिकः or शारद आतपः 'the autumnal heat or sunshine.'

Why do we say "when denoting sickness or heat"? Observe, शारदं दधि 'the autumnal curd'. This ठञ् debars the ऋतु अण् (IV. 3. 16).
entries.note: Sutra line was printed at the bottom of preceding page 765; vritti fragment and English text appear on page 766.

entries.english:
1384. The affix ठञ् comes optionally in the remaining senses after the words 'niśā', and 'pradoṣa'.

This makes optional, where by sūtra IV. 3. 11 § 1381, the ठञ् would have been obligatory. Thus नैशम् or नैशिकम् 'nocturnal', प्रादोषम् or प्रादोषिकम् ॥

1385. The affix ठञ् comes optionally in the remaining senses after the word श्वस् and it takes the augment तुट् ॥

The word श्वस् takes the affix त्यप् by sūtra IV. 2. 105. § 1326. This sūtra ordains ठञ् ॥ When free from the scope of these rules, it takes tyu and tyul affixes also by IV. 3. 23 § 1391. Thus श्वस् + तुट् + ठञ् now applies the following sūtra:—

1386. Before a Taddhita-affix with an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क् the Vṛiddhi is not substituted for the first vowel after य् or व्, but ऐ and औ are respectively placed before these semivowels in द्वार &c.

The following is a list of Dvārādi words:—

1. द्वार 2. स्वर, 3. स्वाध्याय 4. व्यल्कश 5. स्वस्ति 6. स्वर् (स्वर), 7. स्फ्यकृत, 8. स्वादुमृदु 9. श्वस् 10. श्वन् 11. स्व ॥

Thus श्वस् + तुट् + ठञ् -> श्वस् + त् + इक (VII. 3. 3 § 1098) = शौवस्तिकम् (ephemeral).

Note:—As द्वारे नियुक्तः = दौवारिकः, दौवारपालम् from द्वारपाल । The Tyadādi rule applies here, सौवरः from स्वर, (स्वरमधिकृत्य कृतो ग्रन्थः) ॥ So also सौवरोऽध्यायः, सौवर्यः समस्य ॥ वैयल्कशः from व्यल्कश (व्यल्को भगः) । सौवस्तिकम् from स्वस्ति, (स्वस्तीति प्राह) । सौवः from स्वर् (स्वर्भवः) ॥

Some read the word स्वाध्याय also in this list, but it is unnecessary, as it would be governed by the last rule, because it is a compound of सु + अध्याय (स्वाध्यायः), or it may be a compound of स्व + अध्याय, then also it is unnecessary, as स्व is separately mentioned in this list, and therefore when स्व begins a word it would get this peculiar substitution then also. Similarly स्फैयकृत from स्फ्यकृत, स्वायदुमृदवः from स्वादुमृदु, शौवनम् from श्वन्, the prakṛiti-bhāva is by (VI. 4. 167 § 1155) while शौवम् from श्वन् where there is no prakṛitibhāva (by अण् IV. 2. 104); शौवाशुकी (श्वाशुकायां भवः). Similarly सौवम् from स्व (= स्वस्येदम्), सौवग्रामिक from स्वग्राम with the affix ठञ् (अध्यात्मिकादिभ्यष्ठञ्). This sūtra is made because the य् and व् here are not final of a gati word, as they were in the preceding sūtra.

1387. The affix अण् comes in the remaining senses, after the words 'sandhi-velā' &c., and the words expressing 'season' and 'asterism'.

The word कालात् is to be read into the sūtra. All the words must be expressive of time. This debars ठञ् ॥ The repetition of अण् debars छ also in the case of those words which are Vṛiddha in this list (IV. 2. 114 § 1337). Thus (1) सान्धिवेलम्, सान्ध्यम्, (2) ग्रैष्मम्, शैशिरम्, (3) तैषम्, पौषम् are examples of sandhivelā, season and asterisms respectively:—

1. संधिवेला 2. संध्या 3. अमावास्या 4. त्रयोदशी 5. चतुर्दशी 6. पौर्णमासी, 7. प्रतिपद् ॥

Vārt:—The affix अण् is added to संवत्सर when denoting 'fruit' and 'festival', as सांवत्सरं फलम् or पर्व ॥ Otherwise सांवत्सरिकम् ॥
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1987 in source, corrected to 1387.

entries.english:
1388. The affix एण्य comes in the remaining senses after the word प्रावृष् ॥

Note:—This debars the अण् of the last sūtra, though 'prāvṛiṣ' is a season-denoting word. Thus प्रावृषेण्यो बलाहकः "the cloud belonging to the rainy season".

1389. The affix ठक् comes in the remaining senses after the word वर्षा ॥

This debars अण् of IV. 3. 16 § 1387. Thus वार्षिकमनुलेपनम् । The ठक् has the force of साधु &c. of IV. 3. 43 § 1418 here.

1390. The affix अण् comes always after the word 'hemanta,' and (before this affix) the letter त of 'hemanta' is elided.

Thus हैमनम् or हैमन्तम् ॥

Note:—The word सर्वत्र is used to show that the sūtra applies in the Chhandas as well as in the classical literature.

The word हेमन्त will take अण् by sūtra IV. 3. 16 § 1387 as हैमन्ती पङ्क्तिः, but there is no elision of त there. Thus there are three forms हैमन्तम् (IV. 3. 16 § 1387), हैमन्तिकम् (IV. 3. 21 § 1452) and हैमनम् ॥

1391. After the words सायं 'at eve', चिरं 'for a long time', प्राह्णे 'in the fore-noon', प्रगे 'at dawn', and after Indeclinables expressing time, there are the affixes ट्यु and ट्युल and their augment is तुट् ॥

The word कालात् is understood here also. Thus सायं = सायं + अन = सायं + तुट् + अन = सायन्तनम् 'belonging to the evening', चिरन्तनम् 'lasting', प्राह्णेतनम् 'what is of the forenoon', प्रगेतनम् "what is of the early morn".

The replacement of यु by अन under VII. 1. 1 § 1247 takes place prior to the addition of the augment तुट् to the affix, because we find it so in the forms like अद्यतन &c. used by Pāṇini himself in III. 2. 111 § 2205 &c. Had it been added first, then the affix would have become तुयु, and the form would have been अद्यतुयु like इक्षुप्रचुः, for there is no rule which would have changed स्यु into तन ॥ प्राह्णे and प्रगे always end in ए.

As regards Indeclinables, the examples are दोषातनम् 'belonging to the night', दिवातनम् 'belonging to the day'.

Vārt:—The affix त्न comes after the words चिर, परुत् (meaning in the past year) and परारि (meaning in the year before the last). As चिरत्नम्, परुत्नम्, and परारित्नम् ॥

Vart:—The affix डिमच् comes after अग्र, आदि and पश्चात्, as अग्रिमम्, आदिमम् and पश्चिमम् ॥
Vart:—So also after अन्त, as, अन्तिमम् ॥
Note:—The difference between tyu and tyul is in accent. Thus सायन्तन and सायन्तन, चिरन्तन and चिरन्तन, प्राह्णेतन and प्राह्णेतन, प्रगेतन, प्रगेतन, दिवातन and दिवातन, दोषातन and दोषातन. See VI. 1. 1938, S. 676.
entries.note: Continuation tail from previous page without heading; Devanagari restored from clear context.

entries.english:
1392. Optionally after the words पूर्वाह्न and अपराह्न, there are the affixes ट्यु and ट्युल् and their augment in तु ॥
In the alternative ठञ् of IV. 3. 11 S. 1381 also occurs. As पूर्वाह्णेतनम्, अपराह्णेतनम् with tyu, or पौर्वाह्निकम्, आपराह्निकम् with thañ. With tyul we have पूर्वाह्णेतन and अपराह्णेतन. The sign of the locative is not elided by rule VI. 3. 17 S. 975. When the compound is such as not retaining the case-affix, because not in the locative case, as when it is analysed by saying पूर्वाह्णः सोढोऽस्य (IV. 3. 52 S. 1427) then we have, पूर्वाह्णतनम्, अपराह्णतनम्, पौर्वाह्णिकम्, आपराह्णिकम् ॥

1393. The affixes ordained above or hereafter, come after a word in the 7th case in construction, in the sense of 'born or grown or originated there or then'.
The affixes अण् &c. घ &c. have been taught, but no particular sense was assigned to them. See IV. 2. 92. S. 1312. This sutra gives one of the senses, and also declares the particular case in which the stem must be, to which the affix is to be added. Thus स्रुघ्ने जातः = स्रुघ्न + अण् = स्रौघ्नः 'born in Srughna', औत्सः 'born in Utsa', राष्ट्रिय (IV. 2. 93 S. 1313), अवारपारीण &c.

1394. After the word प्रावृष् being in the 7th case-affix, there is the affix टप् in the sense of produced therein.
This debars एण्य of sutra IV. 3. 17 S. 1388. The प् of टप् is for the sake of accent. प्रावृषि जातः प्रावृषिकः 'produced in the rainy season'.

1395. The affix वुञ् comes after the word शरद् in the 7th case-affix, in the sense of 'born therein,' the whole word being a name.
This debars अण् of IV. 3. 16 S. 1387. Thus शारदकाः 'the grass called Saradaka,' 'the pulse called Saradaka.'
Note:—According to some, the word संज्ञायां governs all the succeeding sutras up to IV. 3. 38, S. 1413.

1396. Upto VII. 3. 31 S. 1789 inclusive, the substitution of Vriddhi will take place, for the first vowel of the second member in a compound.
This is an adhikâra sutra, and exerts governing influence upto VII. 3. 32 S. 2574 exclusive. The phrase "of the second member of the compound" should be supplied in all those sutras, to complete the sense. Thus in VII. 3. 11 S. 1397 the word उत्तरपदस्य should be supplied. As पूर्ववार्षिकम्, परवार्षिकम्, पूर्वहैमनम्, अपरहैमनम् ॥
Note:—In those sutras, where the word denoting the first member is not exhibited in the Ablative case, as in VII. 3. 18, 19, 20, 21, the present sutra is absolutely necessary for causing the vriddhi of the second member. But in those sutras where the first member is exhibited in the ablative case, as in VII. 3. 11 S. 1397 (अवयवात्), then this sutra is only explanatory (and not absolutely necessary), and serves also the purpose of placing such vriddhis under the category of 'uttarapada-vriddhi.' This peculiar vriddhi is liable to certain rules of accent, as in VI. 2. 105. Hence the importance of the present aphorism in those sutras also, where the word is exhibited in the fifth case.

1397. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowel of a word denoting season, when it is preceded by a word denoting a part.
As पूर्ववार्षिक from पूर्व + वर्षा + ठञ् meaning वर्षायाम् पूर्व ॥ अपरहैमनः meaning हेमन्तस्यापरः ॥
Note:—The composition with पूर्व and अपर &c. takes place by II. 2. 1 S. 712 and then by IV. 3. 18 S. 1389 there is ठञ् after वर्षा, and अण् after हेमन्त with the elision of तृ by IV. 3. 22 S. 1390. The Tadanta-vidhi, as a general rule, does not apply to compounds, so that a rule made applicable to a particular word, will not apply to a compound which ends with that word; but tadanta-vidhi applies to a word denoting season when it takes an affix causing Vriddhi, and is preceded by a word denoting a portion. We draw this rule from the present sûtra, for वर्षा being formed from वर्षा by a vriddhi-causing affix (IV. 3. 22 S. 1390), the affix will be applied to वर्षा even when it is the second member of a compound, the first member of which denotes a part, (ऋतौ वृद्धिमद्विधाववयवाच्चाणिति I. 1. 72 Vârt. Mahâbhâshya).
Why do we say 'denoting a portion'? Observe पूर्ववर्षासु भवः पौर्ववार्षिकः with ठञ् (IV. 3. 11 S. 1389) and no vriddhi of the of वर्षा because of the maxim "The Tadanta-vidhi applies, when an affix causing Vriddhi is ordained after a word denoting season, provided that, the word denoting season is preceded in composition by a word denoting a part, and not otherwise." Therefore the vriddhi does not take place here, because the preceding word in composition is not a word which denotes a part of varshâ, but is in apposition with it. The tadanta-vidhi applies only when the first member denotes a portion.

1398. After सु, सर्व and अर्ध, the first vowel of the name of a country gets the Vriddhi, when a Taddhita affix with an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क् follows.
As सुपाञ्चालकः, सर्वपाञ्चालकः and अर्धपाञ्चालकः, formed with वुञ् (IV. 2. 124, S. 1348) read with IV. 2. 125 S. 1349 though the word is not a Vriddha. This sutra also gives rise to the following rule सुसर्वार्धाद्दिग्वाचकेभ्यश्च जनपदस्य "The tadantavidhi applies to words denoting country, when the first member is सु, सर्व or अर्ध or a direction-denoting word."
Note:—As shown in the above examples, and for direction-denoting words see the following sutra (I. 1. 72 Vârt. Mahâbhâshya).
1399. After a word denoting direction, the first vowel of the name of a country, with the exception of मद्र,

gets Vriddhi before a Taddhita-affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण्, or क ॥

As ‹?›, (IV. 2. 125, 107) The Tadanta-vidhi applies here, as shown in the preceding sûtra. Why do we say 'denoting direction'? Observe पूर्व पञ्चालानां = पूर्वपञ्चाल, तत्र भवः = पौर्वपञ्चालकः ॥ Why do we say with the exception of मद्र? Observe पौर्वमद्रः with अञ् (IV. 2. 108 S. 1329). The separation of this sûtra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sûtra, in which the anuvritti of "direction" only runs.

1400. After a word denoting direction, the first vowel of the name of a town or city in the land of the eastern people, gets the Vriddhi before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क ॥

Thus पूर्वैषुकामशमः “born in Purveshukamasami”. So also परैषुकामशमः, पूर्वकामशाम, अपरकामशाम (IV. 2. 107 S. 1328). These are town names. पूर्वपाटलिपुत्रकः, अपरपाटलिपुत्रकः, पूर्वकान्यकुब्जः, अपरकान्यकुब्जः ॥ These are city names.

Note:—The word प्राचां in this sûtra, as well as in VII. 3. 24 S. 1431 does not here mean 'the eastern grammarians' but 'the eastern countries', because of the context. पूर्वेषुकामशमः is thus formed. पूर्वा च असौ इषुकामशमी = पूर्वेषुकामशमी ॥ The compounding takes place by II. 1. 50 S. 727. Then the affix अञ् is added to it, in the sense of तत्र भवः by IV. 2. 107 S. 1328. In पूर्वपाटलिपुत्रक the affix वुञ् is added by IV. 2. 123 S. 1347. Though Pâtaliputra is the name of one city, Pûrva-pâtaliputra means the Eastern portion of the city Pâtaliputra.

1401. The affix वुन् comes in the sense of 'born therein' after the words पूर्वाह्ण, अपराह्ण, आर्द्रा, मूला, प्रदोष, and अवस्कर, the whole being a Name.

Thus पूर्वाह्णकः । अपराह्णकः ॥ This debars IV. 3. 24 S. 1392. So also आर्द्रकः । मूलकः ॥ This debars अण् of IV. 3. 16, S. 1387. प्रदोषकः ॥ This debars उञ् of IV. 3. 14. S. 1384. अवस्करकः ॥ This debars the general अण् affix.

When it is not a Name, the other affixes are employed.

1402. The affix वुन् comes after the word पथ, in the sense of 'produced therein', and thereby in the room of पथ, the substitute is पन्थ ॥

Thus पथि जातः पन्थकः 'produced in the way.'

This debars the अण् ॥

1403. The affix वुन् comes optionally after the word amâvâsyâ, in the sense of 'born therein'.

This debars अण् of IV. 3. 16. S. 1387.

Thus आमावास्यकः or आमावास्यः ॥

Note:—This affix वुन् is applied to the word अमावस्य also on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वात् "That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means in consequence of this change, something else than what it was before the change had taken place". Thus अमावास्यकः or आमावास्यः ॥
entries.note: English heading misprinted as 1408 instead of 1403.

entries.english:
1404. And the affix क also is added to the word amâvâsyâ, in the sense of 'born therein'.

This adds a third affix to the वुन् and अण् already given. Thus अमावास्य, अमावास्यक, आमावास्यः ॥ So also after the word अमावस्य as अमावास्य, अमावास्यक and आमावास्य ॥

1405. After the words 'sindhu' and 'apakara', there is the affix कन् in the sense of 'born therein'.

The word सिन्धु occurs in the Kachchhadi class and takes अण् and वुञ् (IV. 2. 133 S. 1357), and अपकर would have also taken अण् under the general rule. This sûtra debars these affixes. Thus सिन्धुकः, अपकरकः ॥

1406. And the affixes अण् and त्रल् come respectively after the words 'sindhu' and 'apakara', in the sense of 'produced therein'.

Thus सैन्धवः and अपकरत्रः ॥

1407. The affix denoting 'born therein', is elided by luk, after the words 'sravishthâ', 'phalgunî', 'anurâdhâ', 'svâti', 'tishya', 'punarvasu', 'hasta', 'vis'âkhâ', 'âshâdhâ', and 'bahulâ', all denoting asterisms.

Note:—The feminine affixes are also elided after these words by I. 2. 49 S. 1408. Thus श्रविष्ठासु जातः = श्रविष्ठः 'produced under Sravishthâ'. So also फल्गुनः, अनुराधः, स्वातिः, तिष्यः, पुनर्वसुः, हस्तः, विशाखः, आषाढः, बहुलः ॥ The 'Bahulâ' is another name of the asterism कृत्तिका ॥ It is exhibited in the sûtra as bahula with a short अ, as it is a Samâhâra Dvandva shortening.

1408. When a Taddhita affix is elided by the word luk, there takes place the elision by luk of the feminine affix also, of the original stem to which the Taddhita affix was added.

The word लुक् defined in I. 1. 61 S. 260, is twice used in this sûtra. Where a Taddhita affix is elided by the word लुक्, there the feminine suffix of the prâtipadika is also dropped, or becomes luk. The word upasarjana used in explaining this sûtra by the author should be taken in its popular sense of non-principal, secondary; and not the technical upasarjana of grammar.

Thus श्रविष्ठा + (अण् = लुक्) = श्रविष्ठः ॥ The Taddhita suffix being luked; the original feminine termination also becomes luk. Therefore the derivative of श्रविष्ठा (is not a longer word, as might have been expected) but actually a shorter word, namely श्रविष्ठः; similarly from फल्गुनी we have फल्गुनः &c.

Vart:—So also the affix is elided after the asterisms चित्रा, रेवती and रोहिणी when the word is feminine.

Thus चित्रायां जाता a woman produced under Chitrâ will be called चित्रा ॥

So also रेवती, रोहिणी ॥

The feminine

affix which had been elided after the two words Revati and Rohini, by the present sutra I. 2. 49 S. 1408 is reordained by IV. 1. 41, S. 498 because these words belong to the Pippalyadi subdivision of the ‹?› class, The Pippalyadi being an akritigana contains these words also.
Vart:—The affixes ‹?› and ‹?› come respectively after ‹?› and ‹?› in forming the Feminine derivatives, As फल्गुनी ( IV. 1. 15 S. 470 ) and ‹?› ॥ The difference is in accent and meaning.
Vart:—The affix ‹?› also comes after 'Sravishtha and Ashadha' even when females are not denoted. As श्राविष्ठीय and आषाढीयः ॥
entries.note: Tail continuation from page 774; embedded Devanagari fragments damaged in source.

entries.english:
1409. In प्रोष्ठपद and its synonyms, the first vowel of the second member gets the Vriddhi, before a Taddhita affix meaning 'born in that time', and having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क् ॥
The word ज means 'born', the affixes denoting 'born under that asterism' are meant here. प्रोष्ठपदा is the name of an asterism, the day when the moon is there is also called ‹?› ( the affix अण् of IV. 2. 3. S. 1204 is elided by IV. 2. 4 S. 1205 ). प्रोष्ठपदासु जातः = प्रोष्ठपादो माणवकः ( with अण् IV. 3. 16 S. 1387). Why do we say 'born in that time'? Observe ‹?› ( = प्रोष्ठपदासु भवः ) धरणीमभिवर्षति ॥ The plural number प्रोष्ठपदानाम् indicates that the synonyms of प्रोष्ठपद such as भाद्रपद are also to be included. As भाद्रपदः ॥

1410. There is luk-elision of the affix denoting “born therein” after a word ending in 'sthana', and after the words 'gosâla' and 'kharasâla'.
Thus गोस्थाने जातः = गोस्थानः, अश्वस्थानः, गोशालः, खरशालः ॥ The word gośâla and kharaśâla in the sûtra end in a short a because they are Neuter under II. 4. 25 S. 828.

1411. There is optionally luk-elision of the affix denoting 'born therein' after the words 'vatsasâla', 'abhijit', 'aśvayuk', and 'satabhik'.
As वत्सशाले जातः = वत्सशालः or वात्सशालः, अभिजित् or आभिजितः, अश्वयुक् or आश्वयुजः, शतभिषक् or शातभिषज् ॥ The two words गोशाल and वत्सशाला are both to be taken. These are all diversities of ‹?› used in the next sûtra.
Vârt:—The affix ‹?›, provided that, it be that in the sense of 'born', is optionally treated as ‹?› which being debarred by IV. 3. 11. S. 1381 is reordained by IV. 3. 16. S. 1387. The affix ‹?› governs all sutras up to IV. 4. 2. S. 1550 by force of IV. 1. 83 S. 1073 but it is debarred by ‹?› of IV. 3. 11 S. 1381 and is re-ordained in IV. 3. 16 S. 1387. Thus शतभिषजि जातः = शातभिषः or शातभिषजः, or शतभिषक् ॥
entries.note: Devanagari sutra and vritti printed on page 775; bold English heading begins on page 776.

entries.english:
1412. There is diversely luk-elision of the affix denoting 'born therein', after the name of an asterism.
Thus रोहिणः or रौहिणः (IV. 3. 16. S. 1387 'person born when the moon is in the asterism of Rohini Aldebaran').

1413. An affix (one of those already taught) comes after a word in the seventh case-affix in construction, in the sense of 'done there', 'obtained there', 'bought there', and 'dexterous therein'.
Thus स्रौघ्नः may mean "done in, or bought in, or obtained in, or skilfull in Srughna".

1414. After a word being in construction in the 7th case, an affix (one of those ordained already) comes in the sense of 'generally found therein'.
The word प्रायः means something less than all i. e. abundant. Thus स्रौघ्नः 'what is abundant or mostly to be found in Srughna', = स्रुघ्ने प्रायेण बाहुल्येन भवति ॥
Note:—This sutra according to Patanjali, is superfluous, as it is covered by the more comprehensive sutra (IV. 3. 53 S. 1428). If प्रायः be explained as ‹?› i.e. what sometimes is to be found and sometimes not, still it will make little difference.
entries.note: Serial number corrected from misread 2414 to 1414; entry spans across pages 776 and 777.

entries.english:
1415. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'generally found therein', after the words 'upajânu', 'upakarṇa', and 'upanîvi', being in the 7th case in construction.
This debars अण् &c. Thus औपजानुकः, औपकण्ठकः, औपनीविकः ॥
Note:—All these three words of the sûtra are Indeclinables, because they are Avyayîbhâva compounds. In the sûtra, they have formed a samâhâra Dvandva and masculine.

1416. After a nominal-stem or a word ending in the feminine affix and being in the 7th case in construction, an affix comes in the sense of 'adapted therein’.
Note:—Except the word 'adapted' which is the meaning of the word संभूत, all the other words of the sutra have been supplied from the previous aphorisms. The word does not mean in this sûtra 'origin' or 'existence' for the words भव and जात already express that notion. It here means 'suitableness', 'adequacy' = अवक्लप्तिः and प्रमाणातिरेकः ॥
Thus स्रौघ्नः 'what is suited to the country of Srughna'.
The word ‹?› is understood here also.

1417. The affix ढञ् comes after the word कोश in the sense of 'adapted to that'.
This debars अण् ॥
Thus कोशे संभूतं = कौशेयं वस्त्रम् silken clothes.
Note:—The word कोश means 'cocoon', कौशेय may literally therefore mean 'anything suited to the cocoon', and may apply to the caterpillar as well as to the silk made out of cocoon. The word कौशेय is however रूढि and means silken. Nor does it mean 'suited to the sheath', as a sword, though kośa means 'sheath' also. This sutra would have been more properly placed after IV. 3. 134. S. 1614 under the heading of विकार rather than of संभूत ॥
In fact, after the sûtra एण्या-ढञ् (IV. 3. 159, 1587) the addition of कोशाञ् would have been more appropriate शाक्षायः ॥

1418. An affix comes after a word denoting time, being in the 7th case in construction, in the sense of 'being good therein', 'flowering therein' or 'ripening therein'.

Thus हेमन्ते साधुः = हेमन्तः 'what is good or pleasant in autumn' as हेमन्तः प्राकारः । So also वसन्ते पुष्प्यन्ति = वासन्त्याः कुन्दलताः 'vernal creepers i.e. which flower in spring'. So also शरदि पच्यन्ते = शारदाः शालयः 'the grains that ripen in autumn'.

Note:— The sûtra touches the base and the sense of the affix. It does not directly teach the affix. The above illustrations are examples of the affix अण् or ठञ्. The word pushpyat in the sûtra is the Present Participle or शतृ of the Dhâtu पुष्प ॥

1419. An affix comes after a word denoting time, being in the 7th case in construction, meaning 'sown therein.'

Thus हेमन्ते उप्यन्ते = हेमन्ता यवाः 'the barley sown in autumn.' ग्रैष्मा व्रीहयः ।

Note:— The separation of this sûtra from the last, is for the sake of the subsequent sûtra in which the anuvritti of उप्त only goes, which could not have been the case had this word been included in the last sûtra.
entries.note: Corrected OCR misread serial number from १४१६ to 1419 based on strict sequence.

entries.english:
1420. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'sown' after the word आश्वयुजी ॥

This debars ठञ् ॥ Thus आश्वयुज्यामुप्ताः = आश्वयुजका माषाः 'the pulse sown in Âśvayujî'. Âśvayujî is the name of the full moon in the Asterism of Aśvayuj. Aśvayuj and Aśvinî are the same. Some texts read अश्विनी instead of अश्वयुज् ॥

1421. The affix वुञ् comes optionally after the words 'grîshma' and 'vasanta', in the sense of 'sown therein'.

This debars अण् (IV. 3. 16 S. 1387). Thus ग्रैष्मम् or ग्रैष्मकम् शस्यम् 'the crop sown in summer', वासन्तम् or वासन्तकम् ॥

1422. After a nominal stem being in the 7th case in construction, denoting time, an affix comes in the sense of 'being then due'; provided that the thing due be debt.

Thus मासे देयमृणं = मासिकम् 'a debt due in a month'.

Note:— Why do we say ऋणे 'it being a debt'? Observe मासे देया भिक्षा where no affix is added.

1423. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'debt then due,' after the words कलापिन्, अश्वत्थ, and यवबुस denoting time and being in the 7th case in construction.

The words कलापी &c. are terms which indirectly denote time. Thus the time in which the peacocks mate and make noise is called कलापी ॥ The time in which the aśvattha tree fructifies is called अश्वत्थः ॥ The time in which barley is thrashed out is called यवबुस 'barley-chaff'. Thus कलापिनि काले देयमृणं = कलापकम् 'a debt to be paid when the peacocks make noise (i.e. mating or rainy season)'. So also अश्वत्थकम् 'a debt due when the fig-tree flowers'. And यवबुसकम् 'a debt due when the barley is thrashed'.

1424. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'debt-due at that time' after the words 'grîshma' and 'avarasama'.

This debars the अण् and ठञ् ॥ Thus ग्रैष्मे देयमृणं = ग्रैष्मकम् ॥ So also आवरसमकम् 'a debt which will be due next year' or 'which fell due last year'.

Note:— This affix causes Vriddhi, while वुन् would not have done it. Hence the separate affix. The word समा is synonymous with वर्ष 'a year'. The word आवरसमकम् means either आगामिनां संवत्सराणामाद्यवत्सरे देयम् or अतीते वत्सरे देयं यद्यपि न तथा, 'a debt which will be due next year,' or 'which fell due last year'.
entries.note: Corrected misprinted serial number १७२४ to 1424.

entries.english:
1425. The affix ठञ् also (as well as वुञ्) comes after the words 'samvatsara' and 'âgrahâyanî' in the sense of 'debt due.'

Thus संवत्सरे देयमृणं = सांवत्सरिकम्, and सांवत्सरकम् ॥ आग्रहायणिकम् or आग्रहायणकम् ॥

Note:— The word occurs in Sandhivelâdi Class (IV. 3. 16. S. 1387) and takes अण् when 'fruit' or 'festivity' is meant. The present sûtra enjoins ठञ् when 'debt' is indicated.

1426. An affix (like अण् or ठञ् &c.) comes after a word in the 7th case in construction, denoting time, in the sense of 'who then makes noise', and the word so formed refers to a wild beast.

Thus निशायां व्याहरति मृगः = नैशः or नैशिकः 'an animal that makes noise at night.' So also प्रादोषः or प्रादोषिकः (IV. 3. 14. S. 1384) 'a brute that yells in the evening'. The affix added is ठञ्, in the alternative with अण्, by IV. 3. 14. S. 1384.

Note:— Why do we say मृगः 'a beast'? Observe निशायां व्याहरति उलूकः for 'owl' is a bird. Here there is no affixing. The word व्याहरति also means 'to wander'. The Sûtra may, therefore, also be translated as: 'After a word denoting time, an affix (IV. 1. 83 S. 1073) comes as expressing a wild beast who roams at large at that time.'

1427. An affix comes after a word in the 1st case in construction denoting time, in the sense of 'this is his habit or endurance'.

The word कालात् is understood here also. The सोढम् = जितम् or अभ्यस्तम् 'endured or habituated'. Thus निशासहचरितमध्ययनं = निशा 'reading by night'. तत् सोढमस्य छात्रस्य = नैशः or नैशिकः 'a student who is habituated or enured to reading by night'. The affix is ठञ् by IV. 3. 14. S. 1384.

1428. An affix comes after a word in the 7th case in construction, in the sense of 'who stays there'.

The anuvritti of कालात् ceases. The sense of भव here is 'existence', and not that of 'birth' because the sense of birth is taught in the sutra तत्र जातः (IV. 3. 25. S. 1393). Thus, स्रुघ्ने भवः = स्रौघ्नः "who stays in Srughna", राष्ट्रियः ॥

Note:— The repetition of तत्र in the sutra, though its anuvritti could have been drawn from the previous sutra is for the sake of stopping the anuvritti of कालस्य ॥
entries.note: Sutra line was printed on previous page; entry text begins at top of page 781.

entries.english:
1429. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'who stays there', after the Nominal stems दिश् &c.

This debars अण् and छ ॥ As दिशि भवः = दिश्यम् 'lying in a particular quarter', वर्ग्यम् ॥

Note:— The words मुख and जघन which ordinarily mean 'mouth' and 'hip' respectively, have not this meaning when this affix is to be added. They must refer to non-corporeal or abstract objects. As सेनामुख्यः 'who stays in the van of the army', सेनाजघन्यम् 'who stays in the rear of the army'. In fact, the words 'mukha' and 'jaghana' here mean the 'van' and the 'rear' of an army. The word उदक् takes this affix, when the word so formed is a Name. As उदक्या = रजस्वला, otherwise we have ‹?› ॥

1 दिश्, 2 वर्ग, 3 पूर, 4 गण, 5 पक्ष, 6 धाय्य (धाय्या), 7 मित्र, 8 मेधा, 9 असर, 10 पथिन्, 11 रहस्, 12 लोक, 13 उषा, 14 साक्षिन्, 15 देश, 16 आदि, 17 अन्त, 18 मुख, 19 जघन, 20 मेघ, 21 यूथ, 22 उदक्संज्ञायाम्, 23 न्याय, 24 वंश, 25 वेश (विश), 26 काल, 27 आकाश, 28 अनुवंश ॥

1430. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after a word denoting a part of the body.

This debars अण् ॥ As दन्तेषु भवः = दन्त्यम् 'dental, i.e. what stays there', कर्ण्यम् ॥

1431. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, the Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowels of both members of the compound, which is the name of a city of the Eastern People, and which ends in the stem नगर ॥

As सौह्मनागरः (= नगरे भवः), पौर्वनागरः ॥ Why do we say 'of the Eastern people'? Observe माद्रनगरः, from मद्रनगरम् the city of the Northern people.

Note:— The word अङ्गस्य of VI. 4. 1. (S. 200) governs this sutra also, with this difference that it is changed into the locative case here and does not give its genitive termination.

1432. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, the Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowel of the compound ending in the stems जङ्गल, धेनु and बलज, and optionally for the first vowel of these second members also.

As कौरुजङ्गलम् or कौरुजाङ्गलम्, "existing in Kurujangala", वैश्वधेनवम् or वैश्वधैनवम्, सौवर्णवलजम् or सौवर्णवालजम् ॥

1433. The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of 'what stays there', after the words 'driti', 'kukshi', 'kalasi', 'vasti', 'asti' and 'ahi'.

Thus दार्तेयम् 'what stays in a leathern bag', कौक्षेयम्, कालशेयम् 'what exists in a pot', वास्तेयम्, आस्तेयम् and आहेयम् ॥ आहेयम् is the name of a poison. The word अस्ति is a noun and not a verb here. Its use as a Noun is to be seen in phrases like अस्तिक्षीरा गौः, अस्तिमान् = धनवान् ॥
entries.note: SK number printed as 1413 in sutra line, corrected to 1433.

entries.english:
1434. The affix अण् also (as well as ढञ्) comes after the word 'griva' in the sense of 'what stays there.'

This debars यत् (IV. 3. 55. S. 1430). ग्रीवायां भवं ग्रैवेयम् or ग्रैवम् ॥

Note:— The word ग्रीवा means blood vessels, and as they are many, the word is used in the plural in the sutra.

1435. The affix ञ्य comes in the sense of 'who stays there', after the word 'gambhira'.

This debars अण् ॥ गम्भीरे भवं गाम्भीर्यम् 'gravity'.

Vart:— So also after पञ्चजन ॥ As पाञ्चजन्यम् ॥

1436. After an Avyayibhava compound the affix ञ्य is employed, in the sense of 'who stays there'.

Ishti:— The affix comes only after the Avyayibhava compounds parimukha and the rest. The affix ञ्य does not come after every Avyayibhava compound, but only after the words included in the list of परिमुखादि as given in the Ganapatha.

Thus परिमुखं भवम् = पारिमुख्यम्, So also पारिहनव्यम् ॥ Not so औपकूलम्, the word कूल not belonging to the class परिमुख ॥

1 परिमुख, 2 परिहनु, 3 पर्योष्ठ, 4 पर्युलूखल, 5 ‹?›, 6 उपस्थूण, 7 परिसीर, 8 अनुसीर, 9 उपसीर, 10 उपस्थल, 11 उपकलाप, 12 अनुवत्स, 13 बाह्यखड्ग, 14 अनुतिल, 15 अनुशीत, 16 ‹?›, 17 अनुयव, 18 ‹?›, 19 ‹?›, 20 ‹?›, 21 प्रतिशाख, 22 अनुसाय ॥
entries.note: English heading misprinted/misread as 1486, corrected to 1436.

entries.english:
1437. After an Avyayibhava compound, having the word अन्तर् as prior term, the affix ठञ् is employed, in the sense of 'who stays there'.

This debars अण् ॥ Thus आन्तर्वेश्मिकम् from antar-vesmam which means "in the house". That which exists in the house is "Antar-vesmikam". So also आन्तर्गणिकम् ॥

Vart:— So also after the words अध्यात्म &c. as, आध्यात्मिकम्, आधिदैविकम्, आधिभौतिकम् ॥ The class अध्यात्मादि is Akritigana.
1438. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, the Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowel of both members of the compounds अनुशतिक &c.

Thus आधिदैविकम्, आधिभौतिकम्, ऐहलौकिकम्, पारलौकिकम् ॥ These words belong to the Ākṛtigaṇa of अध्यात्म &c.

Note :— (1) आनुशासनिकम् (= अनुशासनस्येदम्) V. 1. 21 and IV. 3. 120. (2) आनुहोडिकः (= अनुहोडेन चरति IV. 4. 8). (3) आनुसांवरणम् (अनुसंवरो देवता V. 1. 96). (4) आनुसांवत्सरम् (IV. 3. 60 formed by ठञ् from अनुसंवत्सरेण दीयते). (5) आङ्गारवेणवः (son of अङ्गारवेणु). (6) प्रैत्याहस्त्यः (= प्रेत्यहस्ते भवं). Some read this word as प्रैवहस्त्यः; this will also take अण् as belonging to विमुक्तादि class. As चास्वाहस्त्यः (= स्वाहस्त्य शब्दोऽस्मिनध्यायेऽस्ति). Others read this as आस्थेहितिकः (= आस्थेहितं प्रयोजनमस्य). The word अस्य in these is treated like a Prātipadika, its case-affix is not elided. (7) वाध्योगः (= वध्योगस्य अपत्यं). It belongs to Bīdādi class. (8) पुष्करसदोऽपत्यं = पौष्करसादिः ॥ This belongs to Bāhvādi class. (9) आनुहारत from अनुहरत् ॥ The same as above. (10) कुरुकतः belongs to Gargādi class. Its patronymic is कौरुकत्यः. (11) कुरुपाञ्चालः (= कुरुपञ्चालेषु भवः). The affix वुञ् is not added here, because जनपदसमुदायो जनपदन गृह्यते ॥
entries.note: Continuation from previous page; embedded Devanagari fragments cleaned from clear context.

entries.english:
1439. When a Taddhita-affix having an indicatory ञ्, णू, or क्, follows, आ is substituted instead of Vṛddhi for the first vowels of the following five words :— devikā, śiṁśapā, dityavāh, dīrghasatra, and śreyas.

Thus दाविकम् (देविकायां भवम्) ॥ दाविकमुदकम्; दाविकाकूलाः शालयः (= देविकाकूले भवाः ।), Similarly शांशपचमसः (= शिंशपाया विकारः) ॥ The word belongs to the Palāśādi class (IV. 3. 141 § 1521), and takes अण् or अञ्, the difference being in accent. Similarly दात्याहम् from दित्यवाट् (दित्यवाहम्) and दार्घसत्रम् (दीर्घसत्रे भवम्) and श्रायसम् (श्रेयसि भवम्) ॥

1440. After the word 'grāma', preceded by 'pari' or 'anu', (the whole being an Avyayībhāva), there is the affix ठञ् in the sense of 'who stays there'.

The word "after an Avyayībhāva", is understood here also. Thus पारिग्रामिकः and आनुग्रामिकः ॥

1441. After the words 'jihvāmūla', and 'aṅguli' there is the affix छ in the sense of 'what stays there'.

This debars यत् (IV. 3. 55). Thus जिह्वामूलीयम्, अङ्गुलीयम् ॥

1442. After a word ending with 'varga', the affix छ is employed in the sense of 'what occurs there'.

As कवर्गीयम्, चवर्गीयम् ॥

1443. After a word ending in 'varga', but not meaning 'a letter or word', the affixes यत् and ख are optionally employed, in the sense of 'who stays there'.

As वासुवर्ग्यः (by यत्), वासुवर्गीणः, (by ख), and वासुवर्गीयः (by छ) ॥

Why do we say, when it does not mean 'a word'? For then it takes one affix only i.e. छ; as कवर्गीयो वर्णः 'a letter belonging to क-class.'
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari examples based on Kashika/SK commentary.

entries.english:
1444. The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'what occurs there', after 'karṇa' and 'lalāṭa', the word denoting an ornament.

Thus कर्णिका 'an ear-ring', ललाटिका ॥

Note:—Why do we say 'denoting an ornament'? Observe कर्ण्यम् 'what is in the ear'.

1445. After the name of a subject of commentary, an affix comes in the sense of 'its commentary', as well as in the sense of 'what occurs there'.

Note:—That by which a thing is explained is called a commentary. The name of a thing explainable is called व्याख्यातव्यनामन्. After such a name, being in the 6th case in construction, the affix is added. The affix expresses तस्य व्याख्यानम् as well as तत्र भवम्, the latter being read into the sūtra by virtue of च ॥

Thus सुपाम् व्याख्यानः — सौपः ग्रन्थः 'Saupa, a book on the explanation of case affixes.' So also, 'Taiṅga—a Commentary on Verbal affixes', 'Kārta a Commentary on kṛt affixes', &c. सौपम् may also mean सुपि भवम् &c.

Note:—The anuvṛtti of तस्य व्याख्यानम् and तत्र भवम् runs simultaneously in all the subsequent apavāda sūtras, and hence we have read the anuvṛtti of तत्र भवम् into this sūtra also.
entries.note: Restored corrupted Devanagari in commentary based on clear grammatical context.

entries.english:
1446. The affix ठञ् comes in the senses of 'staying' and 'a commentary', after a polysyllabic word having udātta on the final, (the word being the name of a thing to be explained).

This debars अण्. Thus नत्वणत्विकम् a commentary on the rules of changes of न् and ष् into ण् and ष्. The word is acutely accented on the final by the rule of a compound having accent on the final (VI. 1. 169).

Note:—Why do we say 'polysyllabic'? Observe ऐष्टिकम् &c. A word of two syllables will take अण् (IV. 3. 72 § 1451). So the counter-example must be of words of one syllable.

Why do we say 'having acute accent on the final'? Observe प्रातिलोमिकम् from प्रतिलोम. This word has acute accent on the initial by the rule of Gati-accent (VI. 2. 49).
entries.note: Sutra serial number misprinted as १४४८ in OCR; fixed to 1446.

entries.english:
1447. The affix ठञ् comes, in the senses of 'occurring', and 'a commentary', after the name of a work to be explained, provided that such work relates to a kratu or a yajña.

These two words generally refer to a sacrifice in which the soma-juice is the chief ingredient. But as they can be accomplished without Soma also, so these words include here non-soma sacrifices also.

This debars अण्. Kratu:— आग्निष्टोमिकः 'a commentary on a work on Agniṣṭoma sacrifices', वाजपेयिकः ॥ yajña:— पाकयाज्ञिकः, राजसूयिकः ॥ The word पाक means 'small', a minor or small sacrifice is called पाकयज्ञः । It is a Karmadhāraya samāsa and has the final acute accent of samāsa in general. The
entries.note: Heading misnumbered as 1446 in English letterpress; entry cuts off at bottom of page 786.

entries.english:
sacrifice with new (nava) rice is ‹?› | The word is derived from यज् with the affix ‹?› (III. 3. 90. § 3268). It retains its accent in the compound being a Krit word. नावयज्ञिकः ॥

This sutra refers to words which are not antodātta.

The word 'vājapeya' is acute in the middle, because peya being a Kridanta-word, formed by yat, retains its accent in the compound (VI. 2. 139. § 3873).

Note 1.—The words kratu and yajña mean generally the same thing i. e. 'a soma sacrifice', but the separate mention of kratu implies that the rule applies to yajñas other than Soma-yajñas, because the word 'kratu' is technically applied to Soma-sacrifice only. Thus पाशुकः, दाशौदनिकः ॥

Note 2.—The word stoma (स्तोम) is synonymous with stuti (स्तुति) "praise". The sacrifices in which Agni is praised is called Agnishtoma. It has acute on the final by पदादिश्च पदान्तश्च ॥

The word vājapeya is a compound of vāja "a kind of barley-gruel" and peya "a sacrifice in which something is drunk", it is formed by yat affix of the 'kritya-lyuto bahulam' subdivision. The acute is on e by VI. 1. 213 § 3701.

The sutra is in the plural to prevent the application of the affix to the word forms 'kratu' and 'yajña' (I. 1. 68 § 25).

1448. The affix वुञ् comes after the name of an explainable work called after a Rishi, in the senses of 'occurring therein' or 'a commentary thereon', when it refers to an Adhyāya only.

Note:—The word ऋषि is the name of ‹?› and those Rishis are only meant whose names are in the Pravara list. The word so formed means always an Adhyāya or Chapter of the work. The phrase कृते ग्रन्थे is understood in this sutra, hence the word means a work the author of which is a Rishi.

Thus a Vedic hymn first seen by (revealed to) Vasishtha is called by lakshaṇā or indirectly वसिष्ठ also. वसिष्ठस्य व्याख्यानस्तत्र भवो वा = वासिष्ठको ऽध्यायः "Vāsishṭhika a chapter containing commentary on Vasishṭha".

Why do we say meaning 'chapter'? Observe वासिष्ठी ऋक् ॥
entries.note: Devanagari affix वुञ् and short Sanskrit words in commentary reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
1449. The affix छन् comes in the senses of 'occurring therein' and 'a commentary thereon', after the words 'paurodāśa' and 'puroḍāśa'.

The verses on the purification &c. of Puroḍāśa a sacrificial rice cake, are called पौरोडाश; the commentary on such paurodāśa mantras will be called पौरोडाशीयः, its feminine will be पौरोडाशीया (IV. 1. 41 § 498). A book on Puroḍāśa cake is called पुरोडाश; a commentary there on will be पुरोडाशीयः, f. पुरोडाशीया (IV. 1. 41 § 498). The ईय of the affix indicates that the feminine is formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 41 § 498). The commentary here refers to the mantras or verses relating to Puroḍāśa, and not to the sacrifice.

1450. The affixes यत् and अण् come in the senses of 'occurring therein' and 'a commentary thereon' after the word Chhandas.

This debars ठक् of the following sūtra. As छन्दस्यः or छान्दसः ॥

1451. The affix ठक् comes in the senses of 'occurring therein' and 'a commentary thereon', after a word of two syllables, and a word ending in short ऋ, and the words 'brāhmaṇa', 'ṛik', 'prathama', 'adhvara', 'purascharana', 'nāma', 'ākhyāta' and 'nāmākhyāta', being the names of explainable works.

Note:—The word nāma being a dissyllabic word would have been covered by the first part of the sūtra, viz., dvyach. Its separate enumeration shows that it is to be taken singly, as well as in composition with ākhyāta.

This debars छन् and अण् ॥ 1. Dissyllabic:—ऐष्टिकः, पाशुकः ॥ 2. Ending in ऋ: चातुर्होतृकः ॥ ब्राह्मणिकः, आर्थिकः, प्राथमिकः, आध्वरिकः, पौरश्चरणिकः, नामिकः, आख्यातिकाः, नामाख्यातिकः ॥

1452. The affix अण् comes in the senses of 'occurring therein' and 'a commentary thereon' after the words 'ṛigayana' &c.

This debars छन्, ठक् and वुञ् । भार्गवम्, औपनिषदः, वैयाकरणः ॥

Note:—The repetition of अण् in the sūtra, though the anuvṛitti of this affix was current from before, is for the sake of preventing the application of any subsequent apavāda rule to the words in this list. Thus ऋगयनिकः ॥

1 ऋगयन, 2 पदव्याख्यान, 3 छन्दोमान, 4 छन्दोभाषा, 5 छन्दोविचित, 6 न्याय, 7 पुनरुक्त, 8 निरुक्त, 9 व्याकरण, 10 निगम, 11 वास्तुविद्या, 12 क्षत्रविद्या, 13 अङ्गविद्या, 14 विद्या, 15 उत्पात, 16 उत्पाद, 17 उद्यान, 18 संवत्सर, 19 मुहूर्त, 20 उपनिषद्, 21 निमित्त, 22 शिक्षा, 23 भिक्षा, 24 छन्दोविजिति, 25 अध्याय ॥

1453. An affix (IV. 1. 83. § 1378 &c.) comes after a word being in the 5th case in construction, in the sense of 'what has come thence'.

Thus स्रुघ्नादागतः स्रौघ्नः 'what has come from Srughna'.

1454. After a word denoting sources of revenue, there is the affix ठक् in the sense of 'come thence'.

Note:—The word आय means what is the share appropriated by the lord. The source of आय is called आयस्थान ॥

This debars अण् and ञ्यङ् ॥ Thus शौल्कशालिक 'what is derived from custom house'.

Note:—The plural in the sūtra prevents Svarūpavidhi (I. 1. 68 § 25).

1455. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'thence come', after the words शुण्डिक &c.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus शौण्डिकः 'excise revenue', कार्कणः, तार्थम् ॥

Note:—The repetition of अण् serves the same purpose as in IV. 3. 73, § 1452, बाधकबाधनार्थम् ॥ As औदपानः ॥

1 शुण्डिक, 2 कृकण, 3 स्थण्डिल, 4 उदपान, 5 उपल, 6 तीर्थ, 7 भूमि, 8 तृण, 9 पर्ण ॥

1456. The affix वुञ् comes, in the sense of 'thence come,' after a word denoting a person connected through the relationship of learning or family origin.

Persons related (sambandha) through learning (such as teacher and pupil), or through blood (yoni, e.g. father and son) are called विद्यायोनिसंबन्धाः

Words denoting such persons take the affix ‹?› ॥
This debars ‹?› and ‹?› ॥ Thus उपाध्यायादागतः = औपाध्यायकम्, 'knowledge derived from a spiritual teacher.' So also ‹?› 'wealth derived from a grand-father.'
entries.note: Continuation tail of SK 1456 from previous page.

entries.english:
1457. The affix ‹?› comes in the sense of 'come thence,' after a word ending in short ‹?›, and denoting a person related through learning or blood.
This debars वुञ् ॥ Thus होतूरागतम् = हौतृकम् derived from Hotri. So also of 'blood' as भ्रातृकम् ॥
Note:—The ‹?› in ‹?› is for the sake of facility of pronunciation, there being no such word ending in long ‹?›.
Note:—When the words do not denote relationship through learning or blood, this affix is not employed. As, सावित्रम् ॥
entries.note: Missing/garbled Devanagari affixes and examples.

entries.english:
1458. The affix ‹?› as well as ‹?› comes, in the sense of 'come thence,' after the word 'pitri.'
Thus पितुरागतम् = पितृ + यत् = पित्री + य = पित्र् + य = पित्र्यम् (the ri is replaced by रीङ् by VII. 4. 27 and the long ई of रीङ् is elided by VI. 4. 148 S. 311) 'paternal—i.e. wealth inherited from father.' With ‹?›
entries.note: Panini reference digits misread in OCR; embedded Devanagari derivation reconstructed.

entries.english:
1459. After a word ending with a patronymic affix, the rule of affix in the sense of 'thence come,' is like that relating to the affix denoting 'its mark.'
Note:—The word ‹?› in the sûtra does not mean the technical Gotra of Grammar, but a descendant-denoting affix in general. The affixes denoting ‹?› are taught in IV. 3. 120 S. 1506 and 127 S. 1507. The affix of IV. 3. 126 S. 1506 which comes after Gotra words, in the sense of 'this is his,' is referred to in this sûtra, not merely the affix of IV. 3. 127 S. 1507, denoting 'this is his mark.' Thus ‹?› formed by ‹?› of IV. 3. 127 S. 1507 mean not only 'the mark belonging to the Vaidas, the Gârgyas, the Dâkshis,' but also that which comes from the Vaidas &c. औपगवानाम् अङ्कः = औपगवः 'the mark belonging to the descendants of Upagu.' So also कापार्थक, नाडायनक, चारायणक ॥ The same words will also denote 'come therefrom' as औपगवेभ्य आगतम् = औपगवम् — ‹?› formed by ‹?› (IV. 3. 126 S. 1506).
Note:—The word ‹?› has the force of complete similarity, as in कामो कामवत् (IV. 2. 94 S. 1237), धर्मो धर्मवत् (IV. 2. 46 S. 1255).
entries.note: SK number misread in Devanagari line; spans pages 790-791.

entries.english:
1460. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ‹?›, or ‹?›, the Vriddhi is always substituted for the first vowel of शुचि, ईश्वर, क्षेत्रज्ञ, कुशल and निपुण when preceded by the Negative particle, but this substitution is optional for the vowel of the Negative particle.
As अशौचम् or आशौचम्, अनैश्वर्यम् or आनैश्वर्यम्, अक्षैत्रज्ञम् or आक्षैत्रज्ञम्, अकौशलम् or आकौशलम्, अनिपुणम् or आनिपुणम् ॥
entries.note: SK serial number misread as 1490; Panini reference digits corrected from ७३ । ३० to 7.3.30.

entries.english:
1461. The affix रूप्य denotes that which from something has originated, when it is added to a word denoting 'cause', or to the name of a man viewed as a cause.
The word मनुष्य is used meaning men as causes. हेतु means cause or instrument. Thus समादागतम् = समरूप्यम् or समीयम् by छ of IV. 2. 138 S. 1321, meaning 'what proceeds from a like cause'. So also विषमरूप्यम् or विषमीयम् ॥ So of men also देवदत्तरूप्यम् or देवदत्तीयम् (IV. 2. 143 S. 1325) 'what originates with Devadatta'.
Note:—The word मनुष्य is in the plural in the sûtra indicating that the svarûpavidhi (I. 1. 68 S. 25) does not apply here.
In denoting हेतु, there is employed the Instrumental case as हेतौ (II. 3. 23 S. 568), while according to the jñâpaka in the present sûtra, the Ablative case may also be employed in denoting हेतु. Or the use of the ablative case in the sense of हेतु, may be explained by II. 3. 25 S. 569.
entries.note: SK number misread as 1469 in sutra line; garbled OCR text in Note restored.

entries.english:
1462. After a word denoting a cause or a man viewed as a cause, there is the affix 'mayat' in the sense of 'come thence'.
Thus सममयम्, विषममयम्, देवदत्तमयम् ॥
Note:—The ट् of मयट् indicates that the feminines of these words are formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470) as, सममयी ॥ The separation of this sûtra from the last is for the sake of preventing the application of the rule of mutual correspondence (I. 3. 10 S. 128) which would have been the case had the rule stood as हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यमयटौ ॥
entries.note: SK number misread as 1492 in sutra line; spans pages 791-792.

entries.english:
1463. After a Nominal-stem which is in the 5th case in construction, an affix (one of those already taught) comes in the sense of 'what appears for the first time'.
The word ततः is understood in the sûtra. The word प्रभवति means what manifests itself, or appears for the first time. Thus हिमवतः प्रभवति हैमवती गङ्गा "The Haimavatî", a name of the Ganges, meaning 'which manifests itself for the first time or appears in the Snowy Range, its source being unknown'.
Note:—So also "The Dâradî" i.e. the Indus appearing for the first time in Dardistan. The word प्रभवति has not the sense of जायते because that is included in तत्र जातः; it therefore means प्रकाशते, प्रथमतः उपलभ्यते, the source or origin being unknown.

1464. The affix ‹?› comes, in the sense of 'what manifests itself there', after the word 'Vidûra'.
This debars ‹?›. Thus वैदूर्यो मणिः a kind of gem found at 'Vidûra'.
Note:—The gem as a matter of fact is not found at Vidûra, but in a mountain called ‹?›. Vidûra is the city where the rough stone is worked upon. In other words, it may be said that the affix is really added to ‹?›, when the latter word is replaced by विदूर; such substitute being only shown in the sûtra, the appropriate sthânî (vâlavâya) being left to inference. Or the word Vidûra may denote both the city as well as a mountain. If it be said that there is no mountain known as Vidûra, then we say that the Grammarians call Vâlavâya by the name of Vidûra, as the merchants call Benares by the name of Jitvarî.
entries.note: OCR typographical errors corrected; embedded Devanagari reconstructed from context.

entries.english: 1465. An affix (IV. 1. 83 &c) comes after a word, being in the 2nd case in construction, in the sense of 'what

goes thereto', provided that, that which goes, is a road or a messenger.
Thus स्रुघ्नं गच्छति = "a road or a messenger that goes to Srughna".
The road may either lead to Srughna, or being in Srughna, be used for going.
Note:—Why do we say "meaning a road or a messenger" (पथिदूतयोः)? Observe स्रुघ्नं गच्छति स्वार्थम् 'he goes to Srughna for his own sake'.
entries.note: Continuation from page 792; text begins mid-sentence.

entries.english:
1466. An affix comes, after a word in the 2nd case in construction, in the sense of 'a door which looks towards that'.
Thus सौघ्नम् 'a gate which looks towards Srughna'—as a gate of Kanyakubja.
Note:—Why do we say "when it is a gate"? Observe स्रुघ्नमभिनिष्क्रामति 'a person faces towards Srughna'.

1467. An affix comes after a word in the 2nd case in construction, in the sense of 'made in relation to any subject', when the thing made is a 'book'.
The word अधिकृत्य means 'aiming at, alluding to, referring to'. Thus शारीरकम् अधिकृत्य कृतो ग्रन्थः = शारीरकीयः i.e. a book relating to the Śārīraka sūtras. The form शारीरकभाष्यम् is however more generally employed. Here no distinction is made between the sutras and the bhashya. Hence the commentary is called Śārīraka.

1468. The affix छ comes in the sense of 'a book made relating to a subject', after the following words in the 2nd case in construction, viz. 'śiśukranda', 'yamasabha' and after the Dvandva compounds, and the words 'indrajanana' &c.
The word छ (IV. 3. 85, S. 1465) and अधिकृत्य कृते ग्रन्थे should be read into the sūtra. This debars अण्. Thus शिशुक्रन्दीयः 'a book treating of the crying of infants'. यमसभीयः 'a book relating to the court of Yama'. The compound is Neuter irregularly (nipātana). Dvandva-Compound as किरातार्जुनीयम्. There is no list of इन्द्रजननादि words. They are ākṛtigaṇa, and must be determined by usage. Thus इन्द्रजननीयम्, विरुद्धभोजनीयम् &c.
Note:—The words शिशुक्रन्द and यमसभ might have been included in the inchoate class (आकृतिगण). The separate enumeration of these words in the sūtra, is merely for the sake of amplification.
entries.note: Reconstructed fragmented prose and Devanagari examples across page break.

entries.english:
1469. After a word in the 1st case in construction, an affix comes in the sense of 'this is his dwelling place'.
Note:—The word सः shows that the word to which the affix is to be added is in the nominative case. अस्य 'his' shows that the meaning of the affix is that of a genitive case. निवासः shows that the first word in construction must signify a dwelling place. निवासः means 'a country i.e. where a person lives (nivasanti asmin)'.
स्रुघ्नो निवासोऽस्य = सौघ्नः 'a present dweller of Srughna'.
entries.note: Corrected serial number misread as १४४६ in OCR; restored embedded Devanagari pronouns and keywords.

entries.english:
1470. After a word in the 1st case in construction, an affix comes in the sense of 'this is his mother-land'.
The difference between निवासः and अभिजनः is this. Where a person lives himself for the present, that is his निवासः or dwelling-place. Where his ancestors (पूर्वे) have lived, that is his 'native country, home or ancestral abode'. Thus सौघ्नः 'a person whose ancestral home is in Srughna'.
Note:—The separation of this sūtra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sūtra, in which the anuvṛtti of 'abhijana' only runs.
entries.note: Restored embedded Devanagari keywords from context.

entries.english:
1471. The affix छ comes after a word denoting mountain, in the sense of 'this is his mother-land', when it is a person who lives by arms.
The word आयुधजीविन् means a person who earns his livelihood by arms. The phrase सोऽस्याभिजनः is to be read into the sūtra. Thus हृद्गोलः पर्वतोऽभिजन एषां ते हृद्गोलीयाः 'the mercenary soldiers whose ancestral abode is the Hṛdgola mountain'.
Why do we say आयुधजीविभ्यः? Observe आर्क्षोदा ब्राह्मणाः 'the Brāhmaṇas whose native place is Ṛkṣoda mountains'.
Note:—Why do we say 'mountains'? Observe सांकाश्यका आयुधजीविनः ॥
entries.note: Sutra and Sanskrit vritti are on page 794, but English heading sits on page 795.

entries.english:
1472. The affix ण्य comes in the sense of 'this is his native-land', after the words शण्डिक &c.
This debars छ &c. Thus शाण्डिक्यः, सार्वसैन्यः &c.
1. शण्डिक, 2. सर्वसेन, 3. सर्वकेश, 4. ‹?›, 5. शण्ड (षण्ढ), 6. ‹?›, 7. ‹?›, 8. बोध ॥
entries.note: Restored corrupted Devanagari gaṇa list items.

entries.english:
1473. The affixes अण् and अञ् come respectively, after the words 'Sindhu' &c. and 'Takṣaśilā' &c. in the sense of 'this is his native-land'.
Thus सैन्धवः. So also ताक्षशिलः.
Note:—Many of the words occurring in the Sindhu-class, are found in the Kachchhādi class (IV. 2. 133, S. 1357) also. Those words would have taken अण् by sūtra IV. 2. 133, S. 1357. The present sūtra prevents the affixing of वुञ् (IV. 2. 134, S. 1358) to those words under circumstances mentioned in sūtra IV. 2. 134, S. 1358 when the further significance of अभिजनः is added to them.
1. सिन्धु, 2. वर्णु, 3. मधुमत्, 4. कम्बोज, 5. साल्व, 6. कश्मीर, 7. गन्धार, 8. किष्किन्धा, 9. उरसा (उरस्), 10. दरद् (दरत्), 11. नन्दिका (गान्दिका), 12. कुलून, 13. पिरसा ॥
1. तक्षशिला, 2. वत्सोद्धरण, 3. कैमेडुर (कौमेडुर), 4. ग्रामणी, 5. ‹?›, 6. क्रोष्टु (सिंहकोष्ठ), 8. संकुचित, 9. किङ्कर, 10. काण्डधार (काण्डवार), 11. पर्वत, 12. पावसान, 13. बर्बर, 14. ‹?›, 15. साकल ॥
entries.note: Restored affixes and gana readings from clear context.
Entry cuts off at the bottom of page 795; only the sutra line is printed.

entries.english:
1474. After the words तूदी, शालातुर, वर्मती, and कूचवार, come respectively the affixes ढक्, छण्, ढञ्, and यक् in the sense of 'this is his native land'.

This debars अण् ॥ Thus तौदेयः, शालातुरीयः, वार्म्मतेयः, and कूचवार्यः ॥
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line was on preceding page (p. 795); English heading begins on p. 796.

entries.english:
1475. An affix (IV. 1. 83) comes after a word in the first case in construction, in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration or love'.

The word भक्ति in the sútra means 'serving', 'worshipping or loving'.

Thus स्रुघ्नो भक्तिरस्य = सौघ्नः 'a person who is loyal to Srughna'.

The anuvritti of the word अभिजन ceases. The words सः and अस्य should be read into the sútra.
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari from context.

entries.english:
1476. After a word denoting a thing not possessing consciousness, but not being the name of a country or time, the affix ठक्, is employed, in the sense of 'this is his object of devotion or love'.

This debars अण्; and छ also. Thus अपूपा भक्तिरस्य = आपूपिकः 'a person who loves cakes'. पायसिकः ॥

Why do we say 'not possessing consciousness'? Observe देवदत्तः ॥ Why do we say 'not being the name of a country'? Observe सौघ्नः ॥ Why do we say 'not denoting time'? Observe ग्रैष्मः 'who loves summer.'
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari from context.

entries.english:
1477. The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration', after the word महाराज ॥

This debars अण् ॥ As माहाराजिकः 'who loves or serves the Maharaja'.

The difference between this and the ठक् of the last aphorism, is in the Accent only.
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari from context.

entries.english:
1478. The affix वुन् comes in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration', after the words 'Vasudeva' and Arjuna.

This debars छ and अण् ॥ Thus वासुदेवकः, अर्जुनकः ॥

1479. The affix वुञ् comes diversely, in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration', after a word denoting Gotra or a Kshatriya.

This debars अण् and छ ॥ Thus: ग्लौचुकायनकः 'who loves or serves &c. Gluchukayani Kshatriyas' — नाकुलकः ।

Note:—The word आख्यायां in the sútra indicates that the words should be the names of well-known or famous Kshatriyas, and not of anybody who is a Kshatriya by profession.

The word बहुलम् shows the non-universality of this rule. Thus पाणिनी भक्तिरस्य = पाणिनीयः ॥

Note:—The word गोत्र does not mean here the Grammatical Gotra, but a word formed by a patronymic affix in general.
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari from context.

entries.english:
1480. Of words denoting Princes (lit. who are lords of janapada) the base and the affix meaning 'this is his object of veneration' are the same, in every respect, like those of a word denoting kingdom, provided that, the Prince-denoting words have, in the plural, the same form, as the kingdom-denoting words.

Note:—The words of this sútra require a detailed analysis: जनपदिनाम् gen. plural of जनपदिन् meaning 'lord of an inhabited country' i.e. Kshatriya Princes; बहुवचने 'in the plural'; जनपदेन समानशब्दानाम् 'of the same form as the janapada-denoting word'; जनपदवत् सर्वम् 'every thing is like jana-pada'. In other words, 'after those bases denoting Kshatriya princes which in the plural have the same forms as the names of the countries, the affix in the sense of veneration will be the same as will come after a janapada word'. Now the affixes denoting veneration as regards country words are given in sútras IV. 2. 124 (S. 1348) &c. and those affixes will apply here.

Thus अङ्गकः formed by वुञ् of sútra IV. 2. 125, (S. 1349) meaning 'who loves the country of Angas'. Similarly ‹?› ॥

Similarly अङ्गाः क्षत्रियाः भक्तिरस्य = अङ्गकः formed by the same affix with this difference of meaning 'who loves the Kshatriyas Angas'. So ‹?› &c.

Why do we say 'of Kshatriya Princes' (janapadinám)? Observe, पञ्चाला ब्राह्मणा भक्तिरस्य = पाञ्चालः ॥ Here the general affix अण् is employed.
