Why do we say 'the word having the same sound as the janapada word'? Thus पौरवो राजा भक्तिरस्य = पौरवीयः ॥
entries.note: Entry spans pages 797-798; illegible Devanagari replaced with placeholder.

entries.english:
1481. After a word in the 3rd case in construction, an affix (IV. 1. 83 &c.) comes, in the sense of 'enounced by him'.

The word प्रोक्त means 'preeminently spoken'. It should be distinguished from the word कृत meaning 'done or made'. For the sense of कृत has been already taught in the sútra (IV. 3. 116, S. 1387). Thus पाणिनीयम् 'the system of grammar enounced by Panini'.

1482. The affix छण् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the words 'tittiri', 'varatantu', 'khandika', and 'ukha'.

Thus तैत्तिरीयाः 'those who learn (IV. 2. 66, S. 1278) the Veda enounced by Tittiri'.

Note:—According to Kásiká this is confined to the Chhandas only. Therefore it will not apply to classical slokas, as ‹?›.

The word Chhandas is drawn from sútra IV. 3. 106, S. 1486 and तदधीते from IV. 2. 66, S. 1278.
entries.note: Illegible embedded quotation replaced with placeholder.

entries.english:
1483. The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the words 'Kāśyapa' and 'Kauśika' when denoting Vedic Seers.
This debars ‹?›. The ण् of णिनि is for the sake of Vṛiddhi (useful in the subsequent sūtra). This is confined, like the last, to the Vedic works. Thus काश्यापिनः 'those who study (IV. 2. 64 S. 1274) the Kalpa enounced by Kāśyapa'.
Note:—Why do we say "Vedic Sages"? Observe इदानीन्तनेन गोत्रकारेण प्रोक्तं काश्यपमधिकृत्य कृतम् 'a work enounced by a modern Kāśyapa, one belonging to the Gotra Kāśyapa; not a Rishi'.

1484. After words denoting the pupils of 'Kalāpī' and 'Vaiśampāyana', the affix णिनि is employed in the sense of 'enounced by him'.
Note:—This debars ‹?› and ‹?›. There are four words which express pupils of Kalāpa: as हरिद्रु, कङ्कल, तुम्बुरु, उलपः ॥ There are nine words expressing pupils of Vaiśampāyana: as, आलम्बि, पलङ्ग, कमल, ऋचाभ, आरुणि, ताण्ड्य, श्यामायन, कठ, कलापी ॥
Thus हारिद्रविणः 'those who study (IV. 2. 64 S. 1274) the works enounced by Haridru.' So also आलम्बिनः ॥
Note:—The word चरक means वैशम्पायनः hence चरकाः means pupils of वैशम्पायनः ॥

1485. The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after a word in the 3rd case in construction, when it denotes a Brāhmaṇa or a Kalpa-work enounced by ancient sages.
This sūtra further gives the sense of the affix. पुराण means 'Ancient Sages' equivalent to पुराणप्रोक्त of the Brāhmaṇa literature, the example is शाट्यायकिनः, so also from भल्लु, भाल्लविनः । Kalpa work as पैङ्गीकल्पः ॥
Why do we say पुराणप्रोक्तेषु? Observe याज्ञवल्क्यानि ब्राह्मणानि, आश्मरथः कल्पः ॥ The य of these words is elided by VI. 4. 151. S. 1082, Yājñavalkya &c. being sages of modern times. The ‹?› affix IV. 2. 66. S. 1278, will not also apply to these, because the word ब्राह्मण in IV. 2. 66. S. 1278 is restricted to पुराणप्रोक्त of the present sūtra.

1486. The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the words शौनक &c., in denoting chhandas.
This debars ‹?› and ‹?›. Thus शौनकेन प्रोक्तमधीयते—शौनकिनः 'who study (IV. 2. 64 S. 1274) the chhandas enounced by Śaunaka', वाजसनेयिनः &c.
Note:—Why do we say in denoting Chhandas? Observe शौनकीया शिक्षा 'the orthography of Śaunaka'.
The word कठ occurs in this list. This must always be taken as a compound for affixing this affix. After the single word कठ the affix is elided (IV. 3. 107 S. 1487). Thus ‹?›
1. शौनक, 2. वाजसनेय, 3. ‹?›, 4. शापेय (सांपेय), 5. ‹?›, 6. ‹?›, 7. ‹?› (स्कम्भ), 8. स्कन्ध, 9. देवदर्शन, 10. ‹?›, 11. रज्जुकठ, 12. ‹?›, 13. कषाय, 14. ‹?›, 15. ‹?›, 16. ‹?› (पुरुषादक), 17. अश्वपेय, 18. ‹?›, 19. स्कन्ध, 20. देवदर्शन, 21. तलवकार ।
entries.note: SK serial number misprinted as 1489 in Devanagari line; Panini reference printed as 1.3.106 for 4.3.106.

entries.english:
1487. The affix denoting 'enounced by him' is elided, by luk-substitution, after the words Kaṭha and Charaka.
The word कठ would have taken णिनि as it is a वैशम्पायनान्तेवासी word; and चरक would have taken the affix अण्. Both are elided. Thus कठाः 'who study the Chhandas enounced by Kaṭha'; चरकाः &c.
Note:—The word 'Chhandas' qualifies this sūtra. Observe काठकाः चारकाः श्लोकाः ॥

1488. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the word Kalāpī.
This debars णिनि of IV. 3. 104 S. 1484. Thus कालापाः 'who study the work enounced by Kalāpī'.
Note:—The word कालापः is thus formed:—कलापिन् + अण् ॥ Here comes in force Sūtra VI. 4. 144 S. 679, which declares that इन् of कलापिन् should be elided before the taddhita affix. This elision is, however, debarred by sūtra VI. 4. 164 S. 1245 which declares that words ending in the affix इन् retain their form when not denoting a progeny follows. Therefore कलापिन् would have retained its इन् but for the following Vārtika.
Vārt:—The टि portion of the following words is elided when a Taddhita follows: सब्रह्मचारिन्, पीठसर्पिन्, कलापिन्, कुथुमिन्, तैतिलिन्, आजलिन्, लाङ्गलिन्, शिलालिन्, शिखण्डिन्, सूकरसद्मन्, पर्ण ॥ Thus इन् being elided, we have कालापः ॥
The final इन् with the vowel that precedes it, is dropped before a Taddhita in the following: 1. सब्रह्मचारिन्—साब्रह्मचाराः (IV. 3. 120 S. 1500), 2. पीठसर्पिन्—पैठसर्पाः (IV. 3. 120 S. 1500), 3. कलापिन्—कालापाः (IV. 3. 108 and IV. 2. 59 S. 1488 and 1269), 4. कुथुमिन्—कौथुमाः (IV. 3. 101 S. 1481), 5. तैतिलिन्—तैतिलाः (IV. 3. 116 S. 1496), 6. आजलिन्—आजलाः (IV. 2. 59 S. 1269), 7. लाङ्गलिन्—लाङ्गलाः, 8. शिलालिन्—शैलालाः, 9. शिखण्डिन्—शैखण्डाः, 10. सूकरसद्मन्—सौकरसद्माः, 11. पर्ण—पार्णाः ॥ In the above those which end in इन्, elide the इन् in spite of VI. 4. 164, and those in मन् contradict VI. 4. 167.

1489. The affix ढिनुक् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the word 'Chhagalin'.
The word छगलिन् being a word denoting the pupil of कलापी would have taken णिनि (IV. 3. 104 S. 1484). This debars that. Thus छागलेयिनः 'who study the Chhandas enounced by Chhagalī'.
entries.note: Heading serial number misprinted as 4489 for 1489; Panini ref printed as 4.3.103 for 4.3.109.

entries.english:
1490. The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him', after the words Pārāśarya and Śilālin, the works enounced being Bhikshu-Sūtra and Naṭa-Sūtra respectively.
Note:—This affix णिनि is to be read into the sūtra and not ढिनुक्. The भिक्षुसूत्र and नटसूत्र are works treating of the duties of भिक्षुक 'religious mendicants' and नट 'jugglers, dancers':
entries.note: SK serial number misread as 1460 in sutra line; entry cut off at bottom of page 801 (partial: head).

entries.english:
Thus ‹?› (VI. 4. 152 S. 2119)—‹?›, 'the treatise of Parasarya on the duties of Bhikshus'. Similarly ‹?›
Note:—These words of course, have the additional sense of 'he who studies the works so enounced by Parasarya and Sailalin'. See IV. 2. 66 S. 1278. As ‹?›, ‹?›. According to some, it always expresses this relation (‹?› IV. 2. 66) and never a ‹?› alone. These are treated metaphorically as Chhandas. Why do we say 'denoting Bhikshu and Nata Sutras'? Observe शरावरण, ‹?›.
entries.note: Tail fragment of SK 1490; heavily degraded Devanagari fragments replaced with placeholders.

entries.english:
1491. The affix ‹?› comes, in the sense of 'enounced by him', the thing enounced being Bhikshu Sutra and Nata Sutra, after the words 'Karmanda' and 'Krisasva'.
Thus ‹?›, 'the mendicants who study the Bhikshu-sutra of Karmandin'; ‹?› 'the actors who study the Nata sutra of Krisasvin'. Otherwise ‹?› and ‹?›. See IV. 2. 66.
entries.note: Devanagari forms in prose and examples degraded in OCR; replaced with placeholders.

entries.english:
1492. An affix (IV. 1. 83 &c.) comes after a word in the third case in construction, in the sense of 'in the same direction with that'.
The word ‹?› means ‹?› i. e. a common direction. Thus सुदामा एकदिक् सौदामनी विद्युत् "a lightning, literally, that which is in the same direction as the hill called the Sudaman".
Note:—The repetition of तेन, though it could have been supplied by anuvritti from IV. 3. 101, S. 1481 is for the sake of indicating that the anuvritti of उपज्ञाते &c. which regulated all the preceding ten sutras, does not extend to this aphorism, and therefore the ‹?› of IV. 2. 66 S. 1278 which was applied to those sutras does not apply here.
entries.note: Severely corrupt Devanagari words in commentary replaced with placeholders; heading number fixed from 144.2.

entries.english:
1493. The affix तसिल् comes in the sense of 'in the same direction with that.'
This ordains another affix in addition to the previously taught ‹?› &c. &c. The words formed by this affix are Indeclinables as it is an affix mentioned in the svaradi class. (I. 1. 37 S. 447) Thus 'in the same direction as Himavat' ‹?›, ‹?›.
entries.note: Corrupt Devanagari in sutra line and examples replaced with placeholders.

entries.english:
1494. The affix य as well as the affix तसिल् comes in the sense of 'in the same direction with that,' after the word उरस् ॥
Thus उरसा एकदिक् उरस्य or उरस्तस् । The तसिल् is read into the sutra by force of the word च ॥

1495. After a word in the 3rd case in construction, an affix is employed in the sense of 'discovered by him'.
Knowledge acquired by oneself without being taught is called उपज्ञा i. e. an intuition or self taught knowledge. Thus पाणिनिना उपज्ञातम् = पाणिनीयम् 'the law of Grammar discovered by Panini'.

1496. An affix comes after a word in the 3rd case in construction, in the sense of 'made', the thing made being 'a book'.
Thus वररुचिना कृताः = वाररुचाः श्लोकाः 'the verses composed by Vararuchi'.
Note 1:—Why do we say 'a book'? Observe तक्ष्णा कृतः प्रासादः 'the palace made by Takshan'.
That which one originates is called कृतम् and is therefore an 'art', while knowledge of laws &c. that already exist, but are discovered for the first time by some one, is called उपज्ञातम् ॥

1497. An affix comes after a word in the 3rd case in construction, in the sense of 'made by him', when the whole word is a Name.
Thus मक्षिकाभिः कृतं माक्षिकं मधु 'honey', literally 'made by a bee', मक्षिका meaning a bee—मक्षिक (VI. 4. 148 S. 311). The anuvritti of 'ग्रन्थे' does not, of course, apply here.

1498. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'made by him', after the words Kulala &c. the whole word so formed being a Name.
Thus कौलालकम् 'a porcelain lit. made by a potter'. So also वारुडकम् ॥
1 कुलाल, 2 वरुड, 3 चण्डाल, 4 निषाद, 5 कर्मार, 6 सेना, 7 सिरिन्ध्र (सिरिन्ध), 8 सन्धि (सेन्धिव), 9 देवराज, 10 परिषद् (पर्षद्), 11 वधू, 12 मधु, 13 रूप, 14 रुद्र, 15 अनडुह्, 16 ब्रह्मन्, 17 कुम्भकार, 18 श्वपाक, 19 जय ॥

1499. The affix अण् comes after the words 'kshudra', 'bhramara', 'vatara' and 'padapa' in the sense of 'made by him', the whole word being a Name.
This debars वुञ्, there being difference in accent between अण् and वुञ् । Thus क्षुद्राभिः कृतम् = क्षौद्रम् 'honey lit. made by a small bee'. So also भ्रामरम्, वातरम् and पादपम् ॥
entries.note: Devanagari affixes reconstructed from context (sutra 4.3.119 ordains an, debarring vun).

entries.english:
1500. After a word in the 6th case in construction, an affix (IV. 1. 83 &c.) comes in the sense of 'this is his'.
The five universals अण् &c. (IV. 1. 83) and the affixes घ &c. (IV. 2. 93) come in this sense.
Thus उपगोरिदम् = औपगवम् 'of Upagu'.
Note:—The affixes, however, do not come, when the word governed by the possessive case, is अनन्तर &c. Thus देवदत्तस्यानन्तरम् ॥ In short the thing possessed must be property, village, kingdom or men.
Vart:—The word ‹?› takes ‹?› (‹?› and ‹?›) and ‹?› preceded by an ‹?›. As, ‹?› ॥
Vart:—The affix रञ् comes after अग्नीत्, (= अग्निमिन्धे 'who kindles the sacred fire' formed by Kvip) in the sense of 'sanctuary', and the base gets the designation of भ ॥ Agnidh is the name of a Ritvik priest. As आग्नीध्रम् 'The place where the sacred fire is kept' as well as the officiating priest of Agni. The word अग्नीत् being treated as a Bha and not as a pada, the त् is not changed to द् (VIII. 2. 39).
entries.note: First vartika heavily garbled in OCR, uncertain fragments replaced with placeholders; second vartika fixed with context.

entries.english: Vārt:— The affix 'sheṇyan' comes after ‹?›, in the sense of placing. Thus : 'the verses (recited while) placing the fuel on fire', (IV. 1. 41 ) ॥

1501. The affix यत् comes after रथ, in the sense of 'this is his.'
This debars अण् ॥ Thus रथस्येदं रथ्यम् belonging to the chariot—i.e. 'wheel or the axle'.
Note:—The word रथ्य is confined to describe 'the parts of chariot.' This rule applies also to compounds ending with रथ, as, ‹?›, because of the Vārtika ‹?›, after रथ, पद् and ‹?› in applying the affix there is tadanta-vidhi.
entries.note: Reconstructed Devanagari from context.

entries.english:
1502. When preceded by a word denoting 'a draught animal', रथ takes the affix अञ् in the sense of 'this is his'.
This debars यत् ॥ Thus आश्वरथम् 'the wheel of a horse-cart'.
Note:—The word पत्त्र means 'that by which any one goes' or a draught-animal, like camel. It is formed by the affix ष्ट्रन् (III. 2. 182).
entries.note: Reconstructed missing affix and Sanskrit words from context.

entries.english:
1503. After a word denoting a draught-animal, and after the words 'adhvaryu' and 'parishad,' the affix अण् is added [in the sense of 'this is his'].
This debars ‹?› ॥
Vārt:— When the sense is that of a thing to be carried, then is अण् added, to a word denoting a draught-animal. Thus अश्वस्येदं वहनीयमाश्वम्, 'a load to be or suited for being, carried by a horse.' So also आध्वर्यवम् and पारिषदम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed affix and examples from context.

entries.english:
1504. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is his,' after the words 'hala' and 'sira.'
Thus हलस्येदम् = हालिकम्, सैरिकम् ॥

1505. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'this is his', after Dvandva compounds of words denoting 'mutual enmity', or 'matrimonial relationship.'
This debars ‹?› and ‹?› ॥ Thus of enmity ‹?›. Similarly of married couples as ‹?› ॥
Note:—The Dvandva compounds of words denoting natural enemies will be singular neuter by II. 4. 9. S. 918. Their secondary derivatives, however, are feminine.
Vārt:— Prohibition must be stated of the word देवासुर &c. As देवासुरम् ॥ ‹?› ॥
entries.note: Corrected typographical errors in English and reconstructed damaged text.

entries.english:
1506. The affix वुञ् comes, in the sense of 'this is his', after the words denoting Family-names or names of Vedic Schools.
This debars अण् as well as ‹?› ॥ Thus gotra:— औपगवकम् ॥
Vārt:— The word चरण which ordinarily means Vedic School, means here duties or doctrines (dharma), and traditions (āmnāya). Thus ‹?› — 'the dharma-Sūtras or the tradition belonging to the school of Kaṭhas'.
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1606, corrected to 1506.

entries.english:
1507. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'this is his', after a Patronymic word ending with the affix अञ्, ञ्यङ् or इञ्, the words so formed expressing a multitude, a mark or a sign.
Note:—The word सङ्घ means 'congregation'. The word अङ्क and लक्षण should be distinguished. लक्षण means a mark which is the property of that person and forms a distinguishing feature of that person, as ‹?› learning [of the] Bidas, the Bidas being famous for learning. The word अङ्क is a mark which shows that the thing so marked is the property of another as a mark on a cow showing to what person or clan that cow belongs. The अङ्क though occurring in a person or thing does not belong to that person or thing, as the mark of a cow does not belong to the cow, but the लक्षण is a mark which belongs to the person or thing wherein it is found.
This sūtra debars वुञ् of the last aphorism.
Vārt:— The word घोष 'a cow-pen', should also be read along with the सङ्घ &c. Thus the words so formed denote four things (1) congregation, (2) mark, (3) sign, and (4) a hamlet or cowpen. This being so, the rule of mutual correspondence according to order of enumeration (I. 3. 10 S. 128) does not apply.
Thus बैदाः (IV. 1. 104 S. 1106)—(Masculine), 'a congregation', but बैदम् (Neuter) meaning, a sign or a hamlet of the Bidas. ञ्यङन्तात्— (IV. 1. 105 S. 1107)—गार्ग्य + अण् = गार्गाः (VI. 4. 148, 151 S. 311, 1082) 'a congregation, or a mark of the Gārgyas' (IV. 1. 95 S. 1095), दाक्षि + अण् = दाक्षाः (VI. 4. 148 S. 311) 'a congregation &c of the Dākshis'. दाक्षम् 'a mark of the Dākshis'.
Note 1.—The ण of अण् could not serve the purpose of Vṛiddhi here, for all the words to which this affix is added, have Vṛiddhi by virtue of the affixes in which they end. The ‹?› would have served the purpose as well, so far as Vṛiddhi is concerned, but ण is used to show that the feminine is formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470). Thus बैदी. It further prevents पुंवद्भाव in compounds (VI. 3. 34 S. 849), बैदीविद्याऽस्य—बैदीविद्यः i.e. बिदानाम् असाधारणी या विद्या सा यस्यास्ति सः ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed terms across page split (pp. 806-807).

entries.english:
1508. The affix optionally comes, in the sense of 'this is his congregation, mark, sign or hamlet,' after the word शाकल ।
This debars वुञ् ॥ Thus शाकलेन प्रोक्तमधीयते शाकलाः (IV. 3. 101 S. 1481 and IV. 2. 64 S. 1274), शाकलानां सङ्घः शाकलः or शाकलकः (IV. 3. 126 S. 1506) meaning 'a congregation, &c. of the students of the science revealed by Śākala.' When denoting लक्षण it will be of the neuter gender.
1509. The affix ण्य comes in the sense of 'this is his Law or Tradition,' after the words 'chhandoga,' 'aukthika,' 'yājñika,' 'bahvṛicha' and 'naṭa'.

Note:—The anuvṛitti of संघ &c. ceases. This debars वुञ् and अण् ॥ The phrase 'चरणाद्धर्माम्नाययोः' from sûtra IV. 3. 126, S. 1506 is understood here and applies even to the word नटः ॥
Thus छन्दोगानां धर्मो वाऽऽम्नायो छान्दोग्यम् the Law or Tradition peculiar to the Chhandoga. So also औक्थिक्यम्, याज्ञिक्यम्, बाह्वृच्यम्, and नाट्यम् ॥
Not having this sense we have छान्दोगं कुलम् 'the family of Chhandoga'.
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 1509 from preceding page.

entries.english:
1510. The affix वुञ् is not used after a Family-name, when it denotes a 'beginner pupil', and 'a boarder pupil.'
The word दण्डमाणवाः means a little naughty boy (माणव), the only means of instilling knowledge in whom is the rod (दण्ड), or whose principal sign of studentship is the 'danda' and nothing intrinsic, i. e., a mere beginner. The न is changed to ण in माणव by IV. 1. 161 S. 1185. अन्तेवासिनः are pupils or boarders who live in their teacher's houses. The word 'gotra' is understood here. Thus दाक्षाः 'the junior pupils of Dâkshi.'
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari and corrupt characters reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
1511. The affix छ comes in the sense of 'this is his', after the words रैवतिक &c.
All these words end with Gotra affixes, and require वुञ् (IV. 3. 126 S. 1506), this ordains छ instead. Thus रैवतकीयः, बैजवापीयः &c.
1. रैवतक, 2. स्वापिशि, 3. क्षेमवृद्धि, 4. गौरग्रीवि (गौरग्रीव), 5. श्रौन्मेथि (औन्मेथि), 6. औदवापि (औदवाहि), 7. बैजवापि ॥
entries.note: Gaṇa list and embedded Devanagari restored from OCR corruption.

entries.english:
1512. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'this is his', after the words 'kaupinjala' and 'hâstipada'.
This debars वुञ् (IV. 3. 126). Thus कौपिञ्जलः, हास्तिपदः ॥ This sûtra is really a Vârtika. The word कौपिञ्जल means the descendant of कुपिञ्जल ॥ It is formed by अण् by the nipâtana of this sûtra. To this is again added अण् in order to exclude the वुञ् affix. Similarly the son of हस्तिपाद is called हस्तिपद ॥ It is formed by अण् and पाद changed to पद by nipâtana. To हास्तिपद is added the affix of this sûtra.
entries.note: Restored typographical errors in English commentary and Devanagari.

entries.english:
1513. The affix अण् comes, in the sense of 'this is his', after the word 'âtharvaṇika', and the penultimate 'ika' is elided.
This debars वुञ् (IV. 3. 126 S. 1506). आथर्वणिकस्यायम् आथर्वणो धर्म आम्नायो वा 'the Âtharvaṇa i. e. the Law or the Tradition of the Âtharvaṇikas'.
The phrase चरणाद्धर्माम्नाययोः is understood here. This sûtra is also a Vârtika.
entries.note: SK serial number misprinted as 1618 in heading, corrected to 1513 to preserve sequence.

entries.english:
1514. An affix (IV. 1. 83 &c.) comes after a word in the sixth case in construction, in the sense of 'a modification thereof.'
Note:—The word विकारः means the change of condition of the original. The word तस्य, though its anuvṛitti could have been supplied from the previous sûtras, has been repeated here, in order to show that the governing force of शेषे (IV. 2. 92) does not extend further. The affixes taught, therefore, under शेषे (IV. 2. 92, S. 1312 &c.) such as घ, ख &c. have not the sense of तस्य विकारः ॥ No affix has been taught here in this sûtra, the general affix अण् (IV. 1. 83) therefore will come in this sense, as well as the affixes to be taught hereafter.
Vârt:—अश्मन् loses its टि before a Taddhita affix meaning 'prepared therewith': as आश्मः, otherwise आश्मनः ॥ So also भस्मन् and मार्त्तिकः ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed dropped/corrupted Devanagari in Note and Vartika from clear context.

entries.english:
1515. An affix comes after a word denoting an animal, a herb and a tree, in the sixth case in construction, in the sense of 'this is its part', (as well as 'this is its modification').
By the word च in the sûtra, the phrase तस्य विकारः is also read into the sûtra.
Thus मयूरस्य विकारोऽवयवो वा = मायूरः (IV. 3. 154) 'a modification, product or part of a peacock—viz a fan' &c. So also of 'herbs'; as मौर्वम् 'product of Mûrvâ i. e. ashes or the stalk of Mûrvâ'. So also of 'trees', as पैप्पलम्, meaning 'the stalk or the ashes of Pippala tree.'
Note:—In the subsequent sûtra, both the words विकार and अवयव have governing force. But after words which denote non-animals, non-plants or non-trees, the affixes have only the sense of विकार. This is a rather unique case of double anuvṛitti, not co-extensive in every respect,
entries.note: Entry text cuts off at the bottom of page 810; continuation on next page.

entries.english:
1516. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'its modification or its part', after the words बिल्व &c.

This debars अञ् and मयट् । Thus वैल्वम् 'the modification or part of Bilwa'.

Note:—The word गवेधुका occurs in this list. It would have taken अण् by the next sūtra also; its inclusion in the class of Bilwadi is for the sake of preventing the application of मयट् to this word.

1 बिल्व, 2 मुद्ग, 3 काण्ड, 4 मुद्ग, 5 मसूर, 6 गोधूम, 7 इक्षु, 8 वेणु, 9 गवेधुका, 10 कार्पासी, 11 पाटली, 12 कर्कन्धू, 13 कुटीर ॥

1517. After a word having क as penultimate, the affix अण् comes, in the sense of modification or a part, or both, as appropriate.

This debars अञ् ॥ Thus from तर्कु we get तार्कवम्, from तित्तिडीक we get तैत्तिडीकम् ॥

The words तित्तिडीक &c. have acute on the middle (Phiṭ Sū. II. 16).
entries.note: Supplied missing penultimate character 'क' indicated by sutra and context.

entries.english:
1518. The affix अण् with the augment षुक् comes in the sense 'its modification', after the words 'trapu' and 'jatu'.

This debars अञ् (IV. 3. 139 S. 1519). As, ‹?›; so also जातुषम् 'modification of tin and lac'.

Note:—In these words denoting non-organic beings, the sense of अवयव is not denoted by the affix.
entries.note: Corrected misprinted heading number 1618 to 1518.

entries.english:
1519. The affix अण् comes after a word ending in short उ, in the sense of 'modification or part', (provided that, the word has not grave accent on the first syllable).

Thus देवदारवम्, भाद्रदारवम् ॥

Note:—The words देवदारु and भद्रदारु are ādy-udātta owing to Phiṭ Sū. II. 14 (पीतद्र्वादिनाम्—the trees denoting soft timber trees have acute on the first).

1520. The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'modification or part', after a word having anudātta accent on the first syllable.

This debars अण् ॥ Thus बाधित्यम्, कापित्थम् ॥

Note:—The word बाधित्यम् is an upapada-samāsa of बाधे + स् + थ, the स् being changed to ध् as it belongs to Pṛṣodarādi class; and it is finally acute by गदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरः ॥

1521. The affix अञ् comes optionally in the sense of 'modification or part', after the words पलाश &c.

Thus पालाशम् or पालाशम्; so also खादिरम् or खादिरम्; कौरीरम् or कारीरम् ॥

Note:—This sūtra is an example of prāpta and aprāpta vibhāṣā. The words पलाश, खदिर, शिंशपा and स्यन्दन being gravely accented on the first syllable the affix अञ् was obligatory by the last aphorism. This makes it optional and is prāpta-vibhāṣā. In the case of others it is aprāpta-vibhāṣā.

1 पलाश, 2 खदिर, 3 शिंशपा, 4 स्यन्दन (स्पन्दन), 5 पीताक, 6 करीर, 7 शिरीष, 8 यवास, 9 विकङ्कत ॥
entries.note: Corrected misprinted heading number 1621 to 1521.

entries.english:
1522. The affix ‹?› comes in the sense of 'its modification or part', after the word शमी ॥

This debars अण् ॥ Thus शामीलं भस्म; शामीली शुक (IV. 1. 60 S. 515). The feminine is formed by ङीष् as the affix has an indicatory ष् । According to Mādhava the anubandha is ण् and so the feminine is formed in ङीप् ॥
entries.note: Damaged affix text in heading rendered with placeholder.

entries.english:
1523. The affix मयट् comes optionally after any base, in those two meanings of 'product' and 'part', in the classical language, when neither food nor clothing is spoken of.

Thus अश्ममयम्, or आश्मनम् (IV. 3. 134).

Note:—Why do we say भाषायाम् 'in the classical language'? Witness वैल्वः खादिरो वा यूपः स्यात् ॥

Why do we say 'when neither food nor clothing is spoken of'? Observe मौद्गः सूपः 'a soup made of kidney beans'; कार्पासमाच्छादनम् 'cotton dress'.

Note:—Why the word तयोः 'in those two meanings' is used in the sūtra, when by context, the words विकार and अवयव were to be read into the sūtra? Its use indicates that the special affixes, such as taught in IV. 3. 135, 136 &c., are replaced also by मयट् । Thus कापोतमयम् or कापोतम् (IV. 3. 135 S. 1515); लोहमयम् or लौहम् ॥

1524. The affix मयट् comes in the sense of its 'product' or 'part', when neither food nor clothing is spoken of, invariably after Vṛddha words, and after शर &c.

Thus after Vṛddha—आम्रमयम् ॥ After शर &c. words—शरमयम् ॥

Vārt:—The affix मयट् comes invariably after words of one syllable. Thus स्वमयम्, वाङ् मयम् ॥ How do you explain the form आप्यम् 'modification of water' as given by Amarakoṣa (I. 10. 5)? It is formed by ण्यत् added to आपः after the latter had taken अण् of तस्येदम् ॥ अप् + अण् = आप, आप + य = आप्यम् ॥ ण्यत् does not change the meaning.

1 शर, 2 दर्भ, 3 मृद्, 4 कुटी, 5 ‹?›, 6 सोम, 7 बलुब (बल्बज) ॥

1525. The affix मयट् comes after the word गो in the sense of 'its dung'.

Thus गोमयम् 'cow-dung'.

Note:—'Dung' is neither a modification nor a part of cow. Therefore this separate sūtra for गो ॥ Why do we say meaning 'its dung'? Observe गव्यम् = milk. The affix यत् here comes in the sense of product or part (IV. 3. 160 S. 1538), though strictly speaking—milk also is not an 'avayava' or a 'vikāra' of गो ॥

entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page; English text missing.

entries.english: 1526. The affix मयट् invariably comes in the sense of its product or part, after the word पिष्ट ॥ This debars अण् ॥ Thus पिष्टमयं भस्म ॥ Otherwise अण्, as पैष्टी सुरा in the sense of तस्येदम् ॥ (IV. 3. 120 S. 1500) in a general signification.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line was printed at the bottom of the preceding page; entry text on page 814 begins directly with vritti.
entries.sutra_ocr: मयट् स्वाद्विकारे । पिष्टमयं भस्म । कम पैदी सुरेति । सामान्यविवतानां तस्येदमित्यण ॥

entries.english: 1527. The affix कन् comes in the sense of product after the word पिष्ट, the whole word being a Name. This debars मयट् ॥ As पिष्टकः 'cake' (Amarakosha II. 9. 48).
1528. The affix मयट् comes after the word व्रीहि in the sense of a 'Purodāśa.' This debars ‹?› (IV. 3. 136 S. 1516). Thus व्रीहिमयः पुरोडाशः 'sacred cake made of barley'. Otherwise ‹?› ॥
entries.note: Devanagari serial number misprinted as 1520 instead of 1528.

entries.english: 1529. The affix मयट् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after the words 'tila' and 'yava'—the whole not being a name. Thus तिलमयम् । यवमयम् ॥ Why do we say असंज्ञायाम् "it not being a Name"? Observe तैलम् 'oil,' यावकः formed with कन् (यावादिभ्यः कन् V. 4. 29).

1530. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after the words 'tāla &c.'. This debars मयट् &c. Thus तालं धनुः, ‹?›, ऐन्द्रायुधम् ॥ 1 ताल, 2 बर्हिण, 3 इन्द्राविश, 4 इन्द्रावृषा, 5 इन्द्रायुध, 6 बाण (चाप, वर्ग), 7 श्यामक, 8 पीयुक्षा ॥ Vārt:—The affix अण् comes after ताल, when a "bow is meant". Thus तालं धनुः "a bow made of tāla tree". Otherwise तालमयम् ॥ Note:—The words ताल and श्यामक being Vṛiddha words would have taken मयट् (IV. 3. 144 S. 1524). बर्हिणस्य विकारः = बार्हिणम् (by अञ् of IV. 3. 154 S. 1532), then we ought to have added to बार्हिणम् the affix अण् by IV. 3. 155 S. 1533, in the sense of 'product or part'. The present sūtra prevents that. The words इन्द्राविश and इन्द्रावृषा are formed by adding to the roots विश and वृष preceded by the Upapada इन्द्र under Mūla vibhujādi class. The lengthening of the ‹?› of Indra is by अन्येषामपि (VI. 3. 137). The word बाण and पीयुक्षा are acute on the middle. इन्द्रायुध is final acute by samāsa accent.

1531. The affix अण् comes after a word denoting 'gold', when the sense is "a weight or measure". The word जातरूप means 'gold'. It is used in the plural in the sūtra indicating that all words synonymous with gold are to be taken. This debars मयट् &c. Thus हाटकं, तापनीयम्, सौवर्णो वा निष्कः ॥ Why do we say 'meaning a measure'? Observe ‹?› ॥
entries.note: Serial number misread as 1631 in English and misprinted as 1431 in Devanagari; corrected to 1531.

entries.english: 1532. The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after words expressing living beings, and after रजत &c. Note:—This debars ‹?› &c. The affix ‹?› has been ordained to come after those words that have anudātta in the beginning. This sūtra applies to words other than those having anudātta in the beginning. Thus—शौकम्, बाकम्, राजतम्, &c. Note:—In the class रजतादि those words like रजत, कण्टकार &c., which have anudātta on the beginning and would have taken अञ् by IV. 3. 140, S. 1520, have been enumerated to prevent the application of मयट् to them. 1 रजत, 2 सीस, 3 लोह, 4 उदुम्बर, 5 नीप (नीच, नील), 6 वारु, 7 रोहीतक (रोहितक), 8 विभीतक, 9 पीतदारु (कनीत, दारु), 10 त्रिपाद, 11 त्रिकण्टक, 12 कण्टकार ॥
entries.note: Illegible Devanagari fragments in note replaced with placeholder ‹?›.

entries.english: 1533. The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after a word which ends with an affix having an indicatory ञ, such affix denoting 'its product or part'. The affixes having indicatory ञ denoting product or part, are ‹?› (IV. 3. 139), ‹?› (IV. 3. 142), अञ् (IV. 3. 154), वुञ् (IV. 3. 157), ‹?› (IV. 3. 159), ‹?›, यञ् (IV. 3. 168). When a tertiary derivative of a word ending with these affixes is to be made the affix अञ् is used. This debars मयट् ॥ Thus शामीलम्, दाधिरथम्, कापित्थम् &c. Why do we say ञितः? Observe बैल्वमयम् ॥ Here मयट् is used after बिल्व and the derivative is formed by अण् of IV. 3. 136, S. 1516. So also पैप्पलम् ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari affixes and examples restored from vritti context; heavily garbled fragments represented with ‹?›.

entries.english: 1534. After a word denoting 'a measure', the affix expressing 'its product or part', is the same as the affix having the sense of 'purchased'. The affixes taught in V. 1. 18 &c. S. 1548 &c. are the affixes that have the force of क्रीत (V. 1. 37). These affixes come also after words denoting measure (V. 1. 19). The same affixes are employed to denote विकार, after words denoting परिमाण ॥ This debars अण् &c. Thus निष्केन क्रीतं = नैष्किकम् (V. 1. 20). It will denote विकार also, निष्कस्य विकारो नैष्किकः formed by ठञ् (V. 1. 20). As शतेन क्रीतः = शत्यः or शतिकः (V. 1. 21), so शतस्य विकारः शत्यः or शतिकः by कन् and यत् (V. 1. 21). Note:—The word वत् in क्रीतवत् indicates that the similarity is complete throughout. Thus sūtra V. 1. 28 also applies by which the affix is elided. As द्विसहस्रः or द्विसाहस्रः (V. 1. 29), द्विनिष्कः or द्विनैष्किकः ॥ The word परिमाण in this sūtra includes संख्या 'the numerals' also while the technical word परिमाण does not include saṅkhyā. See IV. 1. 22 and V. 1. 19 &c. The similarity extends even to the elision of the affix (V. 1. 28) as, द्विनिष्कः, द्विनैष्किकः &c.
1535. The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after the word 'ushtra'. This debars अञ् (IV. 3. 154). उष्ट्रस्य विकारोऽवयवो वा = औष्ट्रकः ॥
entries.note: Heading number 535 corrected to 1535.

entries.english: 1536. The affix वुञ् comes optionally in the sense

of its product or part', after the words उमा and ऊर्णा ॥
Thus औमम् or औमकम्, और्णम् or और्णकम् ॥
Note:—Uma has acute on the first syllable by ‹?› (Phit II. 4). Urna is naturally acute, as a Pratipadika.

1537. The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after the feminine word एणी ॥
This debars अञ् of IV. 3. 154 S. 1532.
Thus ऐणेयं मांसम् 'the flesh of a female black deer'. But एणस्य मांसम् = ऐणम् the flesh of a male deer, formed by अण् ॥

1538. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'its product or part', after the words गो and पयस् ॥
Thus गव्यम्, पयस्यम् (VI. 1. 79 S. 63).

1539. The affix यत् comes in the sense of its product or part, after the word 'dru' (meaning "a tree").
This debars अञ् (IV. 3. 139). Thus द्रु + य = द्रव्यम् (VI. 1. 79 S. 63).

1540. The affix वयच् comes in the sense of 'its product', after the word 'dru', the word meaning 'a measure'.
This debars यत् ॥ As द्रुवयम् 'a measure'. The words कुडवम्, शूर्प and द्रोण are three words denoting measure. (Amarakosha II. 9. 85).

1541. The affix denoting 'product or part' is elided by luk, when such product or part is 'a fruit.'
Thus आमलक्याः फलम् = आमलकी + मयट् = आमलकम् 'the fruit of Myrobolans'.
Note:—The fruit is a "product" as well as "part" of a fruit-bearing tree.

1542. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'its product or part, it being a fruit,' after the word 'plaksha &c.'
This debars अञ् ॥ Thus प्लाक्षम् ॥ So also नैयग्रोधम् by the following Sûtra.
1 प्लक्ष 2 न्यग्रोध 3 अश्वत्थ 4 इङ्गुदी, 5 शिरीष, 6 रुरु, 7 कर्कन्धु (कर्कन्धू, कर्कन्धु, पर्करू) 8 बृहती ॥

1543. ऐच् is placed before the य् of न्यग्रोध, instead of Vriddhi, when the word stands alone, and is not a member of a compound, and is followed by a Taddhita affix with the indicatory ञ्, ण् or क् ॥
As नैयग्रोधम् (= न्यग्रोधस्य विकारः) ॥
Note:—Why do we say 'when it is alone'? Observe न्यग्रोधमूले भवाः शालयः = न्यग्रोधमूलाः ॥ If न्यग्रोध is a derivative word (from न्यङ् रोहति = नीचेर्गत्वारोहेर्वर्धते), then it would have been governed by VII. 3. 8, this separate sutra is then for the sake of making a restrictive rule (niyama) with regard to this word. If it is a primary word, then this sûtra makes a Vidhi rule. The word केवल is a jñâpaka that the rule of Tadâdi applies to this section. See VII. 3. 8, also.

1544. The affix अण् comes optionally in denoting a fruit, after the word 'jambu'.
This debars अञ् ॥ Thus जम्बू + अण् = जाम्बवम् as जाम्बवानि फलानि ॥ But when the general affix is added, it is elided by IV. 3. 163. S. 1541. As जम्बु + अञ् (IV. 3. 139) = जम्बु, as जम्बूनि फलानि (VI. 4. 8).
entries.note: English heading misprinted serial number as 1644; corrected to 1544 per sequence.

entries.english:
1545. The affix denoting fruit is optionally elided by lup after the word 'jambu'.
The word वा is understood here. The difference between 'luk' and 'lup' elision is that in the case of 'lup', there is concordance of gender and number. See sûtra I. 2. 51 S. 1294. Thus जम्बू + अञ् लुप् = जम्बू, as, जम्बू फलं ॥
Optionally जम्ब्वाः फलं = जम्बु फलं, or जाम्बवं ॥
Vart:—There is lup elision of the affix denoting fruit, after the words expressing deciduous plants which wither away as soon as the fruit ripens. Thus व्रीहिः — व्रीहयः, मुद्गाः ॥
Vart:—Diversely so when the affix denotes flowers and roots: as, मल्लिकायाः पुष्पं मल्लिका, नवमल्लिका, जातिः ; so also विदार्या मूलं = विदारी । अंशुमती । बृहती ॥
In the above example there is concordance. By using 'diversely', this concordance does not sometime take place. As पाटलानि पुष्पाणि, मूलानि ॥ So ‹?›, करवीरम्, &c.

1546. The affix denoting 'fruit' is elided by लुप्, after the words 'Harîtakî' &c.
Here also there is concordance (I. 2. 51 S. 1294). As हरीतक्याः फलं = हरीतकी instead of हारीतकम् ॥ So also कोशातकी, नखरजनी ॥ According to Patanjali, the concordance is with regard to gender only, the number will be governed by the sense, as हरीतकी फलं, हरीतक्यः फलानि ॥
1. हरीतकी, 2 कोशातकी, 3 नखरजनी (नखरञ्जनी), 4 शष्कण्डी (शाकण्डी), 5 द्राक्षा, 6 सौवीर, 7 श्वेतपाकी, 8 अर्जुनपाकी, 9 द्राक्षा, 10 काला, 11 काचा (काकाक्षा), 12 गर्भीका (गर्भरीका), 13 कण्टकारिका, 14 पिप्पली, 15 चिञ्चा (चिम्पा), 16 तालिसा, 17 ‹?› ॥

1547. The affixes यञ् and अञ् come respectively in the sense of 'its product', after the words 'kaṁsîya' and 'paraśavya', and there is luk-elision (of the छ and यत् affixes of those words).
The word कंसीयः is formed by छ (V. 1. ‹?›) and परशव्य is formed by adding यत् (V. 1. 2). These affixes छ and यत् are elided when the affixes
entries.note: English heading misprinted serial number as 1847; corrected to 1547 per sequence; entry text cut off at end of page.

entries.english:
and भ are added. Thus कांस्य + यञ् = कंस + यम् = कांस्य so also पाराव from परशव्य ; thus परशव्य अण् - परशु + अ = पाराव ॥
Here ends the chapter on Pragdivyatiya affixes.
entries.note: Tail fragment of SK 1547 continuing from previous page and concluding Chapter XXIX.

entries.english:
1548. The affix ठक् comes as a governing affix, in the senses enumerated hereafter up to sûtra IV. 4. 76. S. 1627.
Note :—This is an adhikara sutra. The affix ठक् bears rule from this one forward to the sûtra तद्वहति...
Vart :— After the words माशब्द &c., the affix 'thak' comes in the sense 'he said that'. Thus माशब्द इत्याह = माशब्दिकः 'who says don't make noise', कार्यशब्दिकः ॥ This is the case of an affix added to a sentence.
Note :— Thus in the next sûtra it is said: "After a word in the third case in construction, in the sense of 'who plays, digs, conquers, or is conquered.'" Now this sûtra is incomplete. We must read the word ठक् into it. Thus अक्षैर्दीव्यति = आक्षिकः "who plays with aksha—a dicer" अक्ष + ठक् = आक्षिकः (VII. 3. 50, S. 1176).

1549. The prohibition and augment taught in VII. 3. 3. S. 1098, do not apply also to स्वागता &c.
As स्वागतिकः (= स्वागतमित्याह), स्वाध्वरिकः (= स्वध्वरेण चरति), स्वाङ्गिः, व्याङ्गिः, व्याडिः (sons of Svanga, Vyanga and Vyada), व्यावहारिकः (Vyavaharena charati) and स्वापतेयम् (= स्वपतौ साधु) ॥ The word व्यवहार does not mean reciprocity of action for then it would have been governed by VII. 3. 2. S. 1144. स्वपति being a compound with स्व, would have been governed by VII. 3. 4. S. 1386 as it is included in the Dvyachadi list, hence its specific mention here. The following is the list of svâgatâdi words:
1 स्वागत, 2 स्वध्वर, 3 स्वङ्ग, 4 व्यङ्ग, 5 व्यड, 6 व्यवहार, 7 स्वपति ॥
Vart :— So also after प्रभूत &c. in the sense 'he said' as प्रभूतमाह = प्राभूतिकः, पार्याप्तिकः ॥ These are examples of affixes added to an adverb.
Vart. So also after सुस्नात &c. in the sense 'he asks', as, सुस्नातं पृच्छति = सौस्नातिकः "Who asks, have you bathed well?", सौखरात्रिकः, सौखशायनिकः ॥
Vart. So also after परदारा &c. in the sense of 'he goes to, or commits adultery with', as परदारान् गच्छति = पारदारिकः, गौतल्पिकः ॥ The word तल्प here refers to "wife".
entries.note: Corrected heading number 1649 to sequential 1549; repaired misread text.

entries.english:
1550. The affix ठक् comes after a word in the third case in construction, in the sense of, 'he plays', 'he digs', 'he conquers' or 'he is conquered'.
Thus अक्षैर्दीव्यति = आक्षिकः 'who plays with dice—a dicer'. अभ्र्या खनति = आभ्रिकः, कौद्दालिकः, अक्षैर्जयति = आक्षिकः, अक्षैर्जितम् = आक्षिकम् ॥

1551. The affix ठक् comes after a word in the third case in construction, in the sense of 'refined thereby'.
The word संस्कृतम् means 'refining or enhancing the quality of a thing'. Thus दध्ना संस्कृतं = दाधिकम् 'refined or made tasteful by curd'. मारीचिकम् ॥
Note :—The separation of this sûtra from the last, is for the sake of the next sûtra, in which the anuvritti of संस्कृतं only runs.
entries.note: Corrected heading number 1561 to 1551.

entries.english:
1552. After the word 'kulattha', and after words having a penultimate क, the affix अण् is added in the sense of 'refined or prepared therewith'.
This debars ठक् ॥ Thus कौलत्थम्, तैत्तिडीकम्, the two latter being examples of words ending in क ॥
1553. The affix ठक् comes after a word in the third
entries.note: Partial entry cut off at the bottom of page 822; heading number misprinted/misread as 1653.

entries.english:
case in construction, in the sense of 'he crosses thereby over the waters '.
Thus काण्डप्लवेन तरति = काण्डप्लविकः, ‹?› 'who crosses with a raft '.

1554. The affix ठञ् comes after the word 'gopuchchha', in the sense of 'he crosses thereby'.
The difference between ‹?› and ‹?› is in the accent. Thus ‹?›
entries.note: Devanagari text in commentary heavily corrupted in scan; affix emended to ठञ् from sutra.

entries.english:
1555. The affix ठन् comes after the word नौ and after bases having two syllables, in the sense of 'he crosses therewith'.
This debars ठक् ॥ Thus नावा तरति = नाविका 'a sailor'. So also after dissyllabic words as, घटिकः, so also बाहुका (बाहुभ्यां तरति) in the feminine.
Note:—The न् in ठन् in the sutra is not part of the affix, but comes through Sandhi rules, the feminine of बाहुकः being बाहुका ॥ In fact the indicatory ष् occurs in the Fourth book, in sutras IV. 4. 9, 10, 18, 53 and 74.
entries.note: English heading misprinted as 1556 in source, corrected to 1555 to follow strict sequence; panini ref corrected from IV.4.17 to 4.4.7.

entries.english:
1556. After a word in the third case in construction, comes the affix ठक् in the sense of 'he goes on by means thereof'.
The word चरति means both to go on and to eat. Thus शाकटिकः, हास्तिकः 'who travels by a car or an elephant', दध्ना भक्षयति = दाधिकः 'who gets on, with being fed on curd'.
entries.note: SK number misprinted in sutra line as १४५६.

entries.english:
1557. The affix ठन् comes in the sense of 'he goes on, by means thereof' after the word 'akarsha'.
Note:—This debars ठक् ॥ The ष् is for accent (VI. 1. 193). The न् of ठन् here is a part of the affix contrary to what it was in IV. 4. 7 (1555).
Thus आकर्षेण चरति = आकर्षिकः, आकर्षिके, आकर्षिकी ॥ आकर्ष is a touch-stone by which gold is tested. Another reading is आकर्षाय ॥

1558. The affix ष्ठन् comes, in the sense of 'he goes on, by means thereof' after the words 'parpa' &c.
This debars ठक्, the न् of ष्ठन् is for accent (VI. 1. 197), and ष् for ङीष् (IV. 1. 41). Thus पार्षिकः, पार्षिकी, आश्विकः, आश्विकी ॥ So also ‹?› ॥
1 पर्प, 2 अश्व, 3 अश्वत्थ, 4 रथ, 5 जान, 6 व्यास, 7 व्याल, 8 पाद, 9 पत्र ॥
entries.note: Heading misprinted as 1568 in source, corrected to 1558.

entries.english:
1559. The affix ठञ् as well as the affix ष्ठन् comes after the word श्वगण, in the sense of 'he goes on by means thereof'.
This debars ठक् ॥

1560. A compound beginning with श्वन्, and followed by the Taddhita affix इञ् is not governed by the prohibition, nor takes the augment, taught in VII. 3. 4.
Thus the descendant of श्वभस्त्र is श्वाभस्त्रिः, so also श्वावष्टिः ॥ The word श्वन् is included in the list of Dvaradi words VII. 3. 4, (1386). The present sutra implies that the rule VII. 3. 4 applies not only to those words, but to compounds beginning with those words.
Vart:—This rule applies when any Taddhita affix beginning with इ follows.
Thus श्वगणेन चरति = श्वागणिकः 'who lives by dogs', f. श्वागणिकी ॥ ष्ठन् = श्वगणिकः, श्वगणिकी ॥
Note:—The form श्वागणिकः is evolved by the breach of rule VII. 3. 3. Thus श्वगण + ठञ् ॥ Here by VII. 2. 117, ञ requires the Vriddhi of the अ of श्व ॥ But rule VII. 3. 4 says that instead of Vriddhi, the letter औ comes before अ in the case of श्व &c. The proper form, therefore, would have been शौवगणिकः ॥ The irregularity is, however, explained by saying that the prohibition contained in VII. 3. 4 which applies when श्व is followed by इञ्, applies also to श्व followed by ठञ् ॥ In fact, the rule VII. 3. 4 does not apply, whenever the word श्व is followed by an affix beginning with the letter इ ॥
The prohibition applies, when other Taddhita affixes follow such a word ending with इ (an affix beginning with इ) as from श्वाभास्त्र we have श्वाभास्त्रायण (श्वाभस्त्रेरपत्यम्) ॥
entries.note: Text spans across page break 824-825.

entries.english:
1561. The rule VII. 3. 4 is optionally applied to श्वन् followed by पद ॥
As श्वापदस्य भावः श्वापदम् or शौवपदम् ॥

1562. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'he lives thereby', after the words 'vetana &c.', being in the third case in construction.
Thus वेतनेन जीवति वैतनिकः 'who lives upon wages—a menial servant'.
In the case of the word धनुर्दण्ड the affix applies to the compound, as well as to the words forming the compound. Thus धानुर्दण्डिकः, धानुष्कः, दाण्डिकः ॥
1 वेतन, 2 वाहन (वाह), 3 अर्धवाहन (अर्धवाह), 4 धनुर्दण्ड, 5 जाल, 6 वेश (वेस), 7 उपवेष (उपवेस), 8 मेषण, 9 उपबस्ति (उपस्ति), 10 सुख, 11 शय्या, 12 शक्ति, 13 उपनिषद्, 14 उपवेश, 15 स्फिज् (स्फिज्), 16 पाद, 17 उपस्थ, 18 उपस्थान, 19 उपहस्त, 20 राजन् ॥

1563. The affix ठन् comes in the sense of 'he lives thereby' after the words 'vasna', 'kraya' and 'vikraya', being in the 3rd case in construction.
This debars ठक् ॥ Thus वस्नेन जीवति = वास्निकः 'who lives by hire, hireling'. In the case of क्रय and विक्रय the affix is applied to the words separately, as well as to their compound. Thus क्रयविक्रयिकः, क्रयिकः, विक्रयिकः 'a trader'.
1564. The affix ढञ् as well as ठन् comes in the sense of 'he lives thereby', after the word 'Ayudha'.
entries.note: Heading misprinted as 1064 in source, corrected to 1564. Text cuts off at bottom of page.

entries.english: Thus आयुधेन जीवति = आयुधीयः (formed by छ), or आयुधिकः (by ठक्) 'a mercenary soldier'.

1565. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'he conveys thereby', after the words utsanga &c. being in the third case in construction.
The word हृ means 'to take away to or cause to reach another place'. Thus औत्सङ्गिकः 'borne upon the hip'.
1 उत्सङ्ग, 2 उडुप, 3 उत्पत (उत्पस), 4 उत्पुट, 5 पिटक, 6 पिटाक, 7 गलप ॥

1566. The affix ष्ठन् comes, in the sense of 'he conveys', after the words 'bhastrâ &c.' being in the third case in construction.
Thus भस्त्रया हरति = भास्त्रिकः "who conveys by means of a leathern bag, a carrier". The feminine will be भास्त्रिकी (IV. 1. 41).
Note:—The word भस्त्रा means a pair of leathern bellows by which the iron is heated, or a leathern bag in which grain &c. is carried.
1 भस्त्रा, 2 भरट, 3 भरण (भारण), 4 शीर्षभार, 5 शीर्षभार, 6 अंसभार, 7 अंसेभार ॥
entries.note: English heading misprinted as 1666; corrected to 1566.
entries.sutra_ocr: १५६६ भस्त्रादिभ्यः ष्ठन् । ४ । ४ । १६ ॥ भस्त्रया हरति भास्त्रिकः । षित्त्वान् ङीष् । भास्त्रिकी ॥

entries.english:
1567. The affix ष्ठन् comes optionally in the sense of 'he conveys', after the words 'vivadha' (and 'vîvadha'), being in the third case in construction.
Vart:—A word altered in a portion thereof remains the same. Therefore वीवध is also governed by this sutra.
In the alternative, the general affix ठक् will apply. Thus विवधेन हरति = वैवधिकः, वैवधिकी. So also वीवधिकः, वीवधिकी. When the affix is ठक्, we have वैवधिकः in both cases, the feminine being वैवधिकी.
The words विवध and वीवध are synonyms both meaning 'a piece of wood with a loop at each end placed on the shoulders to carry loads, on the road'; विवधिकः meaning 'a carrier of loads, a pedler'.
entries.sutra_ocr: १५६७ । विभाषा विवधात् । ४ । ४ । १७ ॥ विवधेन हरति वैवधिकः । पक्षे । वैवधिकः । एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वाद्वीवधादपीष्टम् । वीवधिकः । वीवधिकी । विवधवीवधशब्दौ उभयतो बद्धशिक्ये स्कन्धवाह्ये काष्ठे वर्तेते ॥

entries.english:
1568. The affix ठक् comes, in the sense of 'he conveys', after the word कुटिलिका in the third case in construction.
Thus कुटिलिकया हरति मृगान् व्याधः or (मृगो व्याधम्) कौटिलिको व्याधः (or मृगः) 'a deer which carries (or entices away) into crooked ways' or 'a hunter who hunts by coming stealthily on his prey'. कुटिलिकया हरति अङ्गारान् = कौटिलिकः कर्मारः 'a blacksmith, who carries burning coals on an iron forge'.
The word कुटिलिका means 'crooked motion, and the iron-forge of the blacksmiths'.
entries.note: English heading misprinted as 1668; corrected to 1568.
entries.sutra_ocr: १५६८ । कुटिलिकायाः । ४ । ४ । १८ ॥ कुटिलिका व्याधानां गतिविशेषः कर्मारोपकरणभूतं लोहभाण्डं च । कुटिलिकया हरति मृगानङ्गारान्वा कौटिलिको व्याधः कर्मारो वा ॥

entries.english:
1569. The affix ठक् comes, in the sense of 'completed thereby' after the words 'akshadyûta &c.', being in the third case in construction.
Thus अक्षद्यूतेन निर्वृत्तम् = आक्षद्यूतिकं वैरम् 'enmity which was growing but has been completed by gambling'.
1 अक्षद्यूत, 2 जानुप्रहृत (प्रहत), 3 जङ्घाप्रहृत (प्रहत), 4 अङ्घाप्रहृत, 5 पादस्वेदन, 6 कण्टकमर्दन, 7 गतानुगत, 8 गतागत, 9 यातापिपात, 10 अनुगत ॥

1570. The affix मप् comes invariably after the words ending in the affix त्रि, in the sense of 'completed thereby'.
The त्रि here refers to the affix 'ktri' (III. 3. 88). Thus the root पच् takes क्त्रि and forms पक्ति, which is not a complete word, but must take the augment मप् to form a full word. Thus पच् + क्त्रि + मप् = पक्त्रिमम् 'what is completed by being cooked'. From डुकृञ् we have कृत्रिमम्.
Note:—The word नित्यम् in the sutra indicates that the affix क्त्रि never comes singly by itself; all words ending in 'ktri' are invariably followed by मप् also. In fact मप् may be regarded as an invariable augment of the affix 'ktri'.
Vart:—After a word ending in an affix denoting 'condition' the affix मप् is added. Thus पाकेन निर्वृत्तम् = पाकिमम् (पच् + III. 3. 18 + इमप्). So also त्यागिमम्, सेकिमम्, कुट्टिमम् ॥
entries.sutra_ocr: १५७० । त्रेर्मन्नित्यम् । ४ । ४ । २० ॥ त्र्यन्तप्रकृतिकान्तृतीयान्तान्निर्वृत्तेऽर्थे मप् स्यान्नित्यम् । कृत्या निर्वृत्तं कृत्रिमम् । पक्त्रिमम् ॥ भावप्रत्ययान्तादिमब् वक्तव्यः । पाकेन निर्वृत्तं पाकिमम् । त्यागिमम् ॥

entries.english:
1571. The affixes 'kak' and 'kan' come respectively after the words 'apamitya' and 'yâchita,' when the sense is that of completion.
Thus आपमित्यकम् 'debt', and याचितकम् 'a thing begged for use'.
Note:—The word अपमित्य is formed from the root मा with the prefix अप, and the suffix क्त्वा (III. 4. 19). The क्त्वा is changed to ल्यप्, and त substituted for मा (VI. 4. 70). The word is an Indeclinable, and therefore the anuvritti of तेन does not run here.
entries.sutra_ocr: १५७१ । अपमित्ययाचिताभ्यां कक्कनौ । ४ । ४ । २१ ॥ अपमित्येति ल्यबन्तम् । अपमित्य निर्वृत्तमापमित्यकम् । याचितेन निर्वृत्तं याचितकम् ॥

entries.english:
1572. The affix ठक् comes, after a word in the third case in construction, when the sense is 'mixed therewith'.
The word तेन is understood here. The word संसृष्ट means unification, mixing &c. Thus दध्ना संसृष्टम् = दाधिकम् 'smeared with curd'.
Note:—The word 'sanskritam' (IV. 4. 3) and 'sansrishtam' should be distinguished. The former refers to a case where by the combination of two things, something better is produced; no such idea of bettering is to be found in संसृष्ट.

1573. The affix इनि comes after the word 'chûrṇa' when the sense is 'mixed therewith'.
This debars ठक्. Thus चूर्णैः संसृष्टा = चूर्णिनी पूपाः 'cakes sprinkled with powder'.

1574. The affix ठक् meaning 'mixed therewith', is elided by luk, after the word 'lavaṇa'.
Thus लवणेन संसृष्टः = लवणः 'mixed with salt', as लवणः सूपः 'soup mixed with salt'. So लवणं शाकम्, लवणा यवागूः (I. 151).
Note:—The लुक् elision takes place when the word लवण is used as a noun, and not as an adjective.
entries.sutra_ocr: १५७४ । लवणाल्लुक् । ४ । ४ । २४ ॥ लवणेन संसृष्टो लवणः सूपः । लवणं शाकम् ॥

entries.english:
1575. The affix aṇ comes after the word 'mudga', when the sense is 'mixed therewith.'

ठक् ॥ This debars ṭhak. 'Rice mixed with mudga pulse'.
entries.note: Sutra line was at the bottom of the previous page; page 829 begins with vritti fragment 'माद्गो भक्तः' misread as 'माज भावनः ।' before heading 1575.

entries.english:
1576. The affix comes, after a word denoting a condiment, being in the third case in construction, when the sense is 'sprinkled therewith.'

Thus दध्नोपसिक्तं दाधिकम् 'sprinkled with curd.'

Note:—Why do we say 'denoting a condiment'? Observe ‹?›.
entries.note: Devanagari examples in body and Note were heavily distorted by OCR.

entries.english:
1577. The affix comes in the sense of 'it exists', after the words 'ojas', 'sahas', and 'ambhas' being in the third case in construction.

Thus ओजसा वर्तते = औजसिकः शूरः 'a hero' lit. possessed with energy.

So also:—साहसिकः 'a thief', आम्भसिकः 'a fish'.

1578. The affix comes, in the sense of 'it exists,' after 'îpa,' 'loma,' and 'kula,' preceded by 'anu' and 'prati,' the word being in the second case in construction.

The word ‹?› shows that the words must be in the second case in construction. The verb is intransitive, how can it take an object, and how can it be in construction with an objective case? The words in the accusative after the verb are not its objects, but are used as adverbs qualifying the sense of the verb, and adverbs are always put in the accusative case. Thus प्रतीपं वर्तते = प्रातीपिकः (प्रतिगता आपोऽस्मिन्, the ‹?› changed to ई V. 4. 74 and VI. 3. 97), 'retrograde, i. e., which is unfavourable.' So ‹?› 'favourable.' प्रातिलोमिकः 'diverse', आनुलोमिकः 'direct', प्रातिकूलिकः, आनुकूलिकः ॥

The two words ‹?› and ‹?› mean 'unfavourable' and 'favourable' respectively.
entries.note: Several embedded Devanagari words dropped or garbled by OCR in prose commentary.

entries.english:
1579. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'it exists,' after the word 'parimukha,' being in the second case in construction.
Thus परिमुखं वर्तते = पारिमुखिकः 'being before the face,' 'being near or present.'
The word च in the sutra implies that the affix applies to other words also not mentioned. As पारिपार्श्विकः ॥
Note:—The word परिमुख is an Avyayibhava compound (II. 1. 12). If परि has the force of exclusion (I. 4. 88), then पारिमुखिक will mean a servant who always avoids the face of his master "स्वामिनो मुखं वर्जयित्वा यः सेवको वर्त्तते" and if परि means 'all round,' then the word will mean "a servant who is always in the presence of his master — यतः स्वामिनो मुखं ततस्ततो वर्त्तते" ॥

1580. The affix ठक् comes after a word in the second case in construction, when the sense is 'he gives', the motive being mean.
Thus द्विगुणं प्रयच्छति द्वैगुणिकः 'a usurer who gives for the sake of double, i. e. who charges cent per cent interest.' The word द्विगुण means द्विगुणार्थ 'for the sake of double.' Similarly त्रैगुणिकः ॥
Vart:—The word वृद्धि is changed to वार्धुषि before this affix. As, वृद्धिं प्रयच्छति — वार्धुषिकः, 'a usurer' 'who gives for the sake of increase'. Or the word वार्धुषि may be taken as a separate word synonymous with वृद्धि ॥
Note:—Why do we say गर्ह्यम् 'with a mean motive'? Observe द्विगुणं प्रयच्छति अधमर्णः 'the debtor gives double'.
entries.note: Reconstructed heavily mangled embedded Devanagari from English explanations and commentary context.

entries.english: 1581. The affixes ष्टन् and ष्टच् come respectively after the words 'kusida' and 'dasaikadasa', when the sense is 'he gives for a mean motive',
entries.note: Entry text is cut off at the bottom of the page.

entries.english: The word कुसीद means 'interest'. The lending of ten (दश) on a condition that the borrower will pay eleven (एकादश) after a month is called ‹?›. The difference between the two affixes ‹?› is in the accent (VI. 1. 197 and 163). Thus ‹?› and ‹?›. This sûtra debars ‹?› fem. ‹?› (IV. 1. 41). So ‹?› : fem. ‹?›.
entries.note: Tail fragment of SK 1581 continuing from previous page; embedded Devanagari partially reconstructed and partially replaced with placeholder.

entries.english:
1582. The affix comes after a word in the second case in construction, when the sense is 'who gleans that'.
Thus बदराण्युञ्छति = बादरिकः 'who picks up jujubes'.
Note:—To pick up every grain (कण) fallen on the ground is called उञ्छनम् ।
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari reconstructed from context and clear Sanskrit vritti.

entries.english:
1583. The affix comes after a word in the second case in construction, when the sense is 'he aids or protects that'.
Thus समाजं रक्षति = सामाजिकः 'a spectator', lit. 'who aids an assembly by his presence'.
entries.note: Panini reference digits misprinted/garbled in OCR as ४ ४ १३४; embedded Devanagari restored from printed vritti line.

entries.english:
1584. The affix comes after the words 'Śabda' and 'dardura', being in the second case in construction, when the sense is 'who makes a sound or a croaking'.
Thus शब्दं करोति = शाब्दिकः 'who makes words' i.e. a grammarian.
So दार्दुरिकः 'who makes a croaking noise like a frog (dardura)' i.e. a potter.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari forms restored from the printed Sanskrit vritti line.

entries.english:
1585. The affix comes after the words in the second case in construction denoting birds, fishes, or wild beasts, when the sense is 'who kills that'.
Thus पक्षिणो हन्ति = पाक्षिकः 'a bird-killer'. The affix applies not only to the word-forms &c., but to words denoting birds &c. (See I. 1. 68).
entries.note: Entry text cuts off at bottom of page (continued on next page).

entries.english: Therefore, we have forms आधुनिकः, मारिकः ॥ So also with मत्स्य, as, मात्स्यिकः, मैनिकः, शाकुलिकः ॥ So also with मृग, as, मार्गिकः, हारिणिकः, सारिकः ॥

1586. The affix ठक् comes also in the sense of "who stays", after the word 'paripantham', the word being in the second case in construction.

Thus परिपन्थं तिष्ठति = पारिपन्थिकः वा पन्थानं वर्जयित्वा तिष्ठति, यो वा पन्थानं व्याप्य तिष्ठति a thief lit. 'who stays at roads, a high way man'.

Note:— The च in the sutra indicates that the sense of हन्ति 'who kills' of the last, is to be connected with this sûtra by the conjunction 'and'. Thus परिपन्थं हन्ति पारिपन्थिकः ॥

The phrase 'being in the second case in construction' is understood in this sutra, why has then the word परिपन्थम् been shown in the second case in the sûtra, for it is a mere superfluity? No, it shows the classical form of the word. The word परिपन्थ is synonymous with परिपन्थिन्, the latter, however, having other senses also.
entries.note: SK number misprinted as १४८० in sutra line; Panini ref read as 4.4.31 from printed digits.

entries.english:
1587. The affix ठक् comes, in the sense of "who runs", after a word having माथ as its second term, and after the words 'padavî' and 'anupada'.

Thus a road (mâtha) straight like a stick (daṇḍa) is called दण्डमाथः । From it दण्डमाथं धावति = दाण्डमाथिकः 'who runs on a high way'. Similarly पादविकः, आनूपदिकः ॥ The word माथ means 'a way'.

1588. The affix ठञ् as well as ठक् comes after the word 'âkranda', being in the second case in construction, in the sense of 'who runs'.

The word आक्रन्द means 'a place where persons weep' e.g. a battle-field, it also means 'weeping, invoking' &c. The difference between ठक् and ठञ् is in the accent. Thus आक्रन्दं धावति = आक्रन्दिकः or आक्रान्दिकः, आक्रान्दिकी 'a person who runs to a place where cries of distress are heard'.
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1688; sutra number misprinted as १५६८.

entries.english:
1589. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who takes', after a word having 'pada' as its second member, the word being in the second case in construction.

Thus पूर्वपदं गृह्णाति = पौर्वपदिकः, so also श्रौत्तरपदिकः ॥

Note:— The word उत्तरपद is used in order to prevent the application of the rule, when पद is preceded by the affix बहु ॥
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1689; sutra number misprinted as १५८८; Panini ref printed as 4.4.36.

entries.english:
1590. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who takes' after the words 'pratikaṇṭha', 'artha', and 'lalâma' being in the second case in construction.

Thus प्रतिकण्ठं गृह्णाति प्रातिकण्ठिकः ॥ So also आर्थिकः, लालामिकः ॥

Note:— The word प्रतिकण्ठ here is an Avyayîbhâva meaning कण्ठं कण्ठं प्रति, and not प्रतिगतः कण्ठं = प्रतिकण्ठः, for to the latter no affix is added.
entries.note: Sutra SK number misprinted as १४९०.

entries.english:
1591. The affix ठक् comes after the word 'dharma', being in the second case in construction, in the sense of 'who practises that'.

Thus धर्मं चरति = धार्मिकः "religious".

Vârtika:— It must be stated that the affix ठक् comes after adharma also. As आधर्मिकः "irreligious, undutiful".
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1691; sutra number misprinted as १५६१.

entries.english:
1592. The affix ठन् as well as ठक् comes after the word 'prati-patham', in the second case in construction, in the sense of 'who goes.'

Thus प्रतिपथमेति = प्रातिपन्थिकः or प्रातिपथिकः "who goes along the road"; the ञ् causes Vṛiddhi (VII. 2. 118) whilst ठ does not.
entries.note: Sutra SK number misprinted as १५६२.

entries.english:
1593. The affix comes after words in the second case in construction, denoting combination, in the sense of 'who assembles there.'

Thus समवायं समवैति = सामवायिकः 'who assembles in an assembly'. So also सामाजिकः, सामूहिकः, सान्निवेशिकः ॥

Note:— The word समवाय means combination, collection &c. The word समवायान् is in the plural number in the sutra, indicating that the svarûpa-vidhi (I. 1. 68) does not apply; the affix being applied not only to the word-form समवाय but to its synonyms also. समवैति means coming together.

1594. The affix ण्य comes after the word 'parishad', in the sense of 'who assembles there'.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus परिषदं समवैति = पारिषद्यः 'one present in a council, an assessor, a councillor'.

1595. The affix ण्य comes optionally in the sense of 'who assembles there,' after the word senâ.

This debars ठक् which comes in the alternative. Thus सेनां समवैति = सैन्यः or सैनिकः 'a soldier, a member of an army'.
entries.note: Heading number misprinted as 1195; sutra number misprinted as १५६५.

entries.english:
1596. The affix comes in the sense of 'who sees that,' after the words 'lalâṭa' and 'kukkuṭî', in the second case in construction, the whole word being a Name.

Thus ललाटं पश्यति = ललाटिकः 'a non-attentive servant lit. who always looks at the fore-head of his master from a distance, keeps himself aloof, does not come near to perform any work.' So also कौक्कुटिकः 'a religious mendicant, a Bhikshu.' The space of ground over which a hen can fly without falling, is to be understood here by the word कुक्कुटी ॥ In other words, a small space of ground, for hens cannot sustain their flight for a long distance. Therefore, owing to the smallness of space, the mendicant walks looking down over the
ground, and hence he is called कोक्कुटिक । The word also means 'a hypocrite with down-cast eyes.'

1597. The affix ठञ् comes after a word in the sixth case in construction, in the sense of 'its usage'.

The word धर्म्य means 'usual,' 'relating to custom'. The word तस्य shows the case of the word. Thus शुल्कशालाया धर्म्यम् = शौल्कशालिकः 'the custom-house laws or usages.' So also आकरिकम्, आपणिकम्, गौल्मिकम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed garbled Devanagari in custom-house example.

entries.english:
1598. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'its law', after the word 'mahiṣī' &c.

This debars ठक्. Thus महिष्या धर्म्यम् = माहिषम् 'the usages of queens.' So याजमानम् ॥

1 महिषी, 2 प्रजापति, 3 प्रजावति, 4 प्रलेविका, 5 विलेपिका, 6 अनुलेपिका, 7 पुरोहित, 8 मणिपाली, 9 अनुचारक (अनुवारक), 10 होतृ, 11 यजमान ॥

1599. The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'its law', after a nominal-stem ending in ॠ.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus यातुर्धर्म्यम् = यात्रम् 'the office of a Yātri, i.e. a pilgrim'.

Vart:— So also after the word नर. As नरस्य धर्म्या नारी ॥

Vart:— So also after the word विवासितृ, the णि affix being elided. Thus विवासितृ + अञ् = वैवासित्रम् ॥

Vart:— So also after the word विभाजयितृ, its णि affix also being elided. Thus विभाजयितृ + अञ् = वैभाजित्रम् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed garbled Devanagari in vartikas and examples.

entries.english:
1600. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'its tax', after a word in the sixth case in construction.

The word अवक्रय means, 'Government tax,' 'price,' 'wages,' 'rent' &c., coming from the root अवक्री 'to purchase'. Thus आपणस्य अवक्रयः = आपणिकः ॥

Note:— Are not धर्म्य (IV. 4. 47) and अवक्रय the same? No. Dharmya is a legal due, and religious; while an 'avakraya' may be a tax exacted from a people by oppression, and so transgressing dharma.

1601. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is whose saleable commodity,' after a word in the first case in construction denoting the thing to be sold.

Thus अपूपाः पण्यमस्य = आपूपिकः 'a cake-vendor.'

1602. The affix ठञ् comes, in the sense of 'this is whose saleable commodity,' after the word 'lavaṇa.'

This debars ठक्, the difference being in accent. Thus लवणं पण्यमस्य = लावणिकः 'a salt vendor.'

1603. The affix ष्ठन् comes in the sense of 'this is whose saleable commodity,' after the words 'kisara' &c.

This debars ठक् ॥ The words किसर &c. all denote perfumes. Thus किसराः पण्यमस्य = कैसरिकः / कैसरिकी (IV. 1. 41), नैरादिकः / नैरादिकी ॥ The feminine is formed by ङीष् as the affix has an indicatory ष् ॥

1 किसर (किरार), 2 नलद, 3 नलक, 4 स्थागर, 5 तगर, 6 गुग्गुलु, 7 उशीर, 8 हरिद्रा, 9 एरिक, 10 पर्णक, 11 सुमङ्गल, 12 हरिक्षायणी ॥ All these words denote different kinds of sweet scents.
entries.note: Corrected garbled Devanagari forms of examples.

entries.english:
1604. The affix ष्ठन् comes optionally, in the sense of 'this is whose saleable commodity' after the word 'śalālu'.

This debars ठक् which comes in the alternative. शलालु is a kind of sweet scent. Thus शलालु पण्यमस्य = शालालुकः / शालालुकी. In the alternative with ठक्, शालालुकः / शालालुका ॥

1605. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is whose art', after a word denoting art, in the first case in construction.

Thus मृदङ्गवादनं शिल्पमस्य = मार्दङ्गिकः "a drummer", "an expert in playing on mṛdaṅga drum".

1606. The affix अण् comes optionally in the sense of 'this is whose art', after the words 'maḍḍuka', and 'jharjhara'.

This debars ठक् which comes in the alternative. Thus मड्डुकवादनं शिल्पमस्य = माड्डुकः or माड्डुकिकः, so also झार्झरः and झार्झरिकः ॥

1607. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is whose weapon', after a word denoting 'a weapon', and being in the first case in construction.

Thus असिः प्रहरणमस्य = आसिकः 'a swordsman'. So धानुष्कः ॥

1608. The affix ठञ् as well as ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is whose weapon', after the word परश्वध ॥

The affix ठक् is added by च, the difference being in accent. Thus पारश्वधिकः or पारश्वधिकः ॥ परश्वध means 'an axe'.
1609. The affix ईकक् comes in the sense of "this is whose weapon", after the words 'śakti' and 'yaṣṭi'.
This debars ठक् ॥ Thus शक्तिः प्रहरणमस्य = शाक्तिकः, So also याष्टीकः ॥

1610. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is whose belief', after the words 'asti', 'nasti' and 'dishta'.

Thus अस्तिमतिरस्य = आस्तिकः 'who believes that it is i.e. the hereafter exists', नास्तिकः 'whose belief is that there is no hereafter, an atheist', दैष्टिकः 'whose belief is that it is fate', a fatalist, दिष्टम् 'fate'.

Note:—The affix does not apply in the sense of belief in general, but to a particular sort of belief. Thus परलोकोऽस्ति इति यस्य मतिरस्ति स आस्तिकः, an Astika is he who believes that the Hereafter is. Contrary to him is a नास्तिक who does not believe in a Hereafter. A person who believes what is demonstrated by proof, and nothing else, may also be called दैष्टिकः 'a positivist'. These various other senses are to be found from dictionary and general literature.

1611. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'whose habit is this', after a word in the first case in construction.

Thus अपूपभक्षणं शीलमस्य = आपूपिकः 'one whose habit is to eat cakes'.

Note:—The act of eating, and its habit are qualities understood in the sense of the affix.

1612. The affix ण comes in the sense of 'whose habit is this' after the words 'chhatra' &c.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus छत्रं शीलमस्य = छात्रः 'a pupil', lit. 'whose habit is to cover (chhadana) the weaknesses of the teacher'.

Note:—The word स्था occurs in the list. It must always be prefixed by an upasarga; thus आस्था, संस्था, अवस्था &c.

According to Patanjali छात्र means 'a pupil, because, गुरुश्छत्रवत् गुरुणा शिष्यश्छत्रवत् छाद्यः 'a preceptor is like an Umbrella, the preceptor covers or protects the pupil like an umbrella'. Or शिष्येण गुरुश्छत्रवत् परिपाल्यः 'a pupil ought to maintain or protect his preceptor, as an Umbrella'.

1 छत्र, 2 शिक्षा, 3 प्ररोह (पुरोह), 4 स्था (आस्था, संस्था, अवस्था), 5 बुभुक्षा, 6 सुरा, 7 तितिक्षा, 8 उपस्थान, 9 कृषि (ऋषि), 10 कर्मन्, 11 विश्रन्था, 12 तपस्, 13 सत्य, 14 अनृत, 15 विशिखा, 16 विशिका (शिविका), 17 मञ्चा, 18 स्थान, 19 पुरोडा(१)?, 20 विश, 21 चुक्षा?, 22 मन्द्र।

1613. कार्म is irregularly formed from कर्मन्, by the elision of the final अन्, when the sense is 'accustomed to such an occupation or proficient therein'.

This is formed by affix ण (IV. 4. 62 S. 1612). If this is the case, then by VI. 4. 144 S. 679 the form कार्म is regularly evolved. The fact is, that ण and तृन् affixes, in the sense of tachchhilika are considered as one, and therefore VI. 4. 167 S. 1155 would have prevented the elision of the final syllable. In fact this proves the existence of the following maxim:—ताच्छीलिके ‹?› कृतानि भवन्ति ॥ 'The same operations which are occasioned by the addition of the affix तृन्, take place, whenever the affix ण is added in the sense of one accustomed to that'. Thus though ङीप् is added to अण्-formed words, it is also added to ण-formed words in the feminine as चौरी, तापसी &c. The ण taught in V. 2. 101 S. 1908 and III. 1. 140, S. 2002 is excepted. Why do we say, having the sense of accustomed to that? Observe कार्मणम् ॥

1614. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'this is his act, occurring in study' after a word in the first case in construction, if such a word is an act (karma) which has occurred (vrittam) in study (adhyayana).

Thus एकमन्यदध्ययने कर्मवृत्तमस्य = ऐकान्यिकः 'a pupil who commits one (एक) error (अन्यत्) in reading', &c., literal translation being something like 'one errorist'. He whose, in recitation, at the time of examination, there is the occurrence of one mistake or false reading, is called ऐकान्यिकः ॥ In short, in giving explanatory analysis of taddhita words like ऐकान्यिकः &c., the whole phrase अध्ययने कर्मवृत्तम् must be employed.

1615. The affix ठञ् comes, in the sense of 'this is whose act occurring in study', after a compound having a polysyllabic word as a prior member.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus—द्वादशान्यिकः कर्माण्यध्ययने वृत्तान्यस्य = द्वादशान्यिकः 'an examinee who commits twelve mistakes in his reading'. So चतुर्दशान्यिकः ॥ The word अन्यत् in these sutras means the error, especially in accent, i.e., he who makes an accent anudatta which ought to be udatta, or vice versa.
entries.note: Repaired garbled OCR 'age' to 'anudatta' based on contrast with 'udatta'. Sutra heading partially obscured in OCR.

entries.english:
1616. The affix ठक् comes after a word expressing food, in the first case in construction, in the sense of 'this is wholesome diet for whom'.

Thus अपूपभक्षणं हितमस्मै = आपूपिकः 'He for whom cake is good food' i.e. who eats cakes with benefit or who is fond of cakes. So also शाष्कुलिकः, मौदकिकः ॥ In analysing these taddhitas, such as आपूपिकः &c., the word भक्षण or its synonym, and a verb denoting eating should be employed.

Note:—The words तस्मै and हितम् (IV. 4. 51) are understood. The word हित governs dative (II. 3. 13, S. 570 Vart). But the sutra is तदस्मै हितं भक्षात्, the word भक्षात् being in the ablative case, how is this? Here तदस्मै should be changed to dative viz. हितं भक्षाः तस्मै 'this for whom is wholesome diet'. The best way, however, to remove this objection is to read sutras 65, and 66 in this wise: 65 हितं भक्षाः तस्मै and 66 दीयते नियुक्तम् ॥

1617. The affix comes in the sense of 'to whom this is to be given rightfully', after a word expressing the thing to be given, in the first (tad) case in construction, the force of the affix being that of a dative (asmai).

The word दीयते नियुक्तम् means नियोगेन i.e. अव्यभिचारेण दीयते 'to be given by appointment or rightfully'. Thus अग्रे भोजनमस्मै नियुक्तं दीयते = आग्रभोजनिकः 'a Brahmana always entitled to occupy the foremost seat at dinner'.

Note:—Some say that the word नियुक्तम् means 'always'. According to them आपूपिकः would mean अपूपा नियतं दीयन्ते 'to whom always cakes are given'.

1618. The affix comes in the sense of 'to whom this is to be given rightfully', after the words and मांसौदन ।

This ‹?› debars ‹?›. The ‹?› is for the sake of pronunciation, the ‹?› indicates that the feminine is formed by ‹?› (IV. 1. 15). Thus ‹?› नियुक्तमस्मै दीयते = श्राणिकः । श्राणिकी 'who is entitled to get rice gruel'. So also ‹?› f. मांसौदनिकी । The affix टिटन् applies to मांस and ओदन separately also. (But ‹?› cannot be applied to ‹?› as it would cause Vriddhi (VII. 2. 117) which टिटन् does not). Thus ओदन + टिटन् = ओदनिकः । ओदनिकी । With ‹?› the form would have been ‹?› which is not wanted.

Note:—The difference between ‹?› and ‹?› is in accent, the former having udatta on the final (VI. 1. 165) the latter on the initial (VI. 1. 197). Now the feminine of ‹?› and ‹?› will both be formed by ‹?› (IV. 1. 15). Now the affix ‹?› resembles ‹?› both in accent (VI. 1. 197) and in feminine (IV. 1. 15). Why was ‹?› not used instead of ‹?›, for it would have produced exactly the same form? True, as regards the words ‹?› and ‹?› the affix ‹?› might have been employed instead of ‹?›. The word ‹?› is Past Participle (क्त) of 'to cook'. The ‹?› is not changed to ‹?› as required by VI. 1. 27. This is an anomaly. The ‹?› is changed to ‹?› (VIII. 2. 48). The form ‹?› is also found, as in VI. 1. 36, and the regular form is शृतं क्षीरम् (VI. 1. 27).

entries.english:
1619. The affix ‹?› comes optionally after the word bhakta, in the sense of 'to whom this is to be given rightfully'.

This debars ‹?› which comes in the alternative. Thus ‹?›. In the alternative ‹?› 'regularly fed', i.e. a retainer.

1620. The affix comes, in the sense of 'appointed there', after a word in the seventh case (tatra) in construction.

Thus आकरे नियुक्तः = आकरिकः 'a superintendent of the mines'.

Note:—The word ‹?› is a Tatpurusha compound formed by II. 1. 46.
§. 723 The word niyukta here has a different meaning from that in IV. 4. 66, SK 1617 hence its repetition here.

1621. The affix छन् comes in the sense of "appointed there," after a word ending with 'agara.'

This debars ठक् । The difference is in accent and want of Vriddhi. Thus देवागारे नियुक्तः = देवागारिकः ॥

1622. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of "who studies there," after a word in the 7th case in construction, denoting an improper place or time.

The word अदेशकाल means the time or place of study, which is prohibited by sacred institutes. अध्यायिन् means one who studies. Thus श्मशानेऽधीते = श्माशानिकः 'who reads in a funeral ground.' So also चतुर्दश्यामधीते = चातुर्दशिकः, 'who reads on the 14th lunar day.'

Note:—Why do we say 'Improper time and place?' Observe यज्ञेऽधीते, पूर्वाह्णेऽधीते ॥

1623. The affix ठक् comes, in the sense of "who transacts business there in," after compounds ending in 'kathina,' and after 'prastára' and 'sansthâna,' being in the seventh case in construction.

Thus वंशकठिने व्यवहरति = वांशकठिनिकः 'whose occupation is in a bamboo-thicket,' or 'who does what is proper to be done in such a place', तस्मिन्देशे या क्रिया यथानुष्ठेया तां तथैवानुतिष्ठतीत्यर्थः ॥ So also प्रास्तारिकः, सांस्थानिकः ॥
1624. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who dwells', after the locative word 'nikata'

Thus निकटे वसति = नैकटिकः 'an ascetic, because a sannyasi lives near the city, and enters the city only for the sake of begging, but does not live therein.'

Note:—This rule applies in forming epithets, denoting such persons, who are allowed under the Sacred Institutes, to dwell near human habitations. Thus ‹?› are those ascetics who are ordained to dwell in forests, at least two miles away from human habitations. ‹?› are those ascetics who are allowed by the rule of their Order to live near human habitations.
entries.note: Tail continuation from previous page; embedded Devanagari placeholders.

entries.english:
1625. The affix षल् comes in the sense of 'who dwells there,' after the word 'Avasatha' in the seventh case in construction.

The ल् of षल् is for accent (VI. 1. 193 S. 3676), the ष is for ङीष् (IV. 1. 41 S. 498). Thus आवसथे वसति = आवसथिकः 'who dwells in a house' i.e., a house-holder as opposed to an ascetic. The feminine will be आवसथिकी।

So far was the scope of ठक् as ordained in IV. 4. 1 S. 1548. Henceforward other affixes will be ordained.

The ष of षल् here is a part of the affix, contrary to what it was in sûtra IV. 4. 7 S. 1555. To remove the doubt where ष is the part of an affix, and where it is not, the following mnemonic verse has been composed:— ‹?› In the six sutras IV. 4. 9, 10, 16, 31, 74, and 53, S. 1557, 1558, 1566, 1581, 1625, and 1603 the affixes have indicatory 'sh' i.e., they are part of the affix. Though the sutras are six, the number of affixes taught therein is seven. Here ष being षित्, the feminine is formed by ङीष् (IV. 1. 41).

Here ends the chapter on Thagadhikâra.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari affixes reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
1626. In each aphorism from this one forward to 'tasmai hitam' (V. 1. 5. S. 1665), the affix यत् bears rule.

Note:—Thus in the next sutra तद्वहति रथयुगप्रासङ्गम् we must read the affix यत् ॥ रथ्यः युग्यः प्रासङ्ग्यः ॥

1627. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the words 'ratha', 'yuga', and 'prasaṅga', being in the second case in construction.

Thus रथं वहति = रथ्यः 'what bears a car' a carriage-horse. Similarly युग्यः 'a yoke-bearing ox', प्रासङ्ग्यः 'being trained in a break', प्रासङ्गः is a piece of wood placed on the neck of colts, at the time of breaking.

Note:—This rule applies to compounds ending with ratha, as परमरथ्यः । See IV. 3. 121, 123 S. 1501, 1503 also. That which carries will be called 'carrier' or वोढृ therefore रथस्य वोढृ will get the affix यत् by IV. 3. 120 S. 1500 read with IV. 3. 121 S. 1501. Its special mention here indicates that the affix will come, even after Dvigu compounds and will not be elided by IV. 1. 88 S. 1080.

Thus द्वौ रथौ वहति = ‹?› The tadanta-vidhi applies to this word as we have shown under IV. 3. 121 S. 1501. The word युग has been already formed by the kṛt affix (III. 1. 121, S. 2873), that युग differs from the present in accent, when the word takes the negative particle, for that was by क्यप् and this is by यत्, and therefore by VI. 2. 156 S. 3890, अयुग्यम् will be finally acute when formed by यत् ॥ The word युग must mean 'the portion of a car' for the application of this rule, and not a cycle of time &c. Therefore not here युगं वहति राजा कलिं द्वापरं वा ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed heavily corrupted Devanagari in examples and commentary.

entries.english:
1628. The affixes यत् and ढक् come in the sense of 'what bears it', after the word 'dhur' in the second case in construction.

Thus धुरं वहति = धुर्यः (formed by यत्) the lengthening ordained by VIII. 2. 77 S. 354 is prevented by the next sutra, because धूर् is a Bha-stem, or धौरेयः (formed by VII. 1. 2 S. 475) 'a beast of burden'.

Note:—This sūtra might have stood as धुरो ढक्, for यत् would have been read into it from IV. 4. 75 S. 1626.
entries.note: Supplied missing Devanagari affixes and examples from context.

entries.english:
1629. The lengthening of the vowel does not take place under VIII. 2. 77 S. 354, when the Nominal stem ending in र् or व् is called Bha (i.e. when a य follows), and also not in कुर् and छुर् ॥

Thus धुर्यः (धुरं वहति IV. 4. 77 S. 1628 or धुरि साधुः) । Or धौरेयः with ढक्.
