Note:—Why have we qualified the word by saying that it must end in र् or व्? Observe प्रतिदीव्ना, प्रतिदीव्ने ॥ For here the stem which ends in व् is not Bha, and the stem which is Bha does not end in व् but अन् ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed missing characters (r and v) in sutra translation and note.

entries.english:
1630. The affix 'kha' comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the word 'sarva-dhura', being in accusative construction.

Thus सर्वधुरां वहति = सर्वधुरीणः (VII. 1. 2 S. 475).

Note:—The affix applies to other compounds also ending in धुर e.g. उत्तरधुरीणः, दक्षिणाधुरीणः । The word सर्वधुर is a compound of सर्वा धुरा (II. 1. 49 S. 726), the samāsānta being added by V. 4. 74 S. 940. The word being feminine, the whole compound would be feminine by II. 4. 26 S. 812. The word in the sūtra should not be taken, therefore, as regulating the gender, for though सर्वधुरात् is in the masculine gender, the affix comes after the feminine word. In fact सर्वधुर in the sūtra should be taken as a nominal stem or prātipadika equal to सर्वधुरा ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed embedded Devanagari in note.

entries.english:
1631. The affix 'kha' comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the word 'eka-dhura' in the second case in construction, and the affix is optionally elided also.

The elision is optional. Thus एकधुरं वहति = एकधुरीणः or एकधुरः ॥

Note:—The compounding is taddhitārtha (एकां धुरां वहति) to which is added the samāsānta टच् and then the affix ख ॥

1632. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the word शकट in the second case in construction.

Thus शकटं वहति = शाकटः an ox i.e. what bears a car.

Note:—This could be evolved by तस्येदम् as शाकटस्य वोढा = शाकटः । The specification indicates that tadanta-vidhi applies here, as द्वौ शकटौ वहति = ‹?›, and the affix is not elided (IV. 1. 88 S. 1080).
entries.note: Reconstructed Devanagari affix and words in note.

entries.english:
1633. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the words 'hala' and 'sīra', in the 2nd case in construction.

Thus हलं वहति = हालिकः 'a ploughman', सैरिकः 'a plough ox'.

Note:—The affix would have come by IV. 3. 124, S. 1504, the specification shows tadantavidhi and non-elision, as द्विहालिकः, द्विसैरिकः ॥
entries.note: Corrected OCR errors in examples and note.

entries.english:
1634. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what bears it', after the word 'janī', being in the 2nd case in construction, the whole word being a Name.

Thus जनीं वहति = जन्यः 'a friend of a bridegroom', fem. जन्या 'a bride's-maid'. The word जनी means 'bride', जन्या lit. means 'what bears the bride' i.e. who carries the coy bride to the bride-groom at the time of play &c. Kālidāsa has used it in the sense of the bearers of the vehicle in which the bride goes. As यातेन जन्यानयत् कुमारीम् ॥
entries.note: Corrected OCR misreads in Sanskrit words and Kalidasa quote.
Entry cut off at end of batch before English heading and translation (partial: head).

entries.english: 1635. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what pierces it', after a word in the accusative case in construction, provided that, it is not a bow, with which anything is pierced. Thus पादौ विध्यन्ति = पद्याः (VI. 3. 53, S. 991) शर्कराः, 'what pierce the feet' i. e. pebbles. Note:—Why do we say "provided it is not a bow, अधनुषा"? Observe पादौ विध्यति धनुषा, no affix is added here. This exclusion of धनुषा indicates that the act of piercing must be such as not to be done by a bow &c. Therefore the affix does not apply to cases like these अक्षि विध्यति, शत्रुं विध्यति ॥
entries.note: Sutra line omitted from top of page 847 (printed on preceding page); heading begins page 847.

entries.english: 1636. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'who obtains it,' after the words 'dhana,' and 'gana,' being in the second case in construction. Thus धनं लब्धा = धन्यः, so also गण्यः ॥ लब्धा is formed from √लभ् by तृन्, hence it takes the accusative.
entries.note: Entry number corrected from OCR misprint 1686 to 1636.

entries.english: 1637. The affix comes in the sense of 'who obtains it,' after the word ‹?›, in the second case in construction. Thus ‹?› = 'fed,' 'who has obtained food.'
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari illegible in OCR source.

entries.english: 1638. The affix comes in the sense of 'gone,' after the word vasa, 'control' being in the second case in construction. Thus वश्यः 'come under control' i. e. subdued i. e. a dependant or servant. वश = काम इच्छा तां प्राप्तः i. e. परेच्छानुगामी ॥
entries.note: Restored missing word वश्यः before gloss from clear context.

entries.english: 1639. The affix यत् comes after the word 'pada,' in the sense of 'in it is visible,' being in the first case in construction. Thus पदं दृश्यमस्मिन् = पद्यः कर्दमः 'mud' literally, soft mud in which foot-mark can be seen at every step. It describes mud which is neither very hard nor very fluid, but having sufficient consistency to take the impression of the foot. Note:—So पद्याः पांसवः 'dust' for in it also the impression of foot can be seen. It also means the foot-path. The word पद्य means ‹?› this having the force of the kṛtya affix ‘ya’ in दृश्य ॥
entries.note: Entry spans pages 847-848; sutra numeral 1639 misprinted as 1636 in OCR.

entries.english: 1640. The affix comes in the sense of 'whose root is eradicated,' after the word 'mula,' being in the first case in construction. The word ‹?› from ‹?› 'to uproot,' means 'uprooting,'—मूल्या मुद्गाः 'a kind of pulse' e. g. These cereals cannot be harvested without uprooting the whole plant. Note:—According to Padamañjarī the word should be आवर्हि and not आबर्हि, with a व and not ब ॥
entries.note: Disentangled OCR line-scrambling and corrected Padamanjari note.

entries.english: 1641. The word धेनुष्या is irregularly formed, being a Name. This word is formed by adding ‹?› and य to धेनु ॥ It has udātta on the final. It means that cow (धेनु) which is given to a creditor in discharge of a debt or as a pledge to satisfy the debt from her milk. It is also called पीतदुग्धा ॥ As धेनुष्यो भवते दशमी । See Amarakosha II. 9. 72. "धेनुष्या बन्धके स्थिता" ॥
entries.note: Fixed OCR garbles in English prose and Sanskrit quotation.

entries.english: 1642. The affix comes in the sense of 'joined with', after the word 'grihapati' in the third case in construction. The word grihapati means 'sacrificer'. Thus गृहपतिना संयुक्तः = गार्हपत्यः 'the Gārhapatya Fire' i. e. a Fire particularly consecrated by the Householder. Note:—The word संज्ञायाम् of the last sūtra should be read into it, thus गार्हपत्य means a particular Fire, and not every thing relating to ‹?›. The Fire in which husband (grihapati), together with or joined with his wife, performs sacrifice is called Gārhapatya. That sacrifice cannot be performed in Dakṣiṇāgni. Or that fire in which Gṛhapati hymns are learned is called Gārhapatya.
entries.note: Entry spans pages 848-849.

entries.english: 1643. The affix comes after the words नौ 'a boat', वयस् 'age', धर्म 'merit', विष 'poison', मूल 'a root', मूल 'capital', सीता 'a furrow', and तुला 'a balance', in the senses respectively, of "to be crossed", "like", "attainable", "to be put to death", "to be bent down", "equivalent to", "united with" and "equally measured". The words in the above must be all in the Instrumental case in construction, for the sense of the affix shows that they should be so. Thus— 1. नावा तार्यम् = नाव्यम् 'water' 'a river', literally, what can be crossed by a boat. 2. वयसा तुल्यः = वयस्यः 'a friend', lit. one alike in age. 3. धर्मेण प्राप्यम् = धर्म्यम् 'what is attainable through dharma'. Note:—Could not this form have been evolved by the next sūtra (IV. 4. 92, S. 1644)? No, dharmya formed by that aphorism means 'what is consistent with dharma' 'what is just'. The present refers to the 'fruit', the other to the 'act'. 4. विषेण वध्यः = विष्यः 'who deserves to be put to death by poison'. 5. मूलेनानाम्यम् = मूल्यम् "price" lit. or "to be overpowered or bent by the root". Note:—The word ‹?› (which is formed from the root 'to bow' by the affix ‹?› contrary to rule III. 1. 98, S. 2844 which required ‹?›), means ‹?›, 'what ought to be overpowered', hence मूल्य means 'the price, worth, cost', because articles like 'cloth' &c. are produced by the out-lay of stock or capital (मूल); 'price' being a thing which, because it is capital plus profit, is superior to capital, and thus by price or mulyam, the capital or mula is overpowered. 6. मूलेन समः = मूल्यः 'purchasable' lit. 'equivalent to capital' e. g. cloth &c. i. e. equivalent acquisition resulting from the employment of capital. 7. सीतया समितम् = सीत्यम् 'a field', lit. measured out by furrows according to Dr Ballantyne.
entries.note: Text cut off at end of page 849 (item 8 continues on next page); partial head.

entries.english:
Note:—The word ‹?› is equivalent to ‹?› 'united with' according to Kasika therefore, literally means 'a ploughed field' i.e. 'what is united with furrows'. The affix will apply also to words ending with सीता, e.g. परमसीत्यं, ‹?› द्वितीय ॥

8. तुलया सम्मितं = तुल्यम्, 'equal' lit. meted out by the balance. सम्मित means समानं सदृशं ॥
entries.note: Continuation tail of entry 1643 from preceding page.

entries.english:
1644. The affix comes in the sense of 'not deviating therefrom', after the word 'dharma,' 'pathin,' 'artha' and 'nyâya' being in the ablative case in construction.

The ablative construction is inferred from its employment in the sutra itself. Thus धर्मादनपेतं = धर्म्यम् 'just, not deviating from merit.' Similarly पथ्यम् ॥ शास्त्रात् पथो यदनपेतं तत् पथ्यं न तु तस्मादनपेतश्चारः 'wholesome diet,' अर्थ्यम् 'fit', 'just, suitable.'

Note:—The word ‹?› (IV. 4. 89 § 1641) governs this sutra also, and hence the derivatives must have the above meanings.

1645. The affix comes in the sense of 'made,' after the word 'chhandas,' being in the instrumental case in construction.

Thus छन्दसा निर्मितं = छन्दस्यम् 'made at will.' The word छन्दस् is here synonymous with 'will, wish, desire, fancy' &c., and does not mean 'metre or Veda.'

1646. The affix as well as comes after 'uras' in the 3rd case in construction, in the sense of 'made.'

The यत् is drawn into the sutra by the particle च ॥ उरसा निर्मितः = औरसः 'own son, not an adopted son,' lit. 'produced through the loins.' With the form will be These words denote son, and not anything produced from the loin, because the word ‹?› (IV. 4. 89.) governs this sutra also.

1647. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'loved,' after the word 'hridaya,' in the genitive case in construction.

The construction is shown by the aphorism itself. Thus हृदयस्य प्रियः = हृद्यम् (VI. 3. 50 § 988) 'pleasant to the heart' e.g. हृद्यं वनम् ॥

Note:—But we cannot say हृद्यः पुत्रः, the word संज्ञायाम् (IV. 4. 89 § 1641) governs this sutra also, and thus restricts the meaning of the word.

1648. The affix यत् comes in the sense of a bond, after the word 'hridaya,' being in the genitive construction, when the word denotes a 'hymn'.

The word हृदयस्य is understood in the sutra. The word बन्धन gives the sense of the affix and is qualified by the word ऋषि ॥ That by which a thing is bound is called बन्धनम् ॥ The word ऋषि means here the Veda or the Vaidic hymn. Thus हृदयस्य बन्धनमृषिः = हृद्यः, the Mantra by which the heart of another can be brought under one's control, i.e. a वशीकरणमन्त्रः ॥

1649. The affix यत् comes after words 'mata', 'jana', and 'hala', in the sense respectively of 'means', 'gossip', and 'drawing', the words being in the sixth case in construction.

Thus मतस्य करणं = मत्यम् 'the means of acquiring knowledge'. Mata means knowledge. जनस्य जल्पः = जन्या 'a rumour'. हलस्य कर्षः = हल्यम् 'ploughed'.

Note:—So also द्वयहल्यम्, त्र्यहल्यम्: the tadanta vidhi applies रथसीताहलेभ्यो यद्विधौ ॥

1650. The affix यत् comes after a word in the locative construction, in the sense of 'excellent in regard thereto'.

Thus सामसु साधुः = सामन्यः (The अन् remains unchanged by VI. 4. 168 § 154) 'conversant with the Sama Veda'. So also कर्मण्यः, शरण्यः &c. The साधु here means प्रवीणाः or योग्यः 'expert' and 'fit', and does not mean उपकारकः 'a benefactor or a good person'.

Note:—When the sense is that of 'good', the sutra तस्मै हितम् (V. 1. 5) will apply.

1651. The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent in regard thereto,' after the word 'pratijana' &c.

This debars यत् ॥ Thus प्रतिजने साधुः = प्रातिजनीनः (VII. 1. 2 § 475) 'suitable against an adversary' or 'who is excellent for every person'. So also सांयुगीनः, सार्वजनीनः, वैश्वजनीनः ॥

1 प्रतिजन, 2 युग, 3 सयुग, 4 समयुग, 5 परयुग, 6 परकुल, 7 परस्यकुल, 8 अमुष्यकुल, 9 सर्वजन, 10 विश्वजन, 11 महाजन, 12 पञ्चजन ॥
entries.note: Heading number 1661 corrected to 1651 to maintain strict sequence.

entries.english:
1652. The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto', after the word 'bhakta'.

This debars यत् ॥ Thus, भक्ते साधवः = भाक्ताः शालयः 'rice, lit. suitable or excellent for food'.
entries.note: Heading number 1662 corrected to 1652 to maintain strict sequence.

entries.english:
1653. The affix ण्य comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto', after the word 'parishad' (as well as अण्).

This debars यत् ॥ Thus परिषदि साधुः = पारिषद्यः ॥ The affix अण् is also employed here by the method of splitting up a single sutra into two. Thus (1) परिषदः and (2) ण्य ॥ Thus परिषदि साधुः = पारिषदः 'one versed in the affairs of a council', 'a minister'.

1654. The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto', after the words 'katha' &c.

Thus कथायां साधुः = काथिकः (कथा + ठक् = कथ् + ठक् VI. 4. 148 § 311) = काथ् इक (VII. 2. 116 § 2282) 'a narrator of stories'.
entries.note: Heading number 1664 corrected to 1654 to maintain strict sequence; entry continues on next page.

entries.english: 1. कथा, 2. विकथा, 3. विश्वकथा *, 4. संकथा *, 5. वितण्डा, 6. कुष्टविद् (कुटविद, कुष्टचित्), 7. जनवार, 8. जनवाद, 9. आनोवाद * (i), 10. वृत्ति, 11. समक्ष (सद्ग्रह), 12. गुण, 13. गण, 14. आयुर्वेदः ॥
entries.note: Tail fragment of kathādi gaṇa belonging to SK 1654.

entries.english:
1655. The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto', after the words 'guḍa &c.'

This debars यत् ॥ Thus गुडे साधुः = गौडिकः 'sugar-cane lit. excellent in making sugar', साक्तुकः 'barley lit. suitable for making saktu'.

1. गुड, 2. कुल्माष, 3. सक्तु, 4. अपूप, 5. मांसौदन, 6. इक्षु, 7. वेणु, 8. संग्राम, 9. संघात, 10. ललाम *, 11. संवाह, 12. प्रवास, 13. निवास, 14. उपवास ॥
entries.note: Heading serial number misprinted as 1656 in source; corrected to 1655. Affix ठञ् and gaṇa entries corrected.

entries.english:
1656. The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto', after the words 'pathi', 'atithi', 'vasati' and 'svapati'.

This debars यत् ॥ Thus पथि साधु = पाथेयम् (VII. 1. 2, S. 475) 'provision for journey', आतिथेयम् 'hospitality', वासतेयी 'habitable' as वासतेयी रात्रिः, स्वापतेयम् 'wealth, property'.
entries.note: Affix ढञ् restored; misread Sanskrit forms and cross-reference corrected.

entries.english:
1657. The affix य comes after the word 'sabhā' when the sense is 'excellent with regard thereto'.

This debars यत् the difference being in accent (III. 1. 3, S. 3708 and VI. 1. 185). Thus सभायां साधु = सभ्यः 'refined' lit. fit for society.
entries.note: 'sabba' corrected to 'sabhā'; 'it' to 'fit'; affix य restored.

entries.english:
1658. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'resident therein', after the word 'samāna-tīrtha', in the locative construction.

The anuvṛtti of साधु now ceases. The word तीर्थ means here गुरु 'Preceptor'. Thus समाने तीर्थे वासी = सतीर्थ्यः (VI. 3. 87, S. 1015) — 'a fellow-student', who both dwell under the same preceptor.

1659. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'who sleeps', after the word 'samānodara' in the locative construction, and the udātta falls on the letter o.

The word शयितः is equal to स्थितः 'remains'. Thus समानोदरे शयितः = समानोदर्यो भ्राता 'uterine brother' i.e. who has slept in the same womb. See VI. 3. 88, S. 1016.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra is at bottom of page 853, English heading on page 854; missing affix यत् and garbled Devanagari restored.

entries.english:
1660. The affix यत् comes after the word 'sodara', in the sense of 'who sleeps', the word being in the 7th case in construction.

By sūtra VI. 3. 88 समान is optionally changed to स before the word उदर when यत् follows. Thus समानोदरे शयितः = सोदर्यः ॥ Here ओ is not udātta, as it was in the last; the udātta here falls on यत् ॥

Here ends the chapter on Prāgghitīya.
entries.note: Affix यत् and dropped Devanagari forms समान, स, उदर restored from context.

entries.english:
1661. From this sūtra forward up to 'tena krītam' V. 1. 37, S. 1702 the affix 'chha' bears rule.

Note:— The affix छ has the various senses taught in these thirty-seven Sūtras V. 1. 1 to 37, S. 1702. Thus in the Sūtra तस्मै हितम् 'suitable for that', V. 1. 5, S. 1665 the word छ must be read to complete the sense. Thus वत्सेभ्यो हितो वत्सीयो गोधुक्, करभीय उष्ट्रः, भवदीयम् । The limitation of the jurisdiction of this sūtra with regard to छ has been indicated in the sūtra with regard to the meaning of the affix, and not with regard to the affix. As an affix, छ has no force beyond V. 1. 18, S. 1679 the affix ठञ् being the ruling affix thereafter.
entries.note: Affixes छ and ठञ् restored; OCR letter-drops and garbled Sanskrit examples corrected.

entries.english:
1662. The affix 'yat' comes after a prātipadika ending with उ (long or short), and after the words गो and the rest, the senses of the affix being those taught up to Sūtra V. 1. 37, S. 1702.

The senses of Prākkrītiya affixes are three, viz those taught in sūtras V. 1. 5, S. 1665, V. 1. 12, S. 1674 and V. 1. 16, S. 1678. This यत् debars छ ॥

Note the words शङ्कु meaning 'a kind of leather', and चरु 'a kind of हविस् offering', and सक्तु 'a kind of food', all end in उ and are governed by this sūtra, in spite of V. 1. 15, S. 1677 which applies especially to leathers, and V. 1. 4, S. 1664 and its vārtika which applies especially to 'offerings' and 'food modifications'. This is an example where a subsequent sūtra does not debar a prior sūtra (I. 4. 2). Thus शङ्कु + यत् = शङ्कव्यं चर्म, 'leather fit for making Śaṅku', चरु + यत् = चर्व्यास्तण्डुलाः 'rice fit for making charu', सक्तु + यत् = सक्तव्या धानाः 'barley fit for making Saktu'
entries.note: Entry cut off at page boundary (continues onto page 856); garbled Devanagari words and affixes restored.

entries.english:
Gana Sutra :— नाभि is replaced by नभ when the affix यत् is added. Thus नाभये हितम् = नभ्यम् meaning अक्षः 'axis, axle' lit. 'fitted for the nave of the wheel', or a wood fit to be made the nave of a wheel or अञ्जनम् 'the grease.'
Note.—When the word नाभि means 'the navel' of a living being, then it will not take this यत्, but it will take the यत् of V. 1. 6 § 1666. In that case, नभ will not replace नाभि, e.g. नाभि + यत् = नाभ्यम् 'suitable for navel' i.e. oil.
Gana Sutra :—The word श्वन् takes samprasarana, व being changed to उ, and optionally this उ is lengthened; and the udatta accent falls on the final. As श्वन् + यत् = शुन्यम् or श्वन् + यत् = शून्यम् 'fit for a dog.' Contrary to VI. 4. 144, the न् of श्वन् is not elided before the taddhita affix यत् ॥
Gana Sutra :—The final of the word ऊधस् is replaced by अनङ् e.g. ऊधस् + यत् = ऊध् + अन् + य = ऊधन्यः कूपः 'a well'.
1 गवि, 2 हविस्, 3 अक्षर, 4 विष, 5 बर्हिस्, 6 अष्टका, 7 रुक्मा (रुक्म), 8 युग, 9 मेधा, 10 त्रुच् (स्रुच्), 11 नाभि नभ च, 12 शुनः संप्रसारणं वा च दीर्घत्वं तत्संनियोगेन चोदात्तत्वम्, 13 ऊधसोऽनङ्, 14 कृक*, 15 व*, 16 दर (उदर), 17 खर, 18 असुर*, 19 अध्यन् (अध्यन्, अध्या), 20 क्षर*, 21 वेद*, 22 बीज*, 23 वि (वीस), 24 स्कन्द ॥

1663. The affix यत् comes in the Prâk-kritîya senses, after the word 'kambala', when a name is meant.
This debars छ. Thus कम्बल + यत् = कम्बल्यम्. 'A kambalya measure of wool' = 100 Palas of wool. This is the name of a measure, such as कम्बल्यमूर्णा पलशतम् ॥
Why do we say संज्ञायाम्? Observe कम्बलीया ऊर्णा 'wool' lit. 'fit for making blanket', which is formed by छ ॥

1664. The affix यत् comes optionally after the words denoting, 'offering,' and after 'apûpa &c.,' in the sense of Prâk-kritîya.
Thus आमिक्ष्या दधि, 'fit for making आमिक्षा' i.e. curd;—or आमिक्षीयम् with छ. So also पुरोडाश्याः or पुरोडाशीयास्तण्डुलाः, 'suitable for making Purodasa' i.e. a kind of rice.
Note.—The word हविस् occurs in the गवादि class (V. 1. 2 § 1662) and it necessarily takes यत् there being no option. The हविस् here, therefore, means things denoting sacrificial offerings, and not the word-form 'havis'.
So also after अपूपादि, as अपूप्यम् or अपूपीयम् ॥
1 अपूप, 2 तण्डुल, 3 (अभ्यूष), 4 सम्मेष, 5 अवशेष, 6 अभ्योष, 7 पृथुक, 8 ओदन, 9 सूप, 10 पूप, 11 किण्व, 12 प्रदीप, 13 मुसल, 14 कदङ्क, 15 कर्णवेष्टक, 16 इङ्गुद, 17 अर्गल, 18 उत्कार, 19 यूप, 20 स्थूणा, 21 वीप (वीश), 22 अश्व, 23 पत्र, 24 कट, 25 भवस्थूण.
Gana Sutra :—The affix यत् comes optionally after words denoting modifications of food; such as पिष्टम् ॥ In the case of 'saktu' however, no option is allowed. See V. 1. 2 § 1662.

1665. An affix comes after a word in the fourth case in construction, in the sense of 'good for that.'
Thus वत्सेभ्यो हितो गोधुक् = वत्सीयः 'fit for calves' i.e. a cow-milker. So also शङ्कवे हितं = शङ्कु + यत् = शङ्कव्यम् (VI. 4. 146, § 847, VI. 1. 79 § 63). As शङ्कव्यं दारु, 'wood', 'fit for a stake'. गव्यम्; हविष्यम् ॥

1666. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'good for that,' after a word denoting a part of the body.
The word शरीर means animal organism. This debars छ, thus, दन्त्यम् 'good for the teeth' कण्ठ्यम्, नख्यम्, नाभ्यम्, नस्यम् such as dentifrice, snuff, oil &c. See VI. 1. 213.
Vart :—The नस् is substituted for नासिका only when the affixes यत् and तस्, and the word क्षुद्र follow as, नस्यम्, नस्तः, नस्-क्षुद्रः ॥ The यत् is taught in IV. 3. 55 § 1430 and V. 1. 6 § 1666, तस् is taught in V. 4. 45 § 2126.
The word शिरस् 'head' is also governed by this rule, but शिरस् is replaced by शीर्षन् before यत् by the next sutra.

1667. There is the substitution of शीर्षन् for शिरस् when a Taddhita affix beginning with य follows.
The word शीर्षन् is understood here, from the preceding Ashtadhyayi sutra.
This rule teaches substitution. The original for which this substitution comes is not given in the sutra, we must infer it. The appropriate original is शिरस्. Thus शिरसे हितं शुचये यद्वाऽपि, शीर्षण्यः शिरः ॥ The affix is here added by V. 1. 6 § 1666. The word retains its original form before this affix, the final not being replaced by anything else (VI. 4. 168 § 1154).
Why do we say when 'a Taddhita-affix follows'? Observe शिरस्यति, here य is not a Taddhita affix, and so there is no substitution.
Vart :—The substitution is optional when meaning 'hair'. As शीर्षण्याः केशाः or शिरस्याः केशाः ॥
Vart :—There is the substitution of शीर्ष for शिरस् when a Taddhita affix beginning with a vowel follows.
Thus शिरसोऽपत्यम् = हास्तिशीर्षः formed by adding the Patronymic affix अण् (IV. 1. 96 § 1096). So also स्थूलशिरसो हृदयम् = स्थौलशीर्षम् ॥
Note.—Had the word been शीर्षन् (instead of शीर्ष as taught herein) then it would have retained its final before these affixes and would not have given the proper forms (VI. 4. 168 § 1154). Again in forming the feminine of हास्तिशीर्षः by adding ष्यङ् (IV. 1. 78 § 1198), arises this difficulty—ष्यङ् (य) is a Taddhita affix beginning with य, when this is applied to शीर्ष, we must apply the last rule and change the शीर्ष into शीर्षन् (for शीर्षन् being the substitute of शिरस् is prima facie a substitute of शीर्ष also for the purposes of that rule VI. 1. 61 § 1667). The form which we get will be this, हास्तिशीर्ष + ष्यङ् = हास्तिशीर्षन् + य (VI. 1. 61 § 1667) = हास्तिशीर्षन्या (VI. 4. 168 § 1154). But this is a wrong form, the desired form is हास्तिशीर्ष्या ॥ How do we explain this? Thus हास्तिशीर्ष + ष्यङ् = हास्तिशीर्ष् + य (the अ is elided by VI. 4. 148 and in the room of अ we substitute a zero or स्थानिवद्भाव ). Now this zero becomes sthanivat to अ, thus the affix य not being directly applied to शीर्ष because this zero intervenes, शीर्ष is not replaced by शीर्षन् as required by VI. 1. 61, § 1667, for it is not followed by an affix beginning with य but by a zero sthanivat to an affix.

1668. The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'good for that,' after the word 'khala,' 'yava,' 'masha,' 'tila,' 'vrisha' and 'brahmana.'
This debars छ. Thus खल्यम्, 'suitable for threshing floor.' So also यव्यम्, माष्यम्, तिल्यम्, वृष्यम्, or ब्रह्मण्यम् ॥
Note.—No secondary derivatives can, however, be formed of the following:—वृषेभ्यो हितम्। ब्राह्मणेभ्यो हितम्; the full phrases must be used in these cases, for these words take neither छ nor यत् though वृष is = वृषन् and ब्रह्मन् is = ब्राह्मण ॥
The word च in the sutra indicates that the rule applies to words other than those enumerated. Thus रथाय हिता = रथ्या ॥

1669. The affix थ्यन् comes in the sense of 'good for that,' after the words 'aja' and 'avi.'

This debars छ. Thus अजथ्या यूथी 'the yellow jasmine called yûthî', अविथ्या ॥
entries.note: Sutra line printed on previous page (858); entry begins on page 859 with vritti fragment and English heading.

entries.english:
1670. The affix 'kha' comes in the sense of 'good for that,' after the words 'atman,' and 'visvajana' and after compounds having the word 'bhoga' as their second term.

This debars छ ॥ In the sûtra, the न् of आत्मन् has not been elided, indicating that it should not be compounded with the word भोग which would have been the case otherwise. It therefore follows from this irregular construction of the sûtra, that the word भोगोत्तरपद does not apply to the words आत्मन् and विश्वजन, but these words are themselves prakriti. Thus आत्मन् + ख = आत्मनीनम् 'suitable for one's self'. The ti of atman, which required to be elided by VI. 4. 144 (S. 679), is saved by the next sûtra.

1671. The final of the stems आत्मन् and अध्वन् remain unchanged before the affix ख ॥

Thus आत्मने हितं = आत्मनीनः (V. 1. 9. S. 1670).

Note:— अध्वानमलङ्गामी (V. 2. 16. S. 1817) अध्वनीनः ॥ But प्रत्यात्मम् and प्रत्यध्वम् ॥ The first is formed by the samâsânta affix टच् added to the avyayîbhâva (V. 4. 108. S. 678), and the latter by (V. 4. 85. S. 953).

So also विश्वजनीनम् 'suitable for all men'. The word विश्वजन must be a Karmadhâraya compound, meaning 'all men', for the application of this rule; when it is a Tatpurusha or a Bahuvrîhi compound, it will take छ. As, विश्वजनाय हितं = विश्वजनीयम् 'beneficial for mankind'.

Vârt:— So also after Karmadhâraya compound पञ्चजन, as, पञ्चजनीनम्, otherwise पञ्चजनीयम् ॥

Vârt:— After the Karmadhâraya compound सर्वजन, there are the affixes ‹?› and ख, as सर्वजनीनम् and सर्वजनिकम्; otherwise सार्वजनीयम् ॥

Vârt:— The affix ठञ् comes always after the word महाजन whether it be a Karmadhâraya or a Tatpurusha, but not so when it is a Bahuvrîhi compound. As महाजनाय हितं माहाजनिकम् । In a Bahuvrîhi it will be महाजनीयः with छ.

Compounds having भोग as their final term also take the affix ख, as, मातृभोगीणः and पितृभोगीणः ॥ The word भोग means 'body'. But मात्रियः and पित्रियः with छ when the word भोग does not follow.

Vârt:— The words राजन् and आचार्य followed by 'bhoga' take always the affix ख, as राजभोगीनः and आचार्यभोगीनः ॥

Gaṇa-sûtra:— In the case of आचार्यभोगीनः the न is not changed into ण (VIII. 4. 2). The words do not take the affix ख when used singly. As, ‹?›, राज्ञे हितम्, no affix being employed.

1672. The affixes ण and ढञ् come respectively in the sense of 'good for that' after the words 'sarva' and 'purusha'.

Vârt:— The affix ‹?› comes optionally after सर्व, as सर्वस्मै हितं = सर्व्यम् or सार्वम् ॥

Vârt:— The affix ढञ् comes after पुरुष when the word so formed means: 'slaughter', 'modification', 'a crowd' or 'made by him'.

The word तेन is placed in the middle of the Dvandva, according to the employment of the author of the Mahâbhâshya.

Thus पुरुषस्य वधः = पौरुषेयः 'manslaughter.' Here अण् (IV. 3. 120, S. 1500), is debarred. So also पुरुषस्य विकारः = पौरुषेयः 'human.' Here अञ् (IV. 3. 154, S. 1532) is debarred.

Similarly in the sense of समूहः 'crowd,' as in the following line of Mâgha:—

एकाकिनोऽपि परितः पौरुषेयीवृता इव ॥ Here also the अण् of तस्य समूहः is debarred.

So also in the sense of 'the book composed,' the affix अण् would have come, but this debars it. When the thing made is not a book but 'palace' &c, then no other sûtra applies, and this ordains ढञ् as a vidhi.

Thus पौरुषेयो ग्रन्थः 'a human book', as opposed to अपौरुषेया वेदाः 'the non-human Vedas'. So also पौरुषेयः प्रासादः 'a man-built palace'.

1673. The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'good for that', after the words 'mâṇava', and 'caraka'.

This debars छ ॥ As माणवाय हितं = माणवीनम् ॥ So also चारकीणम् ॥

1674. After a word being the name of a product, the above-mentioned affix comes, to denote a thing which is the primitive that is serviceable for that.

Note.— The word ‹?› means primitive or the material cause of a product. The word विकृति means 'the product' or 'modification of such primitive'. तदर्थम् means 'serviceable for that' i.e. the primitive being serviceable for the product. The word shows that the primitive must be serviceable for that particular product and nothing else. That is to say, an affix will not come to denote any product in general, but only when the primitive is serviceable for a particular product and nothing else. The word shows also that the word must be in the 4th case when the affix is added. Some read the words तस्मै हितम् also into this sûtra.

Thus अङ्गारेभ्यो हितानि एतानि काष्ठानि = अङ्गारीयाणि काष्ठानि 'wood serviceable for making charcoal,' so also प्राकारीया इष्टका 'bricks serviceable for making a wall'. Here अङ्गारीय and प्राकारीय are formed by V. 1. 1. S. 1661. Similarly शङ्कव्यं दारु 'wood serviceable for a spear'.

Note:— Why do we say तदर्थम् 'serviceable thereto'? Observe यवानां धानाः, धानानां सक्तवः ॥ Here there is modification of primitive, but सक्तु is the product also of other things than यव, such as ‹?› &c.

Why do we say 'after product'? Observe कूपस्योदकम् there is no affix. For कूपः 'a well' and 'water' do not stand in the relation of प्रकृति and विकृति, i.e. material cause and effect, as 'water' is not the modification or product of 'the well' though it is found in the well, and therefore the affix is not employed.

Why do we say 'to denote a primitive'? Observe ‹?› 'a sheath serviceable for a sword'. The sword is a product of iron, but a sheath is not the primitive of the sword.

By using the words प्रकृति and विकृति it is further shown that the prakriti is liable to modification or vikâra.

1675. The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product, after the words 'chhadis,' 'upadhi', and 'bali' denoting the product.

This debars छ. Thus छादिषेयाणि तृणानि । बालेयास्तण्डुलाः ॥
entries.note: Entry cut off at end of page 861 / batch.

entries.english: Ishti:—The affix comes after the word उपाधि without changing the sense. उपधीयत इत्युपधिः । = रथाङ्गम् part of a wheel between the nave and the circumference or the wheel itself. The word औपधेयम् also means the same.
entries.note: Tail of entry 1675 continuing from preceding page.

entries.english:
1676. The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product, after the words 'rishabha' and 'upânah' denoting the products.
This debars छ ।
Thus आर्षभेयो वत्सः, औपनाहेयो मुञ्जः. Even when the primitive is 'leather' चर्म the affix ढञ् will come after उपानह् debarring by anticipation the अञ् of V. 1. 15 S. 1677. Thus औपनाहेयं चर्म ॥
entries.note: Devanagari fragments and corrupt readings restored from context and vritti.

entries.english:
1677. The affix अञ् comes, in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product, after a word expressing the product of leather.
The word चर्मणः in the aphorism is in the genitive case. This अञ् debars छ । Thus वार्ध्रं चर्म and वारत्रं चर्म a leather serviceable for making a 'vardhra' and 'vâratra' i. e. a leather thong.
entries.note: SK number misprinted/OCR-read as 1477, corrected to 1677.

entries.english:
1678. The above mentioned affixes come after a word in the first case in construction, with the force of a genitive or a locative, when the word in the first case is agent of the verb 'syât' ;—in other words— the above-mentioned affixes have also the sense of 'very well sufficient thereto' and 'very well sufficient to be made therein'.
Note:—The word तत् shows that the word in construction must be in the first case, the words अस्य 'of it' and अस्मिन् 'in it' show the senses of the affix, the word स्यात् 'it can be' qualifies the primitive, the word इति is for the sake of distinctness.
Thus प्राकार आसाम् इष्टकानां स्यात् = प्राकारीया इष्टका 'the bricks sufficient to raise a wall'. So also प्रासादीयं दारु ॥ Similarly प्राकारोऽस्मिन् देशे स्यात् = प्राकारीयो देशः 'place sufficient to make a wall therein', प्रासादीया भूमिः ॥
Note:—The word स्यात् being in the Potential Mood (विधि) of अस् 'to be', has the force of potentiality, sufficiency as given in Sutras III. 3. 154. S. 2811 &c. Such as when the large number of bricks makes it possible to raise a wall, we say प्राकार आसाम् इष्टकानां स्यात् ॥ Similarly when the quality (गुण) of a land, such as its area, situation &c., makes it possible to erect a palace therein, we say, प्रासादोऽस्मिन् देशे स्यात् ॥
In the examples under this sutra, there is no modification (विकार) of the primitive (प्रकृति) into a product, as was the case under sutra V. 1. 12 S. 1674. The examples under this sutra show merely the adequacy, fitness or 'sufficiency' of a thing for a certain purpose. Here lies the difference between this sutra and the previous ones.
The repetition of the word तत् twice in this sutra shows the existence of the Grammatical maxim अनेकस्मिन् प्रत्ययार्थे प्रत्येकं समर्थविभक्तिः संबध्यते 'when the sense of an affix is more than one, the case in construction to which the affix must be added must be shown in each case'.
Why there is no affixing in this case प्रासादो देवदत्तस्य स्यात् ? The use of इति in the Sutra would prevent this, the force of इति being that the classical usage must be looked to in forming these derivatives.

1679. The affix ढञ् comes, after the word 'parikhâ' in the above senses of 'this is sufficient for that', and 'this is sufficient therein'.
This debars छ । Thus पारिखी भूमिः 'land sufficient to make a moat thereon'.
Up to this Sûtra was the governing force of the affixes छ and ढञ्. Hereafter another affix will be taught.
Here ends the chapter on छ and ढञ् affixes.

1680. Upto Sûtra V. 1. 115 S. 1778. (excluding that) the affix ठञ् bears rule.
Note:—The affix ठञ् governs all the succeeding sûtras upto तेन तुल्यं क्रिया चेद्वतिः, and has the senses given to it in Sutras V. 1. 37 S. 1702 &c. Strictly speaking the affix governs only upto V. 1. 110 S. 1773 and not upto 115. Thus in V. 1. 72, the affix ‹?› must be read; as पारायणिकः, तैत्तिरायणिकः, चान्द्रायणिकः ॥

1681. Upto Sûtra V. 1. 63 S. 1728 inclusive, the affix ठक् bears rule, with the exception of the word 'gopuchchha', or a Numeral, or a word denoting a measure of capacity.
Note:—Strictly speaking ठक् governs upto sûtra V. 1. 65 S. 1730. The word आर्हात् is made up of आ + अर्हात्. The force of आ here is अभिविधि or inclusive, so that in the Sûtra तदर्हति (V. 1. 63.) also, the ठक् will be employed. This affix ठक् debars ठञ् ॥ The sense will be the same as given in V. 1. 37 S. 1702 &c. the difference between ठक् and ठञ् being in accent only. Thus शतेन क्रीतं शतिकम् । So also ‹?› ॥

1682. The affix ठक् comes after the words निष्क &c., when they are not parts of a compound, the sense of the affix being that taught in the subsequent sutras upto V. 1. 63, S. 1702.
The word आर्हात् is understood in the sutra also. This ठक् debars ठञ्. Thus नैष्किकः ॥

But when it is a part of a compound, then the word निष्क will take the affix ठञ् ॥

Thus परमनिष्क + ठञ् ॥ Here applies the following rule.

Note:— The following seven are nishkadi words:— 1 निष्क, 2 पण, 3 पाद, 4 माष, 5. वाह, 6. द्रोण, 7 षष्टि ॥ Drona denotes measure, shashti denotes numeral and would have taken ‹?› ॥
entries.note: Continuation tail from preceding page; embedded Devanagari restored from context.

entries.english:
1683. After a numeral, the first vowel of a word denoting mass in its widest sense (with the exception of शाण) gets the Vriddhi before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण्, or क्, when the word so formed does not mean a Name.

Thus परमनैष्किक ॥

The words 'asamase etc when they are not parts of a compound' of the last sutra are jnapaka indicating that in the preceding sutras the tadanta-vidhi applied. Thus we have not only गव्यम्, but सुगव्यम् also (V. 1. 2. § 1662), not only अपूप्यम् but यथापूप्यम् also (V. 1. 4. § 1664). But in the sutras that follow, the tadanta-vidhi applies only when the first member of the compound is a numeral, and that too when there is no luk-elision of the affix. As पारायणिक and द्वैपारायणिकः ॥ (But when not preceded by a numeral, the tadanta vidhi does not apply as परमपारायणं वर्तयति ।) Why do we say 'when there is no luk'? Observe द्वाभ्यां शूर्पाभ्यां क्रीतं = द्विशूर्पम् ॥ द्विशूर्पेण क्रीतं = द्विशौर्पिकम् with ठञ् (V. 1. 26. § 1691), not अण् ॥

Why do we say 'when it is not a name'? Observe पञ्चकलापिकम् ॥ It has taken the affix ठञ् by V. 1. 57. § 1723.

Note:— The word परिमाण in this sutra has its technical signification, and not its etymological sense. Technically परिमाण does not include संख्या, etymologically it does. Panini has used this word परिमाण in some sutras in its technical sense, in others in its etymological sense. Thus in sutras IV. 1. 22. § 480, and V. 1. 19. § 1681 the technical sense is taken, while in sutras IV. 3. 156, § 1534 and V. 1. 57. § 1723 the etymological sense is meant. Technically परिमाण means सर्वतो मानं or a measure of capacity, and surface, namely length and breadth and height or depth, such as प्रस्थ &c. i.e. a cubic measure and a square measure. In this sense it is to be distinguished from the measures of length or lineal measure technically called आयाम as a वितस्ति 'a cubit' &c., on the one side, and the measures of weight, technically called उन्मान such as तुला &c. on the other side. In short उन्मान means a measure of weight or gravity, परिमाण means a measure of volume or capacity, आयाम means a lineal measure, and संख्या is beyond all these.

Note 2.— Is not the employment of the word असमासे in the Sutra redundant? For by the maxim ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति "that which cannot possibly be anything but a pratipadika, does not, contrary to I. 1. 72, § 26, denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself;" the pratipadika निष्क being especially mentioned in the sutra, the rule will apply to the word निष्क and not to a word ending with निष्क ।

A.— The employment of the word असमासे in this Sutra, indicates by implication (jnapaka), that in spite of the above maxim, the I. 1. 72. § 26 applies to the previous sutra, while in the subsequent sutras it does not. As उगवादिभ्यो यत् (V. 1. 2, § 1662) the यत् applies not only to गो &c. but to words ending in गो &c. As गव्यम् and सुगव्यम्, अतिसुगव्यम् । Not only अपूप्यम्, अपूपीयम् (V. 1. 4. § 1664) but also यथापूप्यम्, यथापूपीयम् । Not only दन्त्यम् (V. 1. 6. § 1666) but also राजदन्त्यम् ॥

While in the sutras subsequent to this V. 1. 20, § 1682 the tadanta-vidhi applies only to words preceded by a Sankhya and that also in Sutras upto V. 1. 116. § 1778 and not thereafter as, पारायणिकः and द्वैपारायणिकः (V. 1. 72. § 1726). Even in this latter case, when an affix is elided by luk the tadanta-vidhi does not apply. Thus द्वाभ्यां शूर्पाभ्यां क्रीतं = द्वि + शूर्प + अञ् (V. 1. 18. § 1680) = द्विशूर्पम्, (the affix being elided by V. 1. 28. § 1693). Now in forming a tertiary derivative from this word द्विशूर्प, the tadanta-vidhi will not apply. Thus द्विशूर्पेण क्रीतं, here what affix are we to subjoin? If tadanta-vidhi applied, we get the affix ठञ् (V. 1. 26. § 1691) in the alternative. But tadanta-vidhi not applying, we get the general affix अण् V. 1. 18. § 1669, and have द्विशौर्पिकम् । Here the affix is not elided by V. 1. 28, § 1693 as there is no Dvigu compounding. The above rule is summarised in the following ishti: परिमाणे संख्यापूर्वाणामेव तदन्तानामिष्यते तच्चालुकि ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari restored from clear context.

entries.english:
1684. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण्, or क्, the Vriddhi is substituted for the first vowel of the second member, denoting a mass in its widest sense, when the word अर्ध precedes it, but optionally for the first vowel of अर्ध ॥

As अर्धप्रस्थिकम्, आर्धप्रस्थिकम् with ठञ् (V. 1. 18.).

Why do we say when denoting a mass? Observe only अर्धकौशम् (अर्धक्रोशः प्रयोजनमस्य) ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari restored from clear context and vritti.

entries.english:
1685. When the first vowel of the second member preceded by अर्ध and denoting mass is short अ, the Vriddhi is not substituted for this, before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण्, or क्; and optionally so for the first vowel of the first member (i. e. अर्ध) ॥

Thus अर्धप्रस्थिकः or आर्धप्रस्थिकः (V. 1. 18. § 1680) ॥ अर्धकंसिकः or आर्धकंसिकः ॥ Why do we say 'when it is a short अ'? Observe आर्धकौडविकम् ॥ Why 'short अ'? Observe अर्धखार्यां भवा अर्धखारी ॥ Here Vriddhi is substituted for the आ of खारी, and though the form remains the same, the power of this word is changed. For अर्धखारी being formed by a Taddhita affix causing Vriddhi, in forming a Bahuvrihi compound, this word will retain its feminine form and will not be changed into masculine under VI. 3. 39. § 840, as अर्धखारीभार्यः (अर्धखारी भार्या यस्य) (वृद्धिनिमित्तस्य च तद्धितस्य &c.).

Note:— Wherever Vriddhi is prohibited with regard to a Taddhita affix, that affix cannot be called वृद्धिनिमित्त, and a word formed with such an affix will become masculine in a Bahuvrihi compound referring to a male person. वैयाकरणी भार्या अस्य = वैयाकरणभार्यः ॥ The word वैयाकरण is formed by prohibition of Vriddhi. See VII. 3. 3.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari restored from clear context.

entries.english:
1686. The affix ठन् and यत् come in the senses taught upto V. 1. 63 § 1728 after the word शत when it is not a part of a compound, and when it does not mean merely a 'hundred'.

The word आहीय V. 1. 19 § 1681 is understood here also. These affixes ठन् and यत् debar the affix कन् V. 1. 22 § 1687. Thus शतेन क्रीतं = शत्यम् or शतिकम् 'purchased for a hundred gold coins'.

Why do we say अशते 'when not meaning merely a hundred'? Observe शतं परिमाणमस्य = शतकः सङ्घः 'a band whose measure is hundred'. The word अशते qualifies the sense of the affix and not that of the base, the latter not being possible for the word शत as a base must always mean 'a hundred'. The following examples will illustrate the meaning; शतमध्यायाः परिमाणमस्य ग्रन्थस्य
entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page 867; continued on next page.

entries.english:
शतक a book consisting of hundred Adhyayas. In this case there is essentially no difference between the base (prakriti) and the sense of the affix (pratyayârtha), though there is apparent difference, for the sake of applying the affix. For शतक is a book essentially consisting of hundred, while शत्यं a carriage purchased for a hundred coins, does not contain hundred as its essential part. Similarly शतको गोसंघः 'a herd of cows hundred in number.' Here the संघः essentially consists of शत and so there is the affix कन् and not छन् or वन् (V. 1. 58). But not so in the case of वात्यः शाटकशतः, पांत्यः शाटकशतः, for here the sense of the affix is formed by the sentence and not discovered merely from the word. Hence the following Vârtika शतप्रतिषेधेऽन्यशतत्वेऽप्रतिषेधः ॥

The word च in the sûtra draws in the word असमासे from the previous sûtra. Thus ‹?› 'purchased for a hundred and two coins'. Here the affix is कन् V. 1. 22 S. 1687 so द्विशतकम् ॥ According to the Ishti given in the Sûtra VII. 3. 17. S. 1683 the tadanta-vidhi applies here.
entries.note: Tail continuation of SK 1686; embedded Devanagari partially corrupted in scan.

entries.english:
1687. The affix kan comes after a Numeral, when it does not end with ति or शत्, the sense of the affix being that taught hereafter upto V. 1. 63. S. 1728.

The word प्राग् is to be read into this sûtra also. The word संख्या is defined in I. 1. 23 S. 258. This कन् debars ठञ् ॥ Thus पञ्चभिः क्रीतः पञ्चकः । बहुकः । गणकः ॥

Why do we say when it does not end in ति or शत् ? Observe साप्ततिकः, चत्वारिंशत्कः formed by ठन् ॥

1688. The affix 'kan' coming after a Numeral ending with वत् takes optionally the augment इट्, the sense of the affix being those given upto V. 1. 62.

The words ending in वत् are संख्या; see I. 1. 23 and would consequently take कन् by V. 1. 22. The present sûtra ordains the optional affixing of इट् to this कन् ॥ Thus तावत्कः or तावतिकः ॥

1689. The affix ड्वुन् comes in the senses taught upto V. 1. 63 S. 1728 after the words 'Viñśati' and 'triñśat', when it does not denote a Name: and the ति and शत् of the base are dropped before this affix.

The affix कन् will be added by dividing the sûtra into two viz. (1) विंशतित्रिंशद्भ्याम् (2) असंज्ञायाम् the meanings being (1) the affix 'kan' is added to viñśati and triñśat, (2) the affix ḍvun is added to the same words, when not denoting a name.

Thus विंशति + ड्वुन् = विंश + अक (VI. 4. 142 S. 844) = विंशकः । त्रिंशत् + ड्वुन् = त्रिंश + अक (VI. 4. 143 S. 316) = त्रिंशकः ॥

When denoting a Name विंशतिकः, त्रिंशत्कः formed by affix कन् V. 1. 22.

1690. The affix टिठन् comes in the senses taught upto V. 1. 63 S. 1728 after the word कंस ॥

This debars ठञ्, the anubandha ट् of टिठन् shows that the feminine of the word will be formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 15 S. 470). The इ of it is for the sake of pronunciation, the ण् of टिठन् is for accent (VI. 1. 197 S. 3686). Thus कंसिकः fem. कंसिकी ॥

Vârt:— So also it must be stated after the word अर्ध; e.g. अर्धिकः, अर्धिकी ॥

Vârt:— So also after the word कार्षापण, e.g. कार्षापणिकः fem. कार्षापणिकी ॥ Sometimes the word प्रतिक is substituted for कार्षापण before this affix, as प्रतिकः, fem. प्रतिकी ॥

1691. The affix अञ् comes optionally in the senses taught upto V. 1. 63, S. 1728 after the word 'śûrpa'.

This debars ठञ् which comes in the alternative. As, शूर्पेण क्रीतः = शौर्पम् or शौर्पिकम् ॥

1692. The affix अण् comes in the senses taught upto V. 1. 63, S. 1728 after the words 'Satamâna', 'viñśatika', 'sahasra', and 'vasana'.

This debars ठञ्, ठक् and कन् ॥ Thus शतमानेन क्रीतं = शातमानम्, so also वैंशतिकम्, साहस्रम् and वासनम् ॥

1693. The affix having the senses taught upto V. 1. 63 S. 1728, is elided by लुक्, after a stem beginning with the word adhyardha, and after a Dvigu compound, when it is not a Name.

The word अण् is understood here also. Thus अध्यर्धकंसम्, द्विकंसम्, अध्यर्धशूर्पम्, द्विशूर्पम्, त्रिकंसम्, त्रिशूर्पम् ॥ Here the affixes टिठन् and अञ् are elided.

Note:— Though in the word द्विशूर्पम् &c. the affix is elided, it is only so when the affixing of the taddhita occasions a Dvigu compounding (II. 1. 51. S. 728) such as in द्वाभ्यां शूर्पाभ्यां क्रीतः = द्विशूर्पम् ॥ Here the resultant is a Dvigu compound. But in forming tertiary derivatives the affix is not elided, as द्विशूर्पेण क्रीतं द्विशौर्पिकम् ॥ Hence the following rule: द्विगोर्लुकि तन्निमित्तग्रहणम् ॥ See IV. 1. 88, V. 1. 28.

Why do we say असंज्ञायाम् 'when not a Name'? Observe पाञ्चलोहितिकम् or ‹?› and पाञ्चकलापिकम् being names of certain measures. The feminine word लोहिनी is changed into the masculine by the Vârtika ‹?› given under VI. 3. 35. The lohitâ is the red seed with which gold &c. is weighed.

Note:— The word अध्यर्ध is a Sankhyâ (See I. 1. 23. S. 258) and a word beginning with it will be a Dvigu compound. Its separate mention in this sûtra may appear superfluous. It is however so mentioned, in order to indicate (jñâpaka) that this word is not always a Sankhyâ. Thus for the purposes of the application of the affix कृत्वसुच् (V. 4. 17. S. 2035) this word is not a sankhyâ.

1694. The affix having the senses taught up to V. 1. 63. S. 1728 is optionally luk-elided, after the words kârshâpana, and sahasra, when they are preceded by adhyardha or are members of a Dvigu compound.

This sûtra makes the elision optional, when it was compulsory by the last sûtra. Thus अध्यर्धकार्षापणम् or अध्यर्धकार्षापणीकम्, द्विकार्षापणम् or द्विकार्षापणीकम् here the affix ठन् (V. 1. 25 S. 1690) is elided in one case, and not elided in the other. When it is not elided, प्रति may be substituted for कार्षापण (V. 1. 25. S. 1690) अध्यर्द्धप्रतिकम् प्रतिकम् ॥
So also after the word सहस्र. e.g. अध्यर्द्धसहस्रम् or अध्यर्द्धसाहस्रम् द्विसहस्रम् or द्विसाहस्रम् || When the affix is not elided, the forms above shown with the irregular Vriddhi of the second stem, are evolved by sûtra VII. 3. 15. S. 1752.

1695. The Arhîya-affix (V. 1. 68. S. 1728) is optionally elided after a Dvigu occasioning compound, of the word nishka, preceded by dvi and tri.
The word द्विगोः 'a taddhita occasioning a Dvigu compound' of V. 1. 28, S. 1693 is to be read into this sûtra. Thus द्विनिष्कम् or द्विनैष्किकम्, त्रिनिष्कम् or त्रिनैष्किकम् (VII. 3. 17. S. 1683).
Vart:— So also when nishka is preceded by बहु e.g. बहुनिष्कम् or बहुनैष्किकम् ॥ The irregular Vriddhi of the second term is caused by VII. 3. 17.
entries.note: SK number misprinted as 1665 in Devanagari line; embedded Devanagari restored from context.

entries.english:
1696. The ârhîya-affix (V. 1. 37-63) occasioning a Dvigu compound is optionally elided after the word bista, preceded by dvi or tri.
The word च in the sûtra draws in the words द्वित्रिपूर्वात् । Thus द्विबिस्तम् or द्विवैस्तिकम् ॥
Note :— The separation of this sûtra is for the sake of the subsequent sûtra.
entries.note: SK number misprinted as 1666 in Devanagari line; embedded Devanagari restored.

entries.english:
1697. The affix kha (ख) comes in the Arhîya senses (V. 1. 37-68) after the word viñśatika when preceded by the word adhyardha or a Numeral, occasioning a Dvigu.
Thus अध्यर्धविंशतिकीनम् द्विविंशतिकीनम् ॥
Note :— Being especially ordained, this affix is not elided by V. 1. 28.
entries.note: Misprinted as 1667 in text heading, Devanagari line, and running head; sequence requires 1697.

entries.english:
1698. The affix îkan comes in the Arhîya senses (V. 1. 37-63), after the word khârî, when preceded by the word adhyardha or a Numeral occasioning a Dvigu.
Thus अध्यर्धखारीकम्, द्विखारीकम् ॥
Vart :— So also after the word खारी alone, as खारीकम् ॥
entries.note: Devanagari line and running head misprint SK number as 1668; heading text correctly gives 1698.

entries.english:
1699. The affix yat comes in the ârhîya senses (V. 1. 37-63) after the words paņa, pâda, mâsha and śata when preceded by the word adhyardha, or a Numeral occasioning a Dvigu.
Thus अध्यर्धपण्यम्, द्विपण्यम्, so also अध्यर्धपाद्यम्, द्विपाद्यम् ॥ Here पाद् is not changed to पद् by VI. 4. 130. S. 414, because the elided अ of पाद is sthânivat. Thus द्विपाद + यत् = द्विपाद + 0 (loped by यस्येति च VI. 4. 148, S. 311) + यत् ॥ This lopa elided अ becomes sthânivat and द्विपाद is not considered as ending in पाद् but पाद and so VI. 4. 130 S. 414 does not apply.
Nor is पाद not changed into पद्, by VI. 3. 53. S. 991. The substitution enjoined by VI. 3. 53 takes place when पाद means the foot of a living being, while here it means a measure of capacity.
entries.note: SK number misprinted as 1696 in Devanagari line; embedded grammatical steps restored from context.

entries.english:
1700. The affix यत् comes optionally after the word śâņa in the ârhîya-senses (V. 1. 63), when it is preceded by the word adhyardha or a Numeral occasioning a Dvigu.
This debars ठञ् which also comes in the alternative, and is then elided by V. 1. 28 S. 1693. Thus अध्यर्धशाण्यम् or अध्यर्धशाणम् ॥

1701. The affix अण् as well as 'yat' optionally also comes after the word śâņa, in the ârhîya-senses (V. 1. 37-63) when preceded by the words द्वि and त्रि.
The यत् comes optionally by the last sûtra and is also drawn into this by the word च. Thus we have three forms, द्वैशाणम्, द्विशाण्यम् and द्विशाणम् ॥
Note :— The irregular Vriddhi of the second term in cases of compounds of numerals, taught in VII. 3. 15-17 S. 1752, 1754, 1688, does not however take place in the case of this word being especially excluded from the operation of those rules, see VII. 3. 17. The Vriddhi here is regular as taught by the general rule VII. 2. 117.
Thus in the preceding sûtras V. 1. 18 to V. 1. 36 thirteen affixes have been taught, but the meaning of those affixes have not been given, nor the construction of the words to which they are to be added. In the following sûtras are given the meanings and the construction.
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari restored from Sanskrit vritti and clear surrounding context.

entries.english:
1702. The thirteen affixes taught in V. 1. 18-36, have the sense of "purchased with this price" and are added to a word in the third case in construction.
The thirteen affixes ‹?› have already been taught. Now is taught their sense, and the case construction of the word to which they should be added. The तेन shows that the words must be in the 3rd case in construction and क्रीतम् shows that the sense is that of 'purchased'. The illustrations have already been given in the previous sûtras. Some more may be mentioned here. Thus गोपुच्छेन क्रीतं गौपुच्छिकम्, (the accent falling on गौ); so also with words denoting Numbers and Measures, as सप्तत्या क्रीतं साप्ततिकम्, प्रास्थिकम्, नैष्किकम् ॥
entries.note: Garbled list of 13 affixes replaced with placeholder; embedded Devanagari restored from Sanskrit vritti.

entries.english:
1703. The short इ is substituted in the place of goņî, when the Taddhita affix is elided by luk.
By the sûtra I. 2. 49. S. 1408 when a Taddhita is elided, the long ई of the feminine also required elision. But this rule makes an exception in favor of the word गोणी in which under similar circumstances the short replaces the long, as in the compound पञ्चगोणिः purchased for five goņis. Here the Taddhita suffix which conveys the meaning of "purchased," has been
entries.note: Entry text cut off at bottom of page 873.

entries.english:
rejected after गोणी by V. 1. 28. S. 1693 therefore by the previous sûtra, the feminine suffix ई also required rejection. But this sûtra intervenes and changes the long into short.
Note:— This sûtra is divided into two separate rules by the process called yoga-vibhâga. Thus ह्रस्व is made one sûtra by itself, and then it means, when there is a suppression of a Taddhita affix by लुक्, then the long ई is replaced by short. Thus purchased with five needles = पञ्चभिः सूचीभिः क्रीतः = ‹?›. This is restricted to such examples of purchase only.

1704. The above affixes have further the sense of "for its sake", when the meaning is a relation or an unwonted appearance.
The word तस्य shows that the word in construction must be in the 6th case, the word निमित्त 'cause or occasion' gives the sense of the affix; संयोग means 'a connection, or relation'; उत्पात means 'a portent indicative of good or bad luck'. Thus तस्य निमित्तं धनपतिना संयोगः = शात्यः 'a connection with a rich man for the sake of getting a hundred'. So also शातिकः, साहस्रः ॥ So also शतस्य निमित्तमुत्पातो दक्षिणाक्षिस्यन्दनम् शात्यम्, शातिकम्, साहस्रम् "the twitching of the right eye for the sake of a hundred" i. e. indicative of acquiring or losing a hundred, a thousand &c.
Vart:— The above affixes come after the words वात, पित्त, and श्लेष्म in the senses of allaying or vitiating. As वातिकम् 'allaying or vitiation of windy humour'. So also पैत्तिकम्, श्लैष्मिकम् ॥
Vart:— Also after the word सन्निपात, as, सान्निपातिकम् ॥

1705. After the word गो and after a word having two syllables, with the exception of a Numeral, or a Measure of capacity, or asva &c, the affix yat (यत्) is added, in the above sense of 'a relation or a portent for the purpose of that'.
This debars ठञ् ॥ As गोर्निमित्तं संयोग उत्पातो वा गव्यम् 'a connection or a portent for the sake of a cow.' So also after a word of two syllables, as, धन्यः, स्वर्ग्यः, यशस्यम् ॥
Why do we say "when not a word denoting a Numeral or a Measure of capacity or अश्व &c"? Observe पञ्चानां निमित्तं—पञ्चकम्, सप्तकम्, अष्टकम्, प्रास्थिकम्, खारीकम्, आश्विकः formed by V. 1. 22, 18, 19.
Vart:— The word ब्रह्मवर्चस् should be enumerated, e.g. ब्रह्मवर्चसस्य निमित्तं गुरुणा संयोगः = ब्रह्मवर्चस्यम् "relationship with a teacher in order to acquire Brahmavarchasa."
1 अश्व, 2 अश्मन्, 3 शया, 4 ऊर्जा, 5 उमा, 6 गङ्गा (भङ्ग भङ्गा), 7 वर्षा (वर्ष), 8 वसु ॥

1706. After the word putra, the affix chha (छ) also comes, as well as yat (यत्), in the above sense of 'a relation or a portent for the purpose of that.'
The word पुत्र being a dissyllabic word would always have taken यत् by the last aphorism. This ordains छ also. Thus पुत्रस्य निमित्तं संयोग उत्पातो वा पुत्रीयः or पुत्र्यः ॥

1707. The affixes अण् and अञ् are respectively added to the words sarvabhûmi and prithivî in the above mentioned sense of "a connection or a portent for its purpose".
This debars ठक् ॥ Thus सर्वभूमेर्निमित्तं संयोग उत्पातो वा सार्वभौमः, so also पार्थिवः ॥ In सार्वभौमः there is Vriddhi of both members of the compound by VII. 3. 20. S. 1438.

1708. To the same bases sarvabhumi and prithivi, are added the same affixes an and an respectively, in the sense of "lord thereof".
Note:— Thus सर्वभूमेरीश्वरः सार्वभौमः 'the lord of the whole earth', पार्थिवः 'the lord of the earth'.
Note:— The word तस्य, showing the genitive construction of the base, has been repeated in this sûtra, though its anuvritti was running into it from V. 1. 38 S. 1704 in order to show that the senses given in V. 1. 38 do not extend further. Had तस्य not been repeated here, the word ईश्वरः would have been an attribute, like the words संयोग and उत्पात, of the word निमित्त ॥

1709. To the same bases sarvabhumi and prithivi, being in the 7th case in construction, are added the same affixes an and an respectively, when the sense is that of "known therein".
The word विदित means known, published &c. सर्वभूमौ विदितः सार्वभौमः "known in the whole world". So also पार्थिवः ॥

1710. The affix thañ comes in the sense of 'known therein', after the words loka and sarvaloka, in the 7th case in construction.
Thus लोके विदितः = लौकिकः, सार्वलौकिकः । The irregular Vriddhi of both members takes place by VII. 3. 20 S. 1438.

1711. The above mentioned affixes (V. 1. 18 &c) come after a word in the sixth case in construction, in the sense of 'sown with so much'.
The word वाप means 'sown therein' i.e. a field. Thus प्रस्थस्य वापः क्षेत्रं प्रास्थिकम् 'sown with a Prastha', द्रौणिकम्, खारीकम् i.e. a field sown with a quantity of grain measuring a Prastha or a Drona or a Khari.

1712. The affix shthan comes in the sense of 'sown with so much', after the word patra.
This debars अण् ॥ The न् of ष्ठन् is for accent (VI. 1. 197, S. 3686), the ष् is for ङीष् (IV. 1. 41). The word पात्र denotes a measure of capacity. Thus पात्रस्य वापः पात्रिकं क्षेत्रम्, fem. पात्रिकी क्षेत्रभक्तिः ॥

1713. The above mentioned affixes have also the sense of "an interest, or a rent, or a profit, or a tax, or a bribe given thereby or in that". The affix is added to a word in the first case (प्रथमा) in construction. The sense of the affix is that of a locative (अस्मिन्). The word दीयते 'is given' in the singular number joins with each one of the words वृद्धि, आय &c. The sum paid by a debtor to his creditor over and above the principal, is called वृद्धि or interest. The share of profit taken by the landlord in villages &c. is called आय or rent. The increase over the capital by sale of cloth &c. is called लाभ or profit. The share of the king for protection &c. is called शुल्क or tax. The present or bribe is called उपदा ॥ Thus पञ्चास्मिन् वृद्धिर्वा आयो वा लाभो वा शुल्को = पञ्चकः 'that transaction &c. in which five per cent is given as interest, rent, profit, tax or bribe'. Similarly शत्यः, शतिकः, साहस्रः &c. Vart:— So also in the sense of a Dative. As पञ्चास्मै वृद्धिर्वा आयो वा लाभो वोपदा वा = पञ्चको देवदत्तः “Devadatta to whom five per cent is given as interest &c.” This Vartika may be redundant, if we take the locative as sometimes having the force of dative also. As in the sentence सममब्राह्मणे दानम् ॥
entries.note: Sutra line was printed on preceding page 876.

entries.english: 1714. The affix than comes in the same sense of "an interest, rent, profit, tax or bribe given thereby or therein" after a word denoting an ordinal, and after the word ardha. This debars ‹?› and ठञ् । Thus द्वितीयो वृद्ध्यादिरस्मिन् दीयते = द्वितीयकः, तृतीयिकः, पञ्चमिकः, सप्तमिकः, आर्धिकः । The word अर्ध is technically the name of रूपकार्थः ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari reconstructed from context.

entries.english: 1715. The affix yat (यत्) comes after the word bhāga in the sense of “an interest, rent, profit, tax or bribe given thereby or therein.” By the word च in the sūtra, ठन् also comes. This debars ‹?› । Thus भागो वृद्ध्यादिरस्मिन् दीयते = भाग्यम् or भागिकम् शतम्, भाग्या or भागिका विंशतिः ॥ The word भाग also denotes रूपकार्थम् ॥
entries.note: Embedded Devanagari reconstructed from context.

entries.english: 1716. The above mentioned affixes, after the word भार preceded by the word वंश &c., have the sense of 'who carries away, or conveys or brings that'. The case in construction here is accusative (द्वितीया) ॥ Thus वंशभारं हरति वहति आवहति वा = वांशभारिकः, ऐक्षुभारिकः ॥ According to another explanation, the phrase भाराद् वंशादिभ्यः is explained as भारभूतेभ्यो वंशादिभ्यः ॥ Then the sūtra will mean "the above named affixes come after वंश &c. when they denote a load". Thus भारभूतान् वंशान् हरति = वांशिकः, ऐक्षिकः ॥ Note:— The word हरति means 'to carry to another place or to steal'; वहति means 'to carry on one's back or head'; आवहति means 'to produce or bring'. 1 वंश, 2 कुटज, 3 बल्वज, 4 मूल, 5 स्थूणा, (स्थूल) 6 अक्ष, 7 अञ्जनम्, 8 ‹?›, 9 लक्षण, 10 खट्वा ॥

1717. The affixes than and kan come respectively after the words vasna and dravya, in the second case in construction, in the same sense of 'who carries &c'. Thus वस्नं हरति वहति वा = वास्निकः, द्रव्यकः ॥

1718. The above-mentioned affixes have also the sense of "what is capable of holding that; or takes away that, or cooks that." The word तद् is understood here, showing that the word in construction to which the affix is to be added should be in the accusative. The word सम्भव means the capacity to hold the exact quantity; अवहार means taking away, or containing. Thus प्रस्थं सम्भवति = प्रास्थिकः a vessel capable of holding a prastha measure. So प्रस्थमवहरति or पचति = प्रास्थिकी 'a vessel or a person that takes away, holds or cooks a Prastha measure.' Similarly खाडविकः, and खारीकः ॥ The word सम्भव does not govern the word पचति, thus प्रस्थं पचति ब्राह्मणी = प्रास्थिकी 'a Brāhmaṇī who cooks a Prastha.' Vart:— The affix अण् also comes after the word द्रोण in the sense of 'who cooks that', e.g. द्रोणं पचति ब्राह्मणी = द्रौणी or द्रौणिकी ॥

1719. The affix kha (ईन) may optionally be added in the above sense of 'being capable of holding' &c., after the words āḍhaka, āchita, and pātra. This debars ठञ् which comes in the alternative. Thus आढकं सम्भवति, अवहरति पचति वा = आढकीना or आढकिकी, आचितीना or आचितिकी, पात्रीणा or पात्रिकी ॥

1720. The affix shthan as well as the affix ख (ईन) may optionally come, after the same words āḍhaka, āchita, and pātra, being final of a Dvigu compound, the sense being that of 'what can hold,' &c. The ख is read into the sūtra by the word च of the aphorism. These two affixes ख and ष्ठन् being especially ordained, are not to be elided by V. 1. 28. S. 1693. But when, in the alternative, we add the general affix ठञ्, then it is elided by V. 1. 28. S. 1693. The ष् of ष्ठन् is for accent (VI. 1. 197. S. 2645), and the न् for ङीप् ॥ Thus we have 3 forms:— द्व्याढकिकी, द्व्याढकीना, or द्व्याढकी; द्व्याचितिकी, द्व्याचितीना, द्व्याचिता ॥ In this case of द्व्याचिता the feminine is not formed by ङीप् (IV. 1. 21. S. 479) because of the specific prohibition contained in IV. 1. 22. S. 480. So also द्विपात्रिकी, द्विपात्रीणा and द्विपात्री ॥
1721. After the word kulija, being the final of a Dvigu, there is optionally the elision of the above affixes, or
entries.note: Entry text cut off at end of batch.

entries.english:
the adding of the affix (इन), in the sense of 'what can hold that &c.'
By ‹?› the affix ठन् is also added. The elision being optional, the affix V. 1. 18 S. 1680 may optionally be elided by V. 1. 28 S. 1693. Thus we get four forms: द्विकुलिशिकी (न्), द्विकुलिशीना (ख), द्विकुलिशी (लुक्), कुलिशिकी (ठञ्). In the last example, there is not vṛiddhi of the second term, though it was so required by VII. 3. 17. S. 1683. The anomaly is explained by holding that the word कुलिश should be included in the exception along with संज्ञा and ज्ञाति of VII. 3. 17.
entries.note: Tail fragment continued from previous page.

entries.english:
1722. The affixes taught in V. 1. 18 S. 1680 &c have also the sense of 'this is his portion, price or pay.'
The सः shows that the case in construction is nominative. The word अंश means 'share', वस्न means 'price', भृति means 'wages'. Thus पञ्च अंशो वस्नो वा भृतिरस्य = पञ्चकः 'whose portion, price or pay is five.'

1723. The affixes V. 1. 18 S. 1680 &c have the sense of 'this is its measure.'
The word तत् shows that the word in construction should be in the nominative case. Thus प्रस्थः परिमाणमस्य प्रास्थिको राशिः 'a heap whose mass is a Prastha'. So also खारीकः, शूर्पिकः, पादिकः, मासिकः, द्रोणिकः, कौडविकः, सार्धशतिकः, याष्टिकः ॥ So also षष्टिरधिकं परिमाणमस्य = पाष्टिकं, द्विसाप्ततिकम् ॥
Note:—Why the words तदस्य have been repeated in this sûtra, when their anuvṛitti could have been drawn from the last aphorism, the word सोऽस्य and तदस्य being the same? The repetition shows that the affixes are again ordained, so that the elision taught in V. 1. 28 S. 1693 does not apply. Thus द्वे षष्टी अधिकं परिमाणमस्य = द्विषाष्टिकं, द्विसाप्ततिकम् ॥ Here the affix is not elided by V. 1. 28.

1724. The affixes V. 1. 18 S. 1680 &c come after a word denoting a numeral, in the sense of 'this is its measure,' when the word so formed means a Name, a Multitude, a Book, or a fixed way and mode of study.
The phrase तदस्य परिमाणम् is understood here. The word in construction to which the affix is to be added should be in the nominative case. When it is a Name, the affix does not change the sense of the radical. Thus पञ्च 'the Five' as पञ्चकाः शकुनयः; त्रिकाः 'the Three' 'शालङ्कायनाः ॥ The sense of the primitive is changed when it means a 'a multitude or flock' as पञ्चकः सङ्घः, अष्टकः ॥ So also when it means a सूत्र 'a Book', as अष्टावध्यायाः परिमाणमस्य सूत्रस्य = अष्टकं पाणिनीयम् 'The Ashtaka of Panini viz a Book comprising Eight Adhyâyas'. So also दशकं वैयाघ्रपदीयम्, त्रिकं काशकृत्स्नम् ॥ Is not a collection of Adhyâyas the same as सङ्घः? No, the word सङ्घः is confined to a collection of living beings only.
The word अध्ययन means 'study'. Its numerical measure (संख्यापरिमाण) means the particular number of times, or ways in which it should be read. Thus what is studied five times, or in five modes is पञ्चकम्; so also अष्टकम् or नवकम्.
Vart:—The affix ड comes after the words पञ्चदशन् &c, when the word means a Stoma. As, पञ्चदश मन्त्राः परिमाणमस्य = पञ्चदशः स्तोमः, सप्तदशः स्तोमः &c. The indicatory ड causes the elision of final (टि) by VI. 4. 143, S. 316 in the cases of words like पञ्चदशन् &c. In the case of एकविंश the final is elided by VI. 4. 144, S. 679. Stoma is the praise-hymn sung by the Chhandoga priests at the soma-sacrifice. A triad of verses by repetition becomes 15, 17 &c. Thus in sapta dasa stoma the last verse of the triad is repeated seven times, the other two five times each, thus we have seventeen verses. Similarly when every verse of the triad is recited five times, we have pancha-dasa stoma. When every verse of the triad is recited seven times, it becomes eka vimsa stoma &c.
entries.note: Entry spans page 880 to page 881; misprinted SK number 1893 corrected to 1680 in cross-reference.

entries.english:
1725. The following words are anomalous: paṅkti 'a verse', vinśati 'twenty', trinśat 'thirty', chatvârinśat 'forty', pañchâśat 'fifty', shashṭi 'sixty', saptati 'seventy', aśîti 'eighty', navati 'ninety', and śata 'a hundred'.
Note:—The words तदस्य परिमाणम् are understood here also: पंक्ति is formed by adding क्तिन् to पञ्चन् the final being elided, meaning 'a verse the measure of which is five', i.e. a half quarter consisting of 5 syllables. The word विंशति is formed by adding शति to the word द्वि which replaces the two words द्वौ दशतौ as द्वौ दशतौ परिमाणमस्य संघस्य विंशतिः ॥ So the affix शत् comes after त्रिन् representing त्रयो दशतः; so for चतस्रो दशतौ we have चत्वारि and then add शत्, similarly with पञ्चाशत् ॥ Similarly with the rest.
Note:—All the rest appears to be the conjectural etymology of Patanjali and Kâśikâ-Kâra, and hence it is omitted.
Note:—The word पंक्ति also means a line. As ब्राह्मणपंक्तिः, पिपीलिकापंक्तिः ॥ Here the sense has no relation to its etymology.
entries.note: Entry spans page 881 to page 882; corrupt Devanagari in etymological notes reconstructed from context.

entries.english:
1726. The words pañchat and daśat in combination with varga, may be anomalously so formed, in the sense of 'this is its measure'.
This ordains अति instead of कन् V. 1. 22, which also comes in the alternative. As पञ्चद्वर्गः, दशद्वर्गः; or पञ्चको वर्गः, दशको वर्गः ॥

1727. The affix ḍan comes after the words trinśat and chatvârinśat, in the sense of 'this is its measure', when it is the Name denoting a Brâhmaṇa-book.
The word वर्ग does not govern this sûtra. The indicatory ङ् causes the elision of the last vowel with the consonant that follows it (VI. 4. 143. S. 316). The force of the locative case in ब्राह्मणे is that of अभिधेय and not विषय, i.e., when the word means a Brâhmaṇa itself. Had the force been that of विषय, it would have meant, in the Brâhmaṇa literature. As त्रिंशदध्यायाः परिमाणमेषां ब्राह्मणानां = त्रैंशानि ब्राह्मणानि 'The Brâhmaṇa containing thirty Adhyâyas'. So चात्वारिंशानि ब्राह्मणानि ॥ These are the names of certain Brâhmaṇas.

1728. The affixes V. 1. 18. S. 1680 &c, have also the sense of 'who deserves that'.
The case in construction here is accusative. Thus श्वेतच्छत्त्रमर्हति = श्वाच्छत्त्रिकः 'who deserves the White Umbrella'.
1729. After the words छेद &c in the second case in construction, the above-mentioned affixes have the sense of 'who deserves that under all circumstances'.
entries.note: Entry text cut off at end of batch.

entries.english:
Thus छेदं नित्यमर्हति = छेदिकः, so also वैरािकः ॥

1 ..., 2 ..., 3 ..., 4 ..., 5 नर्त (वर्त ), 6 कर्ष, 7 सीर्य, 8 संप्रयोग, 9 विग, 10 प्रयाग, 11 विप्रकर्ष, 12 प्रेषण, 13 सम्मर्ष, 14 विप्रमर्ष, 15 विकर्ष, 16 प्रकर्ष, 17 विराम, विरव (from ‹?› is formed ‹?›) ॥
entries.note: Continuation tail of SK 1729 from previous page; gaṇa items fragmentary in OCR.

entries.english:
1730. The affix yat as well as the above affixes come after the word śīrshachchheda in the accusative, in the sense of 'who deserves that under all circumstances'.

Thus शिरश्छेदं नित्यमर्हति = शीर्षच्छेद्यः, or शीर्षच्छेदिकः ॥ The word शिरस् is changed irregularly into शीर्ष before the affix.

1731. After the words daṇḍa &c in the accusative, the affix yat comes in the sense of 'who deserves that'.

The word नित्य does not govern this sutra. This affix debars ठक् V. 1. 19. S. 1681. Thus दण्डमर्हति = दण्ड्यः 'deserving to be killed' अर्घ्यः वध्यः ॥

1 दण्ड, 2 मुसल, 3 मधुपर्क, 4 कक्षा, 5 अर्घ, 6 मेघ, 7 मेधा, 8 सुवर्ण, 9 उदक, 10 वध, 11 युग, 12 शन्न, 13 भाग, 14 इभ, 15 भङ्ग, 16 ‹?›

Note:—The Kāśikā gives the sutra as दण्डादिभ्यो यः ; another version gives the sutra as दण्डादिभ्यः only drawing the affix यत् from the last sutra.

1732. The affix ghañ together with yat comes in the sense of "deserving that", after the word pātra.

This debars ठन् and ठञ् ॥ The word पात्र denotes measure also. Thus पात्रमर्हति = पात्र्यः or पात्रीयः ॥

1733. The affix chhañ (ईय) as well as yat (य) comes in the sense of 'deserving that', after the words kaḍaṅkara and dakshiṇā.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus कडङ्करमर्हति = कडङ्करीयः or कडङ्कर्यः 'one deserving straw' such as a cow. So also दक्षिणीयः or दक्षिण्यो ब्राह्मणः 'a Brāhmaṇa deserving alms.'

1734. The affixes chha (ईय) and yat (य) come in the sense of 'deserving that', after the word sthālībila.

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus स्थालीबिलीयास्तण्डुलाः or स्थालीबिल्याः 'rice deserving the pot' i.e. cookable rice.

1735. The affixes gha and खञ् come respectively after the words yajña and ṛitvij, in the sense of 'deserving that.'

This debars ठक् ॥ Thus यज्ञियो ब्राह्मणः 'a Brāhmaṇa worthy of honor at a sacrifice.' आर्त्विजीनो ब्राह्मणः ॥

Vārt:—After the words yajña and ṛitvij, these affixes have also the sense of "deserving the performance thereof". Thus यज्ञमर्हति = यज्ञियो देशः 'a place fit for the performance of sacrifice.' ऋत्विजं कर्मार्हति = आर्त्विजीनो ब्राह्मणः ॥

Here ends the governing power of अर्हति V. 1. 19. S. 1681 henceforward is the government of ठञ् V. 1. 18.

1736. The affix thañ comes in the sense of 'who performs this', after the words pārāyaṇa, turāyaṇa and chāndrāyaṇa being in the 2nd case in construction.

The force of अर्हति ceases. Thus पारायणिकश्छात्रः 'a pupil, who reads under a teacher' : तैरयणिको यजमानः, चान्द्रायणिकस्तपस्वी ॥ The word पारायण means a teacher, (परस्य करोति) ।

1737. The affix thañ comes after the word saṁśaya in the accusative construction, the sense being "fallen into this, or thrown into it".

Thus संशयमापन्नः प्राप्तः सांशयिकः स्थाणुः "doubtful pillar", i.e. in a precarious state.

सांशयिकः ॥

1738. The affix thañ comes in the sense of 'who goes', after the word yojana in the accusative construction.

Thus योजनं गच्छति = यौजनिकः ॥

Vārt:—So also after the words क्रोशशत and योजनशत ॥ As क्रोशशतिकः, योजनशतिकः ॥

Vārt:—The affix after these two words means also "who is worthy to be approached from so far". As क्रोशशतादभिगमनमर्हति क्रोशशतिको भिक्षुः, योजनशतिक आचार्यः ॥

entries.note: Entry cut off at end of batch; sutra and vritti line printed at bottom of page 885, English heading begins on page 886.

entries.english:
1739. The affix shkan comes in the same sense of 'who goes there', after the word patha, being in the 2nd case in construction.
Of the affix ष्कन्, ष् is for ङीष् (IV. 1. 41 S. 498) and न् for accent (VI. 1. 197 S. 3686). As पन्थानं गच्छति = पथिकः fem. पथिकी ॥
entries.note: Sutra line was on preceding page; English heading begins at top of page 886

entries.english:
1740. The affix ṇa comes after the word pantha which becomes the substitute of pathin, the sense of the affix being "who always goes".
The word qualifies the sense of the affix. Thus पन्थानं नित्यं गच्छति = पान्थः as पान्थो भिक्षां याचते ॥ Why नित्यं ? See पथिकः ॥

1741. The affix ठञ् comes after the word uttara-patha in the third case in construction, in the sense of 'who passes by that way' 'what is conveyed by that way.'
The construction of the sūtra shows that the base must be in the 3rd case. The word च shows that the word गच्छति 'who passes by that way' should also be read into the aphorism. Thus उत्तरपथेनाहृतम् = औत्तरपथिकम् or उत्तरपथेन गच्छति औत्तरपथिकः ॥
Vart:— So also after the word पथ preceded by the words वारि, जङ्गल, स्थल, कान्तार the affix has the sense of conveyed by that way or passing by that way. As वारिपथेनाहृतम् = वारिपथिकम्, वारिपथेन गच्छति वारिपथिकः masculine or neuter according as the affix means conveyed or passing.

1742. In the following sutras, the phrase "after a word denoting time" should be supplied to complete the sense.
The word कालात् bears rule in the following aphorisms up to V. 1. 97. S. 1761 exclusive. Thus the next sūtra तेन निर्वृत्तम् means 'accomplished by means thereof'. We must read the word कालात् into it. As मासेन निर्वृत्तम् = मासिकम् &c.

1743. The affix than comes after a word denoting time, being in the third case in construction, in the sense of "to be accomplished by that time".
Thus अह्ना निर्वृत्तम् = आह्निकम् "to be accomplished in a day" i.e. a certain portion of reading &c., आर्धमासिकम्, सांवत्सरिकम् ॥

1744. The above-named affixes come after a word expressing time, in the accusative case in construction, in the sense of “solicited to instruct for such a period,” “hired for such a period,” “which had lasted for such a period,” or “which will last so long”.
The word अधीष्ट means "honorary office", therefore 'one solicited to teach, but who accepts no pay' III. 3. 161, भृतः means "engaged on wages", भूतः means 'the time pervaded or occupied by its existence', and भावी the same as last in the future. The word denoting time will be in the second case by II. 3. 5 S. 558. Thus मासमधीष्टः = मासिकोऽध्यापकः, so also मासं भृतः = मासिकः कर्मकरः, मासं भूतः = मासिको व्याधिः, मासं भावी = मासिक उत्सवः ॥

1745. The affixes yat and khañ come after the word māsa, in denoting 'age'.
This debars ठञ् ॥ The word भूतः of the previous sūtra should be read into this. Thus मासं भूतः = मास्यः or मासीनः ‘a month old’.
Note:— Why do we say when denoting 'age'? Observe मासिकः ॥

1746. The affix yap comes after the word māsa when forming a Dvigu compound, and meaning 'age'.
Thus द्वौ मासौ भूतः = द्विमास्यः ॥

1747. After the word shanmāsa, come the affixes nyat as well as यप् and ठञ्, in the sense of 'age'.
The word vayasi is understood here. So also the affix यप् ॥ By force of च we draw in ठञ् also.
Thus षाण्मास्यः, षण्मास्यः, and षाण्मासिकः ॥

1748. The affix than comes also after the word shanmāsa, when 'age' is not meant.
The च draws in the affix ण्यत् also. Thus षण्मासिको व्याधिः or षाण्मास्यः 'a disease lasting six months'.

1749. The affix kha ( ईन ) comes in the fourfold senses of "solicited," "hired", "lasted", and "will last," after the word samā.
This debars ठञ् ॥ Thus समामधीष्टो भृतो भूतो भावी वा = समीनः ॥ Some say, the sense of the affix is तेन निर्वृत्तम् V. 1. 79, S. 1743 as समया निर्वृत्तम् = समीनः ॥

1750. The affix kha comes optionally in the fivefold senses taught in V. 1. 79, 80 S. 1743 and 1744 after the word samā, forming a Dvigu.
In the alternative ठञ् will also apply. Up to sūtra V. 1. 93. S. 1757, the affixes have the fivefold senses of, 'to be accomplished by that time' (S. 1743), 'solicited', 'hired', 'lasted' and 'will last' (S. 1744). Thus द्विसमीनः or द्विसमिकः ॥ The Vārtika taught in V. 1. 20 (प्राग्वतेः संख्यापूर्वपदानां तदन्तग्रहणमलुकि) applies here also. Thus द्वैमासीनः or द्वैमासिकः, त्रिमासीनः or त्रैमासिकः ॥

entries.note: Entry cut off at bottom of page before English heading and translation

entries.english: 1751 The affix kha comes optionally in the fivefold senses (V. 1. 79, 80 S. 1743 and 1744) after the words rātri, ahan, and samvatsara, occasioning a Dvigu. The word dvigu is understood in this sûtra. In the alternative ठञ् will also come. Thus द्विरात्रीणः, द्वैरात्रिकः, द्व्यहीनः (VI. 4. 145 S. 789) or the samâsânta affix not being universally applicable, we have no टच् ॥ संवत्सरीणः, द्विसांवत्सरिकः (VII. 3. 15. S. 1752. This form gets the irregular vṛiddhi by the following.) द्व्यह्निकः ॥
entries.note: Sutra line was printed on preceding page (888); entry begins on page 889 with English heading.

entries.english: 1752. After a Numeral, the first vowel of संवत्सर and of a Numeral, gets the Vriddhi, before a Taddhita having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्. Thus द्विसांवत्सरिकः = द्वौ संवत्सरावधीष्टो भृतो भूतो or भावी (V. 1. 80 S. 1744), द्विषाष्टिकः = द्वौ षष्टी भृतो वा द्विषाष्टिकः ॥ The words ‹?› &c. when applied to (VII. 3. 16 S. 1754) and Numerals give rise to the affixes taught under kâlâdhikâra (V. 1. 78-97). The special mention of संवत्सर here, (though) this is a परिमाण word and would have been included in the sûtra VII. 3. 17 S. 1683 implies that the word परिमाण in that sûtra does not mean the measure of time, but a measure of any other thing than time.
