Therefore, with other time-words than samvatsara, the Vriddhi takes place in the regular way as द्वैषमिकः ॥ Note:—Similarly in sûtra IV. 1. 22, S. 180 the word परिमाण does not mean the measure of time or numerals, as त्रिवर्षा, द्विवर्षा शाटिका ॥ In short, the word परिमाण in those sûtras (and elsewhere III. 2. 23, II. 1. 46 &c.) means "mass" or "bulk", and not a measure in general.
entries.note: Reconstructed garbled Devanagari from context.

entries.english: 1753. The above affixes kha and thañ may also be elided after a Dvigu ending in varshâ. The affix ख as well as ठञ् come in the five-fold senses (V. 1. 79, 80), after the word वर्ष as forming a Dvigu; and these two affixes may also be elided optionally. Thus we have three forms, द्विवर्षीणः, द्विवार्षिकः and द्विवर्षः 'a disease that lasted two years'. (Compare VII. 3. 16, S. 1754. But when the sense is that of भावी, the form will be द्वैवर्षिकः ॥) To get this irregular vṛiddhi, the following sûtra applies.
entries.note: Reconstructed garbled Devanagari forms from clear context.

entries.english: 1754. After a numeral, the first vowel of वर्ष gets the Vriddhi, before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, when the affix does not refer to a Future time. As द्वे वर्षे अधीष्टो भृतो भूतो वा द्विवार्षिकः ॥ But when denoting future time, we have द्वैवर्षिकः, त्रैवार्षिकः "calculated to last two or three years" as in the sentence यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं धान्यं निहितं भृत्यवृत्तये । अधिकं वापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति ॥ (= त्रीणि वर्षाणि भावी) ॥ The word अभविष्यति does not qualify the words अधीष्ट and भृत (V. 1. 80 S. 1744), the sense of futurity is there denoted by the taddhita affix as द्वे वर्षे अधीष्टो भृतो वा कर्म करिष्यति द्विवार्षिको मनुष्यः ॥ Here VII. 3. 17. S. 1683 applies and it causes the vriddhi of the second member. This sûtra is again given below for the sake of context. 1754 A. After a numeral, the first vowel of a word denoting mass in its widest sense (with the exception of शाण) gets the Vriddhi before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण् or क्, when the word so formed does not mean a Name. As द्वौ कुडवौ प्रयोजनमस्य = द्विकौडविकः (V. 1. 109 S. 1772) द्वाभ्यां शूर्पाभ्यां क्रीतः = द्विशौर्पिकः (V. 1. 37 S. 1702), त्रिशौर्पिकम् ॥ The taddhita affix is optionally elided, see vartika to V. 1. 29. S. 1694. When the affix is elided there can be no Vriddhi as द्विसुवर्णम् ॥ Similarly द्विनैष्किकम्, त्रिनैष्किकम् (V. 1. 30 S. 1695). Why when it is not a name? Observe पाञ्चकपालिकम् (= पञ्चकपालानि परिमाणमस्य V. 1. 30 S. 1695). The whole word is a Name here. Why with the exception of शाण? Observe द्विशाणम् ॥ त्रिशाणम् formed with अण् (V. 1. 35 S. 1700 and 36 S. 1701). Some read the sûtra as असंज्ञाशाणखारीणाम् so that खारि is also excepted as द्वैखारिकः (V. 1. 33 S. 1698). द्वैखारि मेयभाजनम् ॥
entries.note: Includes repeated sutra 1754 A (SK 1683) cited for context.

entries.english: 1755. The affixes meaning "accomplished &c V. 1. 79, 80" are necessarily elided after the word varshâ forming a Dvigu, when it refers to a being endowed with reason. Here the elision is compulsory and not optional. Thus द्विवर्षो दारकः 'a boy two years old'. Note:—Why do we say चित्तवति "when meaning endowed with reason"? Observe द्विवर्षीणो व्याधिः ॥

1756. The anomalously formed word shashtikah has the meaning of "what are matured in sixty nights". The word is not necessarily always plural, though so exhibited in the sûtra. The word षष्टिकाः may be said to be formed by adding कन् to षष्टिरात्रि in the 3rd case in construction, then eliding the word रात्रि, the force of the affix being 'matured'. Thus षष्टिरात्रेण पच्यन्ते = षष्टिकाः 'a kind of barley'. It is a name of barley and therefore does not apply to pulse, beans &c., though they may also ripen in six days.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra number misprinted/misread as 1754, corrected to 1756 from sequence and English heading.

entries.english: 1757. The affix thañ comes after a word denoting time, in the 3rd case in construction, in the sense of "to be subdued", "to be gained or attained", "to be completed" and "to be easily completed in that time". Thus मासेन परिजय्यः (शक्यते जेतुम्) = मासिको व्याधिः, मासेन लभ्यं कार्यं or सुकरं मासिकम् ॥

entries.note: Entry cuts off at bottom of page 891 with Devanagari text only; English translation is on page 892.

entries.english: 1758. The affix thañ comes after a word of time in the sense of "an abstinence that lasts so long" or "who practises abstinence so long". The word तद् shows that the word must be in the accusative case: अस्य shows the force of the affix. ब्रह्मचर्यम् joins both. Thus मासं ब्रह्मचर्यमस्य = मासिको ब्रह्मचारी "who practises abstinence for a month". So also आर्धमासिकः, सांवत्सरिकः ॥ The second case is by II. 3. 5. S. 558. Another explanation is, the affix thañ comes after a word in the first case in construction, in the sense of an abstinence which lasts for such a period. As मासोऽस्य ब्रह्मचर्यस्य मासिकं ब्रह्मचर्यम्, "an abstinence lasting for a month", आर्धमासिकं, सांवत्सरिकम्. In the first case the affix relates to a person, in the second to the vow itself. Both these explanations are valid, as the structure of the aphorism is open to both constructions. Vârt:— So also after the words महानाम्नी &c. in the genitive construction. As महानाम्निकः । Mahânâmnî are certain Ṛik verses. But Haradatta gives the form महानाम्निका by applying the rule of masculisation of the Vârtika भस्याः (VI. 3. 35. S. 836). In this case VI. 4. 144. S. 679 causes the elision of टि ॥ After these words, the affix means also 'who practises that'. As महानाम्नीश्चरति = महानाम्निकः, आदित्यव्रतिकः, गोदानिकः ॥ महानाम्नी + ठञ् = महानामन् + ठञ् (VI. 3. 35. S. 836 Vârt.) महानाम्निका (VI. 4. 144 S. 679). Note:— The affix णिनि comes after the words अवान्तरदीक्षा &c., in the sense of 'who practises'. As अवान्तरदीक्षां चरति = अवान्तरदीक्षी, तिलव्रती ॥ Note:— The affixes वुञ् and णिनि come after the word अष्टचत्वारिंशत्, as अष्टचत्वारिंशद्वर्षाणि संचरति = अष्टचत्वारिंशकः or अष्टचत्वारिंशिन् ॥ Note.— The same affixes come after the words चातुर्मास्य &c. the final य being elided. As चातुर्मास्यानि चरति = चातुर्मासकः or चातुर्मासिन् । Vârt:— The affix ण्य comes after चतुर्मास in the sense of 'produced there'. As चतुर्षु मासेषु भवानि चातुर्मास्यानि ॥ It refers to a sacrifice. Vârt:— The affix ‹?› comes, when it is a Name, as चतुर्षु मासेषु भवा चातुर्मासी पौर्णमासी ॥ So also आषाढी, कार्तिकी, फाल्गुनी ॥ The feminine ङीप् is added because it is an ‹?›-formed word.
entries.note: Sutra line was printed on preceding page (page 891); English heading and text on page 892.

entries.english: 1759. The affix thañ comes after a word being the name of a sacrifice, in the sense of "the fee thereof". As द्वादशाहस्य दक्षिणा = द्वादशाहिकी । So also अग्निष्टोमस्य दक्षिणा = आग्निष्टोमिकी, वाजपेयिकी ॥ The word आख्या in the sûtra implies that the affix comes even after those sacrifice-denoting words which do not express time (V. 1. 78 S. 1742). Had it not been used, the sûtra would have applied only to such sacrifice-denoting words as एकाह, द्वादशाह which are time denoting words as well. The Vârtika in V. 1. 20. S. 1682 would apply to द्वादशाह, &c. Some texts do not read च in the sûtra.

1760. The affixes having the sense of भव (IV. 3. 53, S. 1428, IV. 3. 11 S. 1381) come after a time-denoting word, in the sense of "what is given in that, and what is done in that". As प्रावृषि दीयते or कार्यम् = प्रावृषेण्यम् (IV. 3. 17. S. 1388) शारदम् (IV. 3. 16, S. 1387). All these words mean also what is given or done in those seasons. The word वत् in भववत् means that all the rules of ‹?› (IV. 3. 53. S. 1428) apply here. This sûtra should be divided into two parts, one joining with the previous sûtra, as तत्र च दीयते, यज्ञाख्येभ्यः, as आग्निष्टोमिकं भक्तम्, राजसूयिकम्, वाजपेयिकम् ॥ Here ends the section on Time-affixes.

1761. The affix aṇ comes after the words व्युष्ट &c. in the 7th case in construction, in the sense of "being given therein or done therein". Thus व्युष्टे दीयते कार्यं वा = वैयुष्टम्, तैर्थम् ॥ 1 व्युष्ट, 2 नित्य, 3 निष्क्रमण, 4 प्रवेशन, 5 उपसंक्रमण, 6 तीर्थ, 7 आस्तर (आस्तरण), 8 संग्राम, 9 संघात, 10 पद, 11 पीलुमूल (पीलु मूल), 12 प्रवास, 13 उपवास, 14 संभ्रम, 15 दीर्घ ॥

1762. The affixes ‹?› and यत् come respectively after the words yathâ-katha-cha, and hasta, being in the third case in construction, having the sense of what is "given or is done in this way or with this". The words दीयते and कार्य apply to both; the rule of यथासंख्यम् (I. 3. 10 S. 128) not applying to it. The word यथाकथाच is an Indeclinable, meaning contempt. Of course this word cannot take any case-affix, it therefore only gives the sense of third case. As यथाकथाच दीयते कार्यं वा = याथाकथाचम्; given with contempt or done with contempt. हस्तेन दीयते कार्यं वा = हस्त्यम् ॥

1763. The affix thañ comes after a word in the Instrumental case in construction, in the sense of "fitted for that". The word संपादिन् means 'suitable, proper, fit'. The word संपादिन् is formed by adding णिनि to संपद्, the force of the affix being that of necessity (III. 3. 170 S. 3311), as कर्णवेष्टकाभ्यां संपादि मुखं = कर्णवेष्टकिकं मुखं 'a face fit for ear-rings' which becomes beautified by ear ornaments &c. वपुषिकं शरीरम् i. e. वपुषा वस्त्रयुगेन विशेषतः शोभते ॥

1764. The affix yat (य) comes in the sense of "being fitted with that", after the words karma and vesha, in the third-case in construction. This debars thañ. कर्मणा संपद्यते = कर्मण्यं शौर्यम् । वेषेण संपद्यते = वेष्यो नटः ॥ 'Vesha' means artificial appearance, i. e. disguise.

1765. The affix thañ comes after the words santâpa &c. in the dative construction, in the sense of "what is able to effect that". The word प्रभवति means 'able, capable'. The dative here has the force of ‹?› (II. 3. 36 S. 583). As, संतापाय प्रभवति = सान्तापिकः, सांग्रामिकः ॥ 1 संताप, 2 संनाह, 3 संग्राम, 4 संयोग, 5 संपराय, 6 संवेशन, 7 संपेष, 8 निष्पेष, 9 सर्ग, 10 निसर्ग, 11 विसर्ग, 12 उपसर्ग, 13 प्रवास, 14 उपवास, 15 संघात, 16 संवेष, 17 संग्राव, 18 संवोधन, 19 सक्तु, 20 मांसोदनाद्विगृहीतादपि, 21 उत्सर्ग ॥

entries.note: English heading and translation cut off at end of batch (on page 895).

entries.english:
1766. The affix yat (यत्) is also added in this sense of 'able to effect that', to the word yoga.

By force of the word च 'and' the affix ‹?› also applies. Thus ‹?› = ‹?› or ‹?› ।
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line was printed at the bottom of the preceding page (p. 888)

entries.english:
1767. The affix ukañ comes after the word karman, in the same sense of 'able to effect that'.

This debars ‹?›. As कर्म प्रभवति — कार्मुकं धनुः ॥ This word कार्मुकम् means always a 'bow', and is never employed to designate anything else.

1768. The affix thañ comes after the word samaya, in the first case in construction, in the sense of "that has arrived for it".

Thus ‹?› 'a work for which the time has come'.

1769. The affix aṇ comes after the word ṛitu, meaning "that has come for it".

As ऋतुः प्राप्तोऽस्य — आर्त्तवं पुष्पम् (Guṇa by VI. 4. 146 / S. 847) "the flower for which the season has arrived".

1770. The affix yat (यत्) comes after the word kāla, in the same sense of 'time for it'.

As काल्यं शीतम् ॥ See VI. 1. 213. S. 3701.

1771. The affix thañ comes after a word in the first case in construction, in the sense of "longstanding".

As प्रकृष्टः कालोऽस्य — कालिकं ऋणम् "long-standing debt", कालिकं वैरम् "long-standing enmity".

In this sūtra काल and तस्य are understood, but not so the word प्राप्तम् ।

1772. The affix thañ comes after a word in the first case in construction in the sense of "that whose occasion or purpose is this".

As इन्द्रमहः प्रयोजनमस्य = ऐन्द्रमहिकम् । The word प्रयोजन means fruit or cause.

1773. The affix aṇ comes in the sense of 'that whose purpose is this', after the words viśākhā and āṣāḍha, when the derivative of the first is combined with मन्थ and that of the second with दण्ड ॥

As वैशाखो मन्थः, आषाढो दण्डः ।

Vārt:— So also after the words चूडा &c. As चूडा प्रयोजनमस्य चौडम्, श्राद्धा प्रयोजनमस्य = श्राद्धम् ॥

1774. The affix Chha (ईय) comes in the same sense of "that whose purpose is this", after the words अनुप्रवचन &c.

This debars ठञ् ॥ Thus अनुप्रवचनं प्रयोजनमस्य = अनुप्रवचनीयम् ॥

1 अनुप्रवचन, 2 उत्थापन, 3 उपस्थापन, 4 संवेशन, 5 प्रवेशन, 6 अनुप्रवेशन, 7 अनुवासन, 8 अनुबन्धन, 9 अनुवाचन, 10 धान्यारोहण, 11 प्रारम्भण, 12 पारम्भण, 13 आरोहण, 14 अनुदेशन, 15 अनुवादन, 16 परीक्षण ।

1775. The affix Chha comes in the same sense of "that whose purpose is this", after the word samāpana, when it has a word in composition preceding it.

This debars ठञ् ॥ Thus व्याकरणं समापनं प्रयोजनमस्य = व्याकरणसमापनीयम् ॥

Note:— The specific mention of the word pada in the aphorism indicates that the rule will not apply when a word other than a 'pada,' such as the affix bahuch, V. 3. 68, S. 2023 precedes the word samāpana.

1776. The word aikāgārikaṭ is irregularly formed, in the sense of a 'thief'.

The feminine will be in ङीप् । Thus एकागारं प्रयोजनमस्य ऐकागारिकः fem. ॰की ॥

Note:— This word can be regularly formed by ठञ्, but it will always be restricted to mean a thief. When any other thing is designated, it will not take this affix. Thus एकागारं प्रयोजनमस्य भिक्षाः, here there will be no affixing. The feminine moreover will be in ङीप् ॥ Some say the word is formed by adding the affix ‹?› with the irregular Vṛiddhi of the first syllable.

1777. The word ākālikaṭ is irregularly formed in the sense of "what coincides with the beginning and the end i. e. what lasts only an instant".

— 'a thunder lasting for an instant'

The word आकाल is substituted for समानकाल ॥ Thus आकालिकः स्तनयित्नुः । आकालिकी विद्युत् — "a lightning lasting a twinkle", i. e. whose death is equal to its time of birth or dying as born.

Vārt:— The affixes ‹?› and ‹?› also come after आकाल, as आकालिका विद्युत् ॥

So far is the governing power of the affix ठञ् V. 1. 18.

1778. The affix vati (वत्) comes after a word in the third case in construction, in the sense of "like that", when the meaning is 'similarity of action'.
As ब्राह्मणेन तुल्यं वर्तते ब्राह्मणवत्, as in the sentence ब्राह्मणवदधीते ॥
Why do we say "action"? The affix will not be joined when the similarity is in 'quality'. As पुत्रेण तुल्यः स्थूलः "as big as the son".

1779. The affix vati comes also in the sense of "like what is there in or thereof".
As मथुरायामिव = मथुरावत् 'like that in Mathura' as मथुरावत् कुड्ये प्राकारः, चैत्रस्येव चैत्रवन्मैत्रस्य गावः ॥

1780. The affix vati comes after a word in the second case in construction, in the sense of "befitting that or suited to that".
Thus विधिमर्हति = विधिवत्पूज्यते "respected as god". The word kriyā should be read into this sûtra from V. 1. 115, S. 1778, by 'frog-leap' anuvritti, for it is not to be read in S. 1779.
Therefore, not here राजानमर्हति छत्रम्, "the umbrella as befits a king".

1781. The affixes tva and tal come after a word in the sixth case in construction, in the sense of "the nature thereof".
As गोर्भावः गोत्वम् or गोता ॥ The word formed by tva is of Neuter gender, that formed by tal is feminine.

1782. From this forward as far as the aphorism V. 1. 136, S. 1801 the affixes त्व and तल् bear rule.
Thus in V. 1. 122, S. 1784 त्व and तल् are read, giving the forms पृथुत्व and पृथुता &c. This rule is intended to secure admission for these two affixes notwithstanding the bars in the shape of subsequent aphorisms directing the employment of other affixes. These affixes signify, in addition to भाव (nature), कर्मन् (action) also, in V. 1. 124, S. 1788. The word च in the aphorism is intended to secure their admission notwithstanding the affixes ‹?› and ‹?› (V. 1. 87; S. 1769). Thus स्त्रियाः भावः स्त्रैणम्, स्त्रीत्वम्, स्त्रीता 'the nature of a female', पुंस्त्वम्, पुंस्ता, पौंस्नम् ॥
entries.note: Restored affixes त्व and तल् and corrected OCR corruptions in commentary based on context.

entries.english:
1783. The affixes denoting 'nature', taught hereafter, do not come after a Tatpurusha compound formed by the negative particle नञ्, with the exception of the following :—chatura, sangata, lavana, vata, budha, kata, rasa, and lasa.
Thus the words अपति and अपटु will have two forms only i.e. अपतित्वम् or अपतिता, अपटुत्वम् or अपटुता ॥
Note:—While by V. 1. 128, S. 1793 other compounds will have ष्यञ् also, as सैनापत्यम् ॥ An exception to this is वैदुर्य (VII. 2255; 3065), as used by the Author himself.
Why do we say नञ् पूर्वम् "a Tatpurusha whose first member is नञ्"? Observe बार्हस्पत्यम्, प्राजापत्यम् ॥
Why do we say 'after a Tatpurusha'? Observe, when the word अपटु is a Bahuvrihi compound meaning नास्य पटवः सन्ति, its derivative will be आपटवम्.
So also the compounds of चतुर &c. with अ, e.g. आचातुर्यम्, आसङ्गत्यम्, आलवण्यम्, आवाट्यम्, आबुध्यम्, आकत्यम्, आरस्यम्, आलस्यम् ॥ In some texts, there is युध instead of बुध ॥
entries.note: Reconstructed corrupted Sanskrit examples from context.

entries.english:
1784. The affix imanich (इमनिच्) comes optionally in the sense of 'nature', after the words prithu &c.
The word वा 'optionally' is employed with the intention of securing admission for the affixes अण् &c. Thus पृथु + इमन् । Now applies the following :—

1785. Before the affixes इष्ठ, इमन् and ईयस्, र् is substituted for the ऋ in a stem, when this ऋ is preceded by a consonant, and is not prosodially long (on account of being followed by a double consonant).
Thus पृथु + इमन् = प्रथ् + इमन् । Now applies the following.

1786. The last vowel, with consonant, if any, that follows it, is elided when the affixes इष्ठ, इमन् and ईयस् follow.
Thus पृथोर्भावः = प्रथिमिन् nom. प्रथिमा (पृथु + इमन् = प्रथु + इमन् VI. 4. 161 = प्रथ् + इमन् VI. 4. 155 = प्रथिमा), or पार्थवम् by V. 1. 131, S. 1796. So also म्रदिमा or मार्दवम् ॥ The उ of पृथु and मृदु is elided by the present Sutra and र is substituted for ऋ by VI. 4. 161, S. 1785. Of course, the affixes त्व and तल् come here also as, पृथुत्वम्, मृदुत्वम्, पृथुता, मृदुता ॥
1 पृथु, 2 मृदु, 3 महत्, 4 पटु, 5 तनु, 6 लघु, 7 बहु, 8 साधु, 9 आशु (माशु), 10 उरु (करु), 11 गुरु, 12 बहुल, 13 खण्ड, 14 दण्ड, 15 षण्ड, 16 अकिंचन, 17 बालक, 18 होड, 19 पाक, 20 वत्स, 21 मन्द, 22 स्वादु, 23 ह्रस्व, 24 दीर्घ, 25 प्रिय, 26 वृष, 27 ऋजु, 28 क्षिप्र, 29 क्षुद्र, 30 अणु, 31 वेणु (?).
1787. The affix shyañ also comes, as well as imanich, after a word denoting colour, and after the words dridha &c., in the sense of 'nature thereof'.

Thus शुक्लस्य भावः शौक्ल्यम्, शुक्लिमन्, शुक्लि, शुक्लता ॥ कार्ष्ण्यम्, कृष्णिमन्, द्रढिमन् (nom. -मा) । दृढता ॥

The ष् of ष्यञ् shows that the feminine is formed by ङीष् (IV. 1. 41). As औचित्यम् fem. औचिती (VI. 4. 148 and 150, S. 311 and 472). So also यथाकामी ॥

Vârt :—The following are the six words which substitute र for ऋ under VI. 4. 161, S. 1785: पृथु, मृदु, भृश, कृश, दृढ, परिवृढ । Thus प्रथिमा ॥

Note :—It, therefore, does not apply to words like कृत, मातृ, भ्रातृ, &c. कृतमाचष्टे = कृतयति; मातरमाचष्टे = मातयति; भ्रातरमाचष्टे = भ्रातयति ॥ See III. 1. 21, S. 2677.
entries.note: Continuation tail from previous page.

entries.english:
1788. The same affix shyañ has after a word expressive of quality, and after Brâhmaṇa &c., the sense of 'the activity or occupation of something or some one.'

The च in the aphorism is employed with the intention of including भाव or "nature". The word कर्म denotes activity, जडस्य भावः कर्म वा जाड्यम् ॥ So also मौढ्यम्, ब्राह्मण्यम्, षाण्ढ्यम् ॥

This class of ब्राह्मण &c. is âkritigaṇa, i.e. the fact of a word belonging to which is known only from the forms met with in writers of authority.

Vârt :—The augment नुम् is added to अर्वन् when it takes the affix ष्यञ् । Thus the activity or nature of अर्वन् will be आर्वन्त्यम् fem. आर्वन्ती the न् is elided by VI. 4. 150, S. 472.

The words यथातथ and यथापुर preceded by the negative particle न्, i.e. the words अयथातथ and अयथापुर belong to the Brâhmaṇâdi class. They also take ष्यञ्; the vṛiddhi in their case is governed by the following sûtra.

1789. Before a Taddhita affix having an indicatory ञ्, ण्, or क्, the words अयथातथ and अयथापुर may have vṛiddhi of the first vowel of their first member, or that of the second member, in alternation.

That is, when the Negative particle gets the vṛiddhi, the words remain unchanged; and when these words are vṛiddhied, the negative particle remains unaltered. As आयथातथ्यम् or अयाथातथ्यम्, आयथापुर्यम् or अयाथापुर्यम् ॥

In the sûtra the compounds are exhibited as यथातथ and यथापुर and are Avyayîbhâvas (II. 1. 7, S. 661), and being neuters, the आ of तथा and पुरा are shortened.

The words भाव and कर्म bear rule up to the end of the seventh Book chapter three.

Vârt :—The affix does not change the sense in चातुर्वर्ण्य &c., as चत्वार एव वर्णाः = चातुर्वर्ण्यम् ॥ चातुराश्रम्यम्, त्रैस्वर्यम्, षाड्गुण्यम्, सैन्यम्, सान्निध्यम्, सामीप्यम्, औपम्यम्, त्रैलोक्यम् ॥ &c.

So also सर्ववेदाः All Vedas. One who studies All-Vedas is सर्ववेदः; the affix is here luk-elided by the vârttika under IV. 2. 60, S. 1270. This word सर्ववेद takes the affix ष्यञ् without any change of sense. As सार्ववेद्यम् ॥

Vârt :—There is vṛiddhi of both members of the compound चतुर्वेद 'who studies four Vedas' before shyañ. As चतुर्वेद + ष्यञ् = चातुर्वैद्यम् ॥ Instead of चतुर्वेदस्य, another reading of this Vârttika is चतुर्विद्यस्य; thus चतुर्विद्य + ष्यञ् = चातुर्वैद्यम् ॥ चतुर्वेदः is formed from विद्या by अण् luk-elision (IV. 1. 88, S. 1080); चतुर्विद्यः by ढक् elision (IV. 2. 60, S. 1270, vårt.).

1790. The affix yat (यत्) comes in the sense of 'nature thereof or action thereof', after the word stena, in the genitive, and न is elided before this affix.

The न in the sûtra is taken in its composite form, i.e. न् + अ ॥ The elision herein taught is of न NA and not of न् N only. The word स्तेन is formed by अच् of पचादि class.

Note :—Had न of the sûtra meant the single letter न्, there would arise the following anomaly: स्तेन + ष्यञ् = स्तेन् + य (the न् is elided by VI. 4. 148, S. 311). Here the elided अ becomes sthânivat by I. 1. 57, S. 50 and so when न is elided by the present sûtra, we have स्ते + अ + य ॥ The elided अ would cause the ए to be changed to अय् &c., the form would be स्तय्य ॥ Hence the whole syllable न is elided by this sûtra and not separately by the application of S. 311 and this sûtra.

As स्तेनस्य भावः कर्म वा स्तेयम् ॥ Some divide the sûtra into two: (1) स्तेनात् — यत् भवति, (2) ततो यन्नलोपश्च as स्तैन्यम् and स्तेयम् ॥

1791. The affix य comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof', after the word सखि ॥

As सख्यम् 'friendship'.

Vârt :—So also after the words दूत and वणिक् as दूत्यम् ॥ According to Kâśikâ we have वणिज्यम् । Mâdhava says 'वाणिज्या is inherently feminine. The affix shyañ is added to it in the sense of nature and never in the sense of action.' In the Bhâṣya this vârttika is not at all found. The word वाणिज्यम् is formed by V. 1. 124, S. 1788, वणिक् belonging to Brâhmaṇâdi class.
entries.note: Devanagari sutra line is at the bottom of page 902; English explanation is on page 903.

entries.english:
1792. The affix ḍhak comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof', after the words kapi and jñâti.

Thus कपेः कर्म वा कापेयम्, ज्ञातेयम् ॥ The rule of यथासंख्य (I. 3. 10, S. 128) does not apply anywhere under this head.

1793. The affix yak comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof', after a compound ending with pati, and after purohita &c.

Thus सेनापतेर्भावः कर्म वा सैनापत्यम्, पौरोहित्यम्, राज्यम् ॥

1 पुरोहित, 2 राजाऽसे (असमासे, राजन् असे), 3 ग्रामिक (सग्रामिक), 4 पिण्डिक, 5 सुहित, 6 बाल, 7 मन्द, 8 खण्डिक, 9 दण्डक, 10 वर्मिक (वर्मिन्), 11 कर्मिक, 12 धर्मिक, 13 शिलिक (शीलिक), 14 सूतिक, 15 मूनिक, 16 तिलक (तिलिका), 17 अञ्जलिक, 18 अञ्जनिक (अञ्जनिका), 19 ऋषिक, 20 पुत्रिक (पुत्रक), 21 अत्रिक, 22 क्षत्रिक, 23 पर्णिक, 24 पथिक (पथिका), 25 मणिक, 26 प्रतिक, 27 सारथि (सारथिक), 28 आस्तिक, 29 सूचिक, 30 साक्ष, 31 सूचक (संरक्षसूचक), 32 नास्तिक, 33 भजनिक, 34 शाक्वर (शक्वर), 35 नागरक, 36 चूडिक, 37 एडिक, 38 मिलिन्द, 39 स्तानक, 40 चूडितिक, 41 कृषिक, 42 वृतिक, 43 पत्रिक, 44 सलनिक, 45 पक्षिक, 46 जलिक, 47 धार्मिक, 48 तित्तिर, 49 ऋचिक, 50 अधिक, 51 परिक्षक, 52 पूजनिक, 53 मूषिक, 54 स्वरिक ॥

Vârt :—The word râjan gets yak affix when not in a compound. As राज्यम्, 'the nature or action of the king—royal'. In the compound it will take shyañ of the Brâhmaṇâdi class. As आधिराज्यम् ॥
